## §415 — Self-play Step 0: own-play run-victory labels barely improve the OOC leaf's picks (2026-10-09)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-09):** before an expert-iteration loop (OOC MCTS plays games, run
victory labels them, retrain leaf and prior, repeat), does the outcome-trained leaf pick better
with more of our own games?
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/ooc_outcome_curve_20261009/PREREG.md) committed at `086fcf4b`
before the run. Offline, no seeds, TEST closed. The §394 P0 recipe (X2-B recipe, public 457
features) on nested 1/8..1/1 of the 696 #334 TRAIN sources: `SRC` source-trajectory rows only
(87..696 own-play games) and `ALL` with counterfactual branch rows. Selection gain vs V4's
choice on #334 VALIDATION siblings (1,329 decisions) and E3 VALIDATION (333 states), slope per
doubling with source-clustered bootstrap. Rule on `SRC`: GO if a slope ≥ +0.005 with CI lower
> 0 and the E3 card skip share falls; STOP if both CI uppers < +0.005.
**Validity:** `ALL` at 1/1 reproduces §394 P0 exactly (trees 278/355/373, NLL 0.4237).
**Result:** `INCONCLUSIVE`. `SRC` slope +0.0028 [−0.0010, +0.0066] (#334) and +0.0020 [−0.0038,
+0.0077] (E3). At 696 games: NLL 0.469 (`ALL` 0.424), E3 boss-relic gain −0.072 (uniform random
−0.090), card −0.002, skip share 0.236→0.221. Below ~200 games the GBM stops at 1–3 trees.
`ALL` has the only clearly positive slope: E3 boss relic +0.019 [+0.004, +0.033]; `ALL` at 174
sources matches `SRC` at 696 on NLL.
**Interpretation (Inference):** plain games labelled with the run outcome add about +0.003
selection gain per doubling; closing the E3 gap to V4 (−0.037) at the upper CI would need
~22k games (~680 CPU-h at ~110 CPU-s per OOC-MCTS game), at the point estimate far more. The
ranking signal sits in paired counterfactual branches, which E3/#334 already collect.
**Decision:** Philipp chose to shelve the self-play loop (no iteration 0, seeds 66M unused).

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/ooc_outcome_curve_20261009/README.md).

**Knowledge impact:** `ooc-label-pipeline.md` routes `tools.vwin_outcome_curve`.

## §418 — #396 Stage 1: forward-map block and `bossId` ablation on the public-safe `v_win` baseline (2026-10-09)

**Question:** does the compact map block of the rich `v_win` state (`fmDElite`,
`fmDRest`, `fmDShop`, `fmDBoss`, `fmCElite`, `fmCRest`, `fmCShop`, `fmCEvent`,
`fmCMonster`, `fmCTreasure`, `curMapX`, `curMapY`) carry held-out run-win
signal, separately from the public act-boss identity `bossId`? This decides
whether #396 Stage 2 (richer map encodings) is justified.

**Protocol:** preregistered in `tools/analyze_vwin_map_396.py` (committed
`c1c35f33` before any arm was trained; the decision rule is its docstring).
Offline only: frozen #334 corpus `corpus-mixed-512.json` (SHA-256
`ca4b6e2b…cd87f`), A3 run `a3-trainval-20261001-50713b83/selected`
(preflight/validation hashes equal to §374), TRAIN 333,367 / VALIDATION 68,903
MAP rows, no gameplay seeds, no C++ build, no TEST rows. Frozen A3 X1 recipe,
XGBoost seeds 0–4, arm prediction = 5-seed mean probability. Arms: **P** the
457-feature public-safe baseline (§371 B); **M** P minus the 12 map fields
(`bossId` kept); **Bz** P minus `bossId`; **P2** P with seeds 5–9 (null control
for retraining noise); inverse diagnostic **S** (TRAIN-variable basic scalars
`act`, `floor`, `curHp`, `maxHp`, `gold` + `bossId`; `ascension` is constant)
and **O** = S + map fields. Rule per ablation X ∈ {M, Bz}: `MATTERS` if the
ensemble ΔNLL (X − P) ≥ 0.002, its source-clustered 95% CI lower bound > 0,
ΔNLL − |null ΔNLL| ≥ 0.002 and ≥ 4 of 5 per-seed deltas > 0; `LOW_VALUE` if
the CI upper bound < 0.002; else `INCONCLUSIVE`.

**Gates:** the 461-feature A3 set at seed 0 reproduced the frozen X1 exactly
(NLL `0.44453298345900494`, 290 trees, drift 0); the P ensemble NLL 0.443381
matched §374 (0.44338).

**Results (5-seed ensemble, VALIDATION):**

| arm | features | NLL | Brier | AUC | ECE | pooled sibling acc. | MAP sibling acc. (23 pairs) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| P | 457 | 0.44338 | 0.14534 | 0.8062 | 0.0481 | 0.570 [0.522, 0.617] | 0.478 [0.289, 0.688] |
| P2 (null) | 457 | 0.44594 | 0.14635 | 0.8029 | 0.0489 | 0.571 [0.525, 0.617] | 0.478 [0.320, 0.658] |
| M (no map) | 445 | 0.44836 | 0.14686 | 0.8019 | 0.0481 | 0.571 [0.525, 0.617] | 0.457 [0.283, 0.625] |
| Bz (no `bossId`) | 456 | 0.44459 | 0.14604 | 0.8064 | 0.0492 | 0.565 [0.517, 0.612] | 0.413 [0.200, 0.611] |
| S | 6 | 0.50145 | 0.16624 | 0.7076 | 0.0248 | 0.499 [0.463, 0.537] | 0.435 |
| O (S + map) | 18 | 0.50523 | 0.16747 | 0.7023 | 0.0258 | 0.516 [0.484, 0.549] | 0.435 |

Ensemble ΔNLL [source-clustered 95% CI, 77 sources]: M − P **+0.0050
[−0.0012, +0.0109]**, per seed +0.0044, +0.0057, +0.0073, +0.0006, +0.0022
(5/5 positive); Bz − P **+0.0012 [−0.0032, +0.0056]** (3/5 positive); null
P2 − P +0.0026 [−0.0008, +0.0061]; O − S +0.0038 [+0.0005, +0.0072] (adding
the map block to the small scalar model made it worse). M's NLL loss is spread
over acts (act 1/2/3: +0.0014/+0.0080/+0.0039) and is largest on pre-boss rows
(+0.0128, n 5,142). M trains shallower ensembles (145–201 trees vs 189–346).

**Variability and importance (descriptive):** all 13 fields are in the A3
TRAIN-variable mask and vary widely (non-modal fraction 0.51–0.93). In the P
seed-0 model the 12 map fields together hold 0.23% of total gain; their best
TreeSHAP rank is `fmDElite` 116 of 457, the rest rank 216–372. `bossId` holds
1.1% of total gain and ranks 22.

**Verdict:** **`MAP_INCONCLUSIVE`** and **`BOSSID_INCONCLUSIVE`**; #396 outcome
**`MAP_STAGE1_INCONCLUSIVE`**. Removing the map block worsened every seed and
the ensemble by about twice the null retraining shift, but its CI includes
zero and the retraining null alone moves the ensemble by +0.0026, so the
effect is not resolvable on this split (consistent with the ±0.005 resolution
noted in §375). `bossId` is used heavily by the trees, yet removing it costs
less than retraining noise. **Inference:** its information is largely
recoverable from `act` and the deck/relic state. The inverse diagnostic gives
no sign that the map block carries standalone signal. The MAP sibling
comparison (23 discordant pairs) cannot separate any arm.

**Decision:** per #396's rule, Stage 2 (richer map encodings, Burning-Elite
features, graph encoders) is **not justified** by this evidence; the current
block and `bossId` stay unchanged in the feature contract. No default can be
affected: pathing is the heuristic DP, the tracked `models/v_win_trees.txt`
is untouched (#397), and the A3 models are used only by opt-in OOC MCTS leaves.
A map signal at this size could only be resolved by more sources or a direct
MAP-decision counterfactual corpus, not by feature work on #334.

**Evidence:** `/home/philippherrmann/Documents/sts/artifacts/vwin-map-396/stage1-20261009-c1c35f33/`
(`report.json` SHA-256 `4ec15a543344246ce8ead8f93c23a7a9dc559fc378689180e8b1eca3f3585825`,
`validation_predictions.npz` `2774375023304cff168d36c17014fa0c0e6e0f83339a291987afc292e4230ff2`,
run log alongside); summary copy in `/mnt/project-files/map-path-396/RESULT.md`.
xgboost 3.4.0, numpy 2.5.1, 4 threads, CPU only. 17:55 wall, 1,792 CPU-s,
5.1 GB peak RSS.

**ELI5:** We took the map summary away from the win predictor and retrained it
five times. It got a little worse every time, but retraining with the map
still there moves the score about half as much, so we can't tell a real loss
from noise. Taking away which boss is coming barely mattered. Nothing here
says a fancier map description would help.

**Knowledge impact:** #396 Stage 1 summary in `operations/ooc-label-pipeline.md`
and `evaluation/current-research.md`.

## §420 — A20 Silver combat-strength card pilot: SCALE by rule, not shown (2026-10-10)

**Question:** after §416, does combat strength measured with real A20 teacher
Silver fights pick card rewards better than the teacher, and better than CTM
strength on the same states? Philipp asked for it on 2026-10-09 21:38Z.

**Design:** [PLAN-SILVER-STRENGTH.md](evidence/a20_card_floor_20261009/PLAN-SILVER-STRENGTH.md),
frozen at `2cbb90f8` (binary `f0cc3b6a…`).
- **States:** 200 of the §416 states, hash-selected (`silver_pilot_seeds.txt`).
- **Fights:** `cardstrengthprobe … 20 1` plays one teacher Silver fight per
  option and act-pool encounter. It starts from the post-pick state at ASC 20,
  with combat RNG paired across options.
- **Score:** pools and weights as in §416.
- **Verdicts:** PASS if the gain CI lower bound > 0. SCALE if the gain is
  ≥ +0.30 floors and higher than CTM strength on the same states. STOP
  otherwise.

**Result: `SCALE` by the pre-registered rule; gain CI includes 0.**

| States: 200 | Silver strength | CTM strength (§416 run) |
|-------------|-----------------|-------------------------|
| Gain over teacher | +0.64 floors [−0.43, +1.73] | +0.55 [−0.28, +1.34] |
| Agreement with teacher | 35% | 58% |
| Skip rate (teacher 6%) | 25% | 2% |
| Median option spread | 0.066 | 0.009 |

- **Data quality:** 0 trajectory mismatches. 26 of 13,657 fights were invalid
  and dropped. One state was unscored.
- **Same states, uniform random pick:** −0.68.
- **By act (Silver):** +0.94, +0.29 and −0.17 in acts 1–3.

**Interpretation (Inference):**
- Silver separates options about 7× more than the CTM. It disagrees with the
  teacher on two thirds of states and skips six times as often, yet it is not
  worse than the teacher.
- The SCALE condition is met only narrowly: Silver beats CTM strength by
  +0.09 floors on the same states, which is far inside the noise.
- This sample is kinder to strength picks than the full set: CTM strength
  scores +0.55 here against +0.14 on all 970 states.
- The high skip rate is a plausible bias. One fight against the act's pools
  rewards a thin deck now and ignores later acts.
- So the pilot does not show that Silver strength is better. It only fails to
  rule it out.

**Cost:** fights 2.0 CPU h by thread CPU. The whole run took about 2.5 h of
wall time on 4 cores, so the replay and per-call overhead dominate (about
3 CPU min per state).

**Evidence:** [report-silver-pilot.json](evidence/a20_card_floor_20261009/report-silver-pilot.json),
[report-ctm-on-silver-pilot.json](evidence/a20_card_floor_20261009/report-ctm-on-silver-pilot.json),
raw outputs in `/mnt/project-files/card-strength-probe/silver-pilot-2cbb90f8/`.

**Knowledge impact:** this entry, plus `SILVER_REPS` on the default-off
`cardstrengthprobe` mode. No defaults changed.

## §421 — A20 Silver card strength with the next act, all 970 states: NOT_SHOWN (2026-10-10)

**Question:** after §420 (Silver strength pilot, SCALE by rule), does Silver
combat strength against the rest of the current act plus the next act pick
A20 card rewards better than the teacher on floor reached, over all 970
§416 states? Philipp asked for it on 2026-10-10 07:42Z ("Merge, then add next
act and scale").

**Design:** [PLAN-SILVER-NEXT-ACT.md](evidence/a20_card_floor_20261009/PLAN-SILVER-NEXT-ACT.md),
frozen at `34523017` (binary `187fa5e1…`).
- **Fights:** as in §420 (one paired teacher Silver fight per option and
  encounter, ASC 20, from the post-pick state). `NEXT_ACT=1` adds the next
  act's weak, strong, elite and boss pools for acts 1–2 (fight act + 1), and
  the second boss (the two unrevealed act-3 bosses) for act 3.
- **Counts:** current act as in §416; next act fixed at weak 2, strong 3,
  elite 2, boss 1 (act 3: second boss 1).
- **Rule:** PASS if the gain CI lower bound > 0, else NOT_SHOWN.
- **Execution:** 16 cloud workers × 4 lanes, 128,626 fights, 22.2 CPU h of
  fights.

**Result: `NOT_SHOWN`.**

| States | Next act (primary) | Current act only (§420 score) | CTM strength (§416) |
|--------|--------------------|-------------------------------|---------------------|
| Scored | 966 | 967 | 970 |
| Gain over teacher | −0.29 floors [−0.70, +0.13] | −0.37 [−0.83, +0.13] | +0.14 [−0.24, +0.54] |
| Agreement with teacher | 36% | 35% | 56% |
| Skip rate (teacher 4%) | 24% | 25% | 3% |
| Median option spread | 0.074 | 0.061 | 0.008 |

- **Data quality:** 0 trajectory mismatches; 356 fights invalid or
  unsupported and dropped; 4 states unscored (a whole pool unsupported).
- **Baselines, same states:** uniform random −0.94, oracle +4.28.
- **By act (primary):** −0.52 [−1.18, +0.09], +0.10 [−0.62, +0.80] and
  +0.02 [−0.22, +0.24] in acts 1–3.
- **Skips:** on the 216 states where the score skips and the teacher takes a
  card, the gain is −0.86 floors; on the 710 states where both take a card it
  is −0.16.
- **Mean utility by pool:** current weak 0.90, strong 0.87, elite 0.73,
  boss 0.27; next weak 0.64, strong 0.43, elite 0.17, boss 0.08.

**Interpretation (Inference):**
- The §420 pilot was a kind sample. At full scale the current-act Silver
  score is −0.37, not +0.64, and the next act moves it only to −0.29.
- Silver strength beats a random pick by about 0.65 floors but does not beat
  the teacher, and is no better than the much cheaper CTM score.
- Adding the next act did not remove the skip bias (24% vs 25%). Fights from
  the current HP, with no rests, upgrades or later cards, mostly lose against
  next-act elites and bosses, so those pools add little separation.
- Most of the loss comes from skipping cards the teacher takes.

**Evidence:** [report-silver-next-act.json](evidence/a20_card_floor_20261009/report-silver-next-act.json),
[report-silver-next-act-current-only.json](evidence/a20_card_floor_20261009/report-silver-next-act-current-only.json),
raw outputs in `/mnt/project-files/card-strength-probe/silver-next-act-34523017/`.
The §420 skip-rate row is corrected to the teacher's 6% on the pilot states.

**Knowledge impact:** this entry, plus the default-off `NEXT_ACT` argument of
`cardstrengthprobe` and `--current-act-only` in `tools/a20_card_strength.py`.
No defaults changed.

## §417 — #347 default-stack boss deaths: 40% winnable on a planner re-roll, 40% lost every time (2026-10-09)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-09, #347 triage):** most default-stack losses are boss
deaths and more boss search did not help (§377, §387). Are those deaths fights
the same combat policy would usually win with another planner seed (combat is
the lever), or entries it loses every time (preparation is the lever)?
**Design:** [PLAN](evidence/boss_deaths_default_347_20261009/PLAN.md) frozen at
`93d0bd35` before any seed ran. Default stack: ADR-0026 live profile (V4 gate
stack, learned-stop Silver, 10k cap), OOC MCTS off, Act-3 stop, current main
gameplay. Stage 1: 256 fresh runs, seeds 66000000..66000255 (the §395 Fprod rows
are not in the repo, and current main cannot reconstruct the §377 runs).
Stage 2: every boss death is reconstructed with `bossrescue347` (new schema
`boss_deaths_default_347_selection_v1`) and replayed with 8 fresh planner seeds
under the same learned-stop policy; the live battle RNG is unchanged. Per entry
0/8 = `DOOMED`, ≥ 4/8 = `WINNABLE`, else `MARGINAL`; verdict by which class
holds at least half the entries.
**Validity:** 214/256 runs won (83.6%); 42 losses, 35 to an act boss (act
1/2/3: 1/13/21). All 35 entries `VALID`: exact reconstruction, exact control
parity (outcome, terminal HP, action trace, post-exit digest, simulations),
identical repeats, no root above 10k. 1.74 CPU-hours in total.
**Result:** `MIXED`. 15 `WINNABLE`, 14 `DOOMED`, 6 `MARGINAL`; mean fresh win
rate 40.0%, entry bootstrap 95% [26.4%, 53.6%]; bimodal (14 entries 0/8, 7
entries 8/8). Time Eater 14/80 fresh wins (7 of 10 doomed), Awakened One 6/48
(4 of 6), while Automaton 24/24, Donu and Deca 25/40, Champ 24/56. Act 2 59/104,
act 3 45/168. Doomed entries arrive with 61% of max HP, winnable ones with 83%.
**Interpretation (Inference):** both levers are real. About 40% of boss deaths
are planner variance on winnable entries, so combat consistency (not budget)
matters there. Another 40% are lost on every replay, mostly at Time Eater and
Awakened One and at lower entry HP; this experiment cannot tell preparation
from a combat weakness specific to those bosses. The 40% is conditional on a
lost fight and is not a win-rate estimate. Planner repeats share one game
environment.
**Decision:** diagnostic only; no default change.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/boss_deaths_default_347_20261009/README.md);
copies in `/mnt/project-files/boss-deaths-347/`.

**Knowledge impact:** this entry; `bossrescue347` gains a schema, recorded in
`docs/knowledge-base/CODE_MAP.md` and `operations/ooc-label-pipeline.md` where
the mode is routed.

## §414 — OOC MCTS root selection × cpuct screen: picking by mean Q is far worse, no cpuct beats 1.5 (2026-10-09)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-09):** on seed 63000084 (the §412 `cand` arm's Act 1 Hexaghost loss) the search's own
Q preferred a different root option at several decisions, but OOC MCTS picks the most-visited option, and at cpuct 1.5
the visits follow the V4 prior. Does picking the root option by mean Q, or another cpuct, win more runs?
A single-seed replay (pick by Q won that seed; cpuct 0.5 and temperature 2 still lost; a uniform leaf policy changed
nothing, because with `LEAF_COMBATS=0` the leaf playout never runs) prompted a pre-registered paired screen.

**Design:** [PREREG.md](evidence/ooc_mcts_q_select_screen_20261009/PREREG.md), written before any cohort seed.
* Base = the §412 `cand` arm verbatim (OOC MCTS on, pathb-r2 CTM, 2048 sims, early stop, V4 prior, screen-GBM leaf,
  fair native Silver exact 10k, Ironclad A0, stop after the Act 3 boss), binary `dddb09f0` built from `648334e3`.
* 8 arms: root selection {visits, mean Q} × cpuct {0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 3.0}; control `v15` = current setting.
  With Q selection the planner skips the visit-lock early stop, so Q arms always spend 2048 sims per root.
* Seeds `65000000..65000127` (128, paired across all arms), smoke `65009000`. 32 cloud workers × 4 CPU,
  512 units of 2 seeds, all through `tools/seed_guard.sh`.
* Primary: `q15 − v15` paired win-rate difference, paired bootstrap 95% CI (10,000 resamples), exact McNemar.
  Secondary: every arm vs `v15`; a `CI_ABOVE_0` arm would only earn a fresh-seed confirmation.

**Deviations** ([DEVIATIONS.md](evidence/ooc_mcts_q_select_screen_20261009/DEVIATIONS.md)), both before any result
was read: D1, the smoke's integrity check failed because `analyze.py` also read the `.mcts.csv` traces as result
files; fixed (exact `ARM-LO.csv` names only), smoke re-checked on the same outputs and passed. D2, worker 02 killed a
duplicate launch; the four killed units were renamed and rerun whole, and the analyzer ignores them.

**Execution:** 512/512 units rc 0, no seed failures, no missing seeds; 1,024 runs.

**Result: `Q_WORSE`.** No arm beats the control.

| Arm | Win % | Δ vs v15, pp [95% CI] | McNemar p | Mean floor | Boss deaths (act 1/2/3) | Non-boss deaths | CPU s/run |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v05 | 76.6 | −2.3 [−11.7, +7.0] | 0.75 | 47.8 | 3/7/10 | 10 | 115 |
| v10 | 76.6 | −2.3 [−10.2, +5.5] | 0.69 | 49.2 | 0/9/15 | 6 | 110 |
| **v15** (control) | **78.9** | — | — | 49.0 | 1/6/13 | 7 | 113 |
| v30 | 68.0 | −10.9 [−19.5, −2.3] | 0.029 | 47.3 | 0/15/14 | 12 | 110 |
| q05 | 43.8 | −35.2 [−44.5, −25.8] | 2e-10 | 38.2 | 17/17/11 | 27 | 122 |
| q10 | 49.2 | −29.7 [−39.8, −19.5] | 1e-7 | 39.6 | 10/21/6 | 28 | 128 |
| **q15** (primary) | 41.4 | −37.5 [−46.9, −28.1] | 3e-11 | 39.2 | 13/29/10 | 23 | 126 |
| q30 | 35.2 | −43.8 [−53.1, −34.4] | 7e-14 | 37.8 | 12/21/13 | 37 | 118 |

**Post-hoc, descriptive** ([POSTHOC-picks.txt](evidence/ooc_mcts_q_select_screen_20261009/POSTHOC-picks.txt)): the Q
arms skip 33–37% of card rewards (visits arms 0.5–1.6%), smith more than they rest, and at Neow take the second
(non-card) bonus slot in 61–76% of runs (visits at cpuct 1.5: always the card slot). **Inference:** arg-max mean Q
over options with few visits picks noise winners, and it hands the decision to the screen-GBM / X2-B leaf, whose
skip preference and card mispricing are known (§396, 2026-10-07 card-pricing check). At cpuct 1.5 the visit rule lets
the V4 prior overrule that leaf. The seed 63000084 win was a lucky draw.

**Decision:** no change. Root selection stays `visits`, cpuct stays 1.5; OOC MCTS stays off by default (ADR-0027).
Lower cpuct (0.5, 1.0) ties the control; 3.0 is worse. Improving OOC MCTS needs a better leaf, not a different root
rule.

**Evidence:** [folder](evidence/ooc_mcts_q_select_screen_20261009/) (PREREG, worker.sh, analyze.py, brief,
deviations, smoke markers, report.json, post-hoc picks, SHA256SUMS). Raw unit outputs (CSV, logs, traces) are in
`/mnt/project-files/ooc-mcts-q-select-screen/w01..w32/`. Seeds `65000000..65000127` and `65009000` are now used.

**Knowledge impact:** this entry and one paragraph in `docs/knowledge-base/evaluation/current-research.md`; no
defaults or maintained interfaces changed.

## §419 — V4 OOC token net retrained at A20: input guard and Q-head retrain both not adopted; the retrain on 2x data is worse (2026-10-10)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-09 21:46Z):** retrain V4 at A20. The deployed V4
(`ooc_strategic_tok_final.native`, sha e62abd83) was trained on A0 only: ascension, blueKey and
greenKey have exported `inv = 1e6`, so at A20 the ascension input clamps to +8 against an
untrained weight column.
**Design:** [evidence packet](evidence/v4_a20_retrain_20261009/), pre-registrations committed
before each gate. Gate stack for every arm: live V4 gates (REST/EVENT/SHOP/TREASURE/BOSS_RELIC,
margin 1.0), learned stop gbt-770201c31f7b, keys off, `STS_STOP_AFTER_ACT=3`,
`bestbench 10000 N 20`; primary = mean paired floor difference with a 95% paired bootstrap CI.
- **G1** input guard (`STS_OOC_STRATEGIC_TOK_CONST_GUARD=1`: training-constant inputs fed as 0),
  seeds 67100000–127.
- **Data:** `strategicgen2` at A20 on frozen `2c89ed97` (binary 4a3c9ecc), 8 sampled decisions per
  run, every option played to the run's end 4 times with common random numbers, Silver 2,000
  exact root sims with root prior v1 (w400). Round 1: 25 workers × 9 h, seeds 67M, 611 runs,
  4,856 labeled decisions. Round 2: 48 workers × ~4.5 h, seeds 68M, 642 runs, 5,136 decisions.
- **Training:** `STRAT_LABEL_SCALE=floor` (new trainer option), warm start from the deployed V4
  re-imported by `tools/import_strategic_tok_native.py` (byte-exact round trip), Q head only,
  best validation strict Q top-1, seed-disjoint split.
- **G2** round-1 candidate (sha 135e5500), seeds 67200000–127. **G3** round 1 + 2 candidate
  (sha 08d239f9), seeds 67300000–255.

**Result:**

| Gate | Arms | Wins | Mean floor | T − C floor [95% CI] | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | current / guard | 16 / 12 of 128 | 36.12 / 34.90 | −1.22 [−3.51, +1.11] | not adopted |
| G2 | current / r1 retrain | 14 / 12 of 128 | 33.39 / 32.29 | −1.10 [−4.16, +1.96] | `NOT_SHOWN` |
| G3 | current / r1+r2 retrain | 29 / 16 of 256 | 35.07 / 29.48 | −5.59 [−7.75, −3.38] | `RETRAIN_WORSE` |

Offline strict Q top-1 on held-out decisions with ≥ 2 labeled options: random 0.255, heuristic
chosen action 0.334 (r1) / 0.341 (r1+r2), deployed V4 0.255 / 0.268, retrain 0.309 / 0.302.
**Interpretation (Inference):** no model beats the heuristic it overrides on these labels, and
doubling the labels did not raise offline accuracy, so one-ply heuristic-continuation labels at
~4 playouts per option look too noisy for a better A20 Q head. The A0-only training of V4 is
not a measurable A20 win-rate lever. Current V4 at A20 with this stack: 59/512 wins (11.5%) over
G1–G3 control arms.
**Decision:** no default change; the guard flag and trainer option stay off by default.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/v4_a20_retrain_20261009/). Data and models:
`/mnt/project-files/v4-a20-retrain/`. Seeds 67M and 68M are now used.

**Knowledge impact:** `operations/environment-variables.md` documents
`STS_OOC_STRATEGIC_TOK_CONST_GUARD`; one paragraph in `evaluation/current-research.md`.

## §422 — rollout3 OOC MCTS replicates on the current CTM: +10.9 pp wins over MCTS off (2026-10-10)

**Question:** §277's rollout3 profile (V4 prior, 2048 sims, native `v_win` leaf after 3 extra CTM
combats) won 28/32 vs V4 24/32 on the old V2 CTM (CI crossed zero). Does it win more runs than MCTS
off on the current stack? Requested by Philipp after §391's boss-rollout leaf was traced to a
saturated, noisy 0/1 value (act-1 root Q ≈ 0.997; this thread's probe, seeds 69000001–004).
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/ooc_rollout3_replication_20261010/PREREG.md) frozen at `f5734322`
after independent review (PR #475). Code `cd405b4c`, binary `39cdac96…`, production pathb-r2 CTM,
sampled noncombat futures, `STS_REST_WIN=0`, 1 OMP thread; control = MCTS off on the §411 research
base (flat exact-10k Silver). Seeds 70000000–127 (smoke 70009000), 16 cloud workers × 4 CPU.
Primary: paired bootstrap 95% CI of Δwin; REPLICATED if the lower bound > 0.
**Validity:** 160/160 units rc=0, 128/128 pairs, no seed failures, config banners checked.
**Result:** **REPLICATED.** rollout3 115/128 (89.8%) vs off 101/128 (78.9%), Δwin +10.9 pp
[+2.3, +19.5], discordant 23 vs 9, McNemar p = 0.020. Boss deaths 11 vs 23; Δfloor +0.69
[−0.65, +2.0]; Δ end HP +12.6. Cost 936 vs 57 s per run (about 16x); 105k simulations and 850 s MCTS
CPU per run. 19.8% of OOC decisions fell back to V4 (99% of support aborts are Lizard Tail).
**Interpretation (Inference):** the gain comes mostly from fewer boss deaths. The value comes from
the 3-combat rollout leaf (contrast §384 `screengbm` leaf −22 pp, §391 boss rollout 9/32).
**Decision:** no default change (pre-registered). Candidates for follow-up, one variable at a time
on these seeds: uniform prior, outcome merging, no early stop, cheaper budgets; then a fresh-seed
confirmation.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/ooc_rollout3_replication_20261010/README.md). Raw:
`/mnt/project-files/ooc-rollout3-replication/`. Seeds 70000000–127 and 70009000 are now used.

## §423 — Lizard-capable CTM inside rollout3: aborts gone, no win gain (2026-10-11)

**Question:** in §422, 19.8% of rollout3 OOC decisions fell back to V4, 99% of them on active Lizard Tail states the
production CTM refuses (Fairy Potion + Tail 1,889, Entropic Brew + Tail 875). Philipp: "first fix the lizard tail issue".
Does rollout3 with a CTM that prices those states win more than §422 rollout3?
**Candidate:** production pathb-r2 fast artifact with a header-only `tools/ctm_lizard.py extend --brew --fairy`
(`c6d56bbc…`, research-candidate manifest `64da1776…`); Brew r refit on the cloud Path B `lizard_fairy`/`lizard_brew`
corpora, production fast r unchanged, no C++ change. Composed survival on those corpora: Fairy+Tail predicted 0.9987 vs
observed 0.9984 (119 Tail-fired rows), Brew+Tail 0.9982 vs 0.9977 (43).
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/ooc_rollout3_lizard_20261010/PREREG.md), independent review PASS (`bd991730`), run commit
`cf801ef2`, binary `39cdac96…`. Only the candidate arm ran (16 cloud workers, seeds 70000000–127); control = the
§422 rollout3 runs, reused after the rerun of seed 70000000 matched them byte for byte. Forced-Tail smoke 72000000–001.
Primary: paired bootstrap 95% CI of Δwin; IMPROVED / WORSE / NOT_SHOWN.
**Validity:** 128/128 units rc=0, no seed failures, banners and §422 hashes checked, 0 Lizard support failures.
**Result:** **NOT_SHOWN.** 111/128 (86.7%) vs 115/128 (89.8%), Δwin −3.1 pp [−10.9, +4.7], discordant 11 vs 15,
McNemar p = 0.56. Boss deaths 14 vs 11; Δfloor +0.06. Fallback 2.4% vs 19.8%, support aborts 0 vs 21.8 per run;
1,075 vs 936 s per run. On the 13 seeds with >40% fallback in §422: 11 vs 13 wins.
**Interpretation (Inference):** the V4 fallback on active-Tail states was not what limited rollout3; pricing those

## §424 — rollout3 at 512 simulations: a third of the cost, between off and 2048 (2026-10-11)

**Question:** rollout3 at 2048 simulations (§422) wins +10.9 pp over MCTS off at about 16x CPU. Philipp: "continue,
lets do 512 sims". Does rollout3 at 512 simulations still beat MCTS off, and how much of the 2048 result does it keep?
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/ooc_rollout3_sims512_20261011/PREREG.md), independent review PASS (`3c9493da`; delta
`ab16de57` for tar upload). Arm `r512` = §422 rollout3 environment with `STS_OOC_MCTS_SIMS=512`, binary `39cdac96…`,
8 cloud workers × 16 seeds 70000000–127; controls = §422 `off` (primary) and `rollout3` 2048 (secondary), reused (the
§423 launch gate showed §422 runs rerun byte for byte). Smoke 72000002. Primary: paired bootstrap 95% CI of
r512 − off; GAIN_KEPT / WORSE_THAN_OFF / NOT_SHOWN.
**Validity:** 128/128 units rc=0, no seed failures, tar hashes, banners and §422 hashes checked.
**Result:** **NOT_SHOWN.** r512 108/128 (84.4%) vs off 101/128 (78.9%): +5.5 pp [−3.9, +14.8], discordant 23 vs 16,

## §425 — OOC MCTS root picks on the A20 gold decisions: not shown better than the heuristic (2026-10-11)

**Question (Philipp):** how often does OOC MCTS pick the best option at A20, on the §419 gold labels
(524 decisions, every option played to the run's end 16 times)? All MCTS models are A0-trained.
**Design:** offline, no live play. `strategicgen2` replay (run commit `d93fad14`, binary `cd0bb658…`) re-plays each
gold run with its recorded actions and runs 4 OOC MCTS searches per labeled decision (search run seeds
73000000–73324999). Arms: `prod` (§411/§414 settings, `screengbm` leaf, pathb-r2 CTM) and `rollout3` (§422).
Targets scored only if every replayed row up to the decision matches the gold row; 386 of 409 multi-option decisions
verified. Decision bootstrap, 10,000 samples.
**Result:** on 378 verified decisions with a recorded choice, mean floor regret: heuristic 4.55, `prod` 4.35
(Δ −0.20 [−0.89, +0.49]), `rollout3` 4.22 (Δ −0.33 [−0.77, +0.12]); random 4.88. Tie-aware top-1 0.276 / 0.280 /
0.295 (random 0.260). Strict top-1 (GOLD-RESULT definition) 0.344 / 0.252 / 0.286; the gap comes from reward screens,
where the heuristic's gold-pile pick wins first-argmax ties and MCTS collects gold at the root. `rollout3` aborts
24% of searches at A20 (Lizard Tail 316, `hp_envelope` 54 of 1,544) and falls back. `rollout3` ran on the production pathb-r2 CTM, not the §423 Lizard-capable research candidate (`STS_CTM_RESEARCH_CANDIDATE_MANIFEST`, manifest `64da1776…`); that is the cause of the Lizard Tail aborts, the large majority of its aborts (a follow-up check on 4 gold seeds: 7/8 searches aborted on the production CTM, 0/8 on the candidate, on decisions picked because they had aborted, so 7/8 is not a base rate; search seeds 74002000–74002003; raw `/mnt/project-files/ooc-rollout3-a20-lizard-check/a20-lizard-check.tgz`).
**Interpretation (Inference):** with A0 models, OOC MCTS is not shown better than the heuristic at A20 (CIs allow
up to about 0.9 floors), and neither is far from random on these labels. Rerun with A20 floor/win models when they exist.
**Side finding (verified in review):** `finishOocCounterfactual` sets `t_curPath = nullptr` on return and
`strategicgen2` never restores it, so from the first decision with options on, the gold runs' main-trajectory policy
ran path-blind (no undefined behaviour; readers fall back to an empty path). Replaying unforced with `t_curPath`
cleared at labeled decisions reproduces seeds 69100000 and 69101007 exactly. Branch labels are unaffected; the
"heuristic" baseline here is this path-blind variant of the production heuristic. **Unverified:** likely every
`strategicgen2` run with branching is affected, possibly including the A0 corpus behind the deployed V4.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/ooc_mcts_a20_gold_20261011/README.md). Seeds 73000000–73324999 (search run seeds)
are now used; the Lizard check used search seeds 74002000–74002003 (Lizard thread's 74002xxx block).

**Knowledge impact:** one paragraph in `evaluation/current-research.md`.

## §431 — Generator OOC policy drift: strategicgen's copied chain plays 4.5 floors worse at A20; all generators now share the deployed step (2026-10-11)

**Question (code audit 2026-10-11, finding 1):** the strategic generators and the counterfactual continuation each
copied the out-of-combat chain and the copies drifted from `runFullRunOOC`. How far do they diverge from the deployed
policy, and does it reach the labels?
**Design:** measurement-only probe `oocpolicydrift` (commits `474237b8`, `cd1d99a5`, `8790fa27`; removed with the
refactor). It plays a run with one chain as the main trajectory and at every OOC decision applies all four chains to
copies of the same state and agent: `canon` (`runFullRunOocPolicyStep`, shop value on), `sg` (strategicgen and
strategicgen2 main trajectory), `cf` (`finishOocCounterfactual` continuation, which produces every Tier-B branch label)
and `v4` (`stepFrozenV4Ooc`, strategicmarggen/oocfactoreval). Release, 1000 sims, default flags; 64 A0 and 64 A20
seeds, plus 32 A0 seeds with the V4 gates on. The `canon` trajectory equals `bestbench` on 128/128 seeds.
**Result:**
- Per decision, resolving the whole screen: `sg` differs at 5.6% (A0) / 6.3% (A20) of decisions, about 9 per run,
  mostly shops (455 of 623 A0 shop visits: the agent heuristic buys the first affordable relic or takes a random
  action instead of shop value), card selects and Match and Keep; `cf` and `v4` differ at 0.6-1.4% (removal by shop
  value outside shops, Match and Keep, `cf` resting by first legal action). With the V4 gates on, `sg` and `cf` ignore
  them and differ at 16.3% / 13.0% of decisions (`v4` 0.3%). Reward order (relic before gold, potions with full slots)
  differs on about 600 reward screens per 64 runs but leaves the same state.
- As the main trajectory, paired against `canon`: A20 `sg` −4.48 floors [−8.38, −0.72], wins 1/64 vs 7/64
  (−9.4 pp [−17.2, −3.1]); A20 `cf` −0.80 [−2.91, +1.25], `v4` −0.56 [−2.64, +1.53]; at A0 nothing is detectable
  (`sg` −0.33 [−2.80, +2.00]). Identical end states: A0 `sg` 5/64, `cf` 30/64, `v4` 36/64.
- `strategicgen2` labels before vs after the refactor (32 seeds per ascension, 8 sampled decisions per run, K=3), on
  labeled decisions whose pre-states are still identical: argmax(labelFloor) unchanged on 31/32 (A0) and 75/77 (A20);
  some option label changed on 4/32 and 13/77; mean labelFloor shift +0.03 and −0.39.
**Interpretation (Inference):** the gap is real. Data from `strategicgen`/`strategicgen2` main trajectories (the A20
value-model runs `runs-2c89ed97`, the §419 A20 V4 corpora and gold runs) carry won/endFloor/endHp outcomes of a
policy about 4.5 floors weaker at A20 than deployment, and their `chosen` rows imitate it. Branch labels moved little
on the comparable states, but only early decisions are comparable, and with the V4 gates on the continuation ignored
them at 13% of decisions. Effect on any trained model: **Unverified**.
**Change:** `deployedOocPolicyStep` (`apps/one_combat/run_driver.cpp`) is now the only OOC step for `strategicgen`,
`strategicgen2`, `finishOocCounterfactual` and `stepFrozenV4Ooc` (so also the branch continuations of the
`counterfactual_gen.cpp` generators, `oocfactoreval` and `semantic_pilot.cpp`, whose main trajectories keep their own
chains); `strategicgen`/`strategicgen2` also reset path-policy state per seed and use `fightSims` like
`runFullRunOOC` (no-ops at default flags); oracles stand down inside continuations; ctest `generator_policy_parity`
pins `strategicgen`/`strategicgen2` end states to `bestbench` (continuations and the V4 step are not pinned by a test
of their own). Default `bestbench` play is bit-identical: 8 seeds at 300 sims here, and in independent review 180 runs
(seeds 74008900-989, A0 and A20, 1000 sims) with identical traces. Data generated before this change is not
regenerated.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/generator_policy_drift_20261011/README.md). Seeds used: 74008000-063, 74008100-163,
74008200-231, 74008300-331, 74008400-431, smoke/tests 74008990-999.

**Knowledge impact:** generator policy parity paragraph in `architecture/training-and-inference.md`.

## §432 — `strategicgen2` branch futures shared their combats; with independent futures, short-branch labels beat the heuristic at A20 (2026-10-11)

**Question:** §419's A20 Q-head retrains and §425's MCTS scoring used `strategicgen2` labels averaged over
`STRATEGIC_BRANCH_FUTURES` (4 in the §419 corpus, 16 in the gold set). Are those futures independent, and which
label source ranks A20 options best once they are?
**Bug (verified in code and by rerun):** each future only changed the agent RNG. Native Silver combat does not
consume it, and battle RNG is `Random(gc.seed + gc.floorNum)` (`src/combat/BattleContext.cpp:50`), so the futures of
an option shared their encounters and battle RNG. They diverged only through out-of-combat choices that draw on the
agent RNG (`apps/one_combat.cpp:1699`): 55% of the 2,258 old gold labels end on a non-integer mean floor, and in a
no-reseed run changing only the future index changed 39% of labels. The effective number of samples per label was
therefore well below the nominal 4 (§419 corpus) or 16 (gold). The pilot short-branch labels (3 fights, 8 futures)
also shared gold's first fights, which made them agree with gold more than they should. **Unverified:** which A0 `strategicgen2` corpora with
`STRATEGIC_BRANCH_FUTURES>1` are affected the same way.
**Fix (default off):** `STRATEGIC_BRANCH_RESEED=1` sets each future's `gc.seed` to its branch seed and redraws the
act's remaining encounters before the action; all options of a decision share future `f` (common random numbers).
Persistent out-of-combat streams (`cardRng`, `eventRng`, `merchantRng`, …; `GameContext.cpp:92-102`) are not
reseeded. `STRATEGIC_BRANCH_FUTURE_OFFSET` shifts the branch seed index so two runs on the same decisions get
disjoint futures. Default-off labels are unchanged (seed 69100001 byte-identical).
**Design:** commit `65ed71f4`, Release `one_combat` sha256 `a2ef5fb3…`, ASC 20, Silver 2k with the natpert prior
(weight 400), the 262 §419 gold seeds (69100000+1000W+k, reused on purpose).
- **Gold2:** full-run labels, `STRATEGIC_BRANCH_FUTURES=16`, `RESEED=1`, offset 0, 25 workers. 260/262 seeds
  finished (69116003 crashed with Silver "descent exceeded depth bound"; 69103004 hit the 12,000 s timeout after
  repeated loop-guard lost fights). Main trajectories match the old gold row for row (108,579 rows, 0 `chosen` or
  floor mismatches), so the decisions are the same. Old-vs-Gold2 option labels correlate 0.81 overall but only 0.35
  within a decision (2,128 labels, decision means removed); the overall figure is mostly between-decision spread.
- **SB2:** short-branch labels, 3 fights then a value-tree bootstrap, `FUTURES=8`, `RESEED=1`, offset 100 (disjoint
  from Gold2), 8 workers. Each option is scored by both the A0 trees (`v_rich_trees`, `v_win_trees`) and the A20
  candidates `models/candidates/v_rich_a20_419.txt` / `v_win_a20_419.txt` via `STS_CF_ALT_BOOT_FLOOR_TREES` /
  `_WIN_TREES` (XGBoost on 1.0M states from 101k `strategicgen` A20 runs; held-out floor R² 0.51 vs −0.56 for A0,
  win AUC 0.85 vs 0.82).
- **Metric:** mean floor regret against the Gold2-best option (Gold2 mean floor of the picked option vs the best
  one), on the 397 decisions with ≥2 labelled options that every picker covers; paired decision bootstrap, 10,000
  samples. Top-1 counts ties as hits. Neural pickers scored with `train_strategic_tok.py` at 0 epochs plus a
  per-decision dump (patch in the packet).

**Result (Gold2, 397 decisions):**

| Picker | Regret (floors) | Top-1 | Heuristic minus picker |
|---|---|---|---|
| SB, A20 floor trees | 1.25 | 0.49 | +1.01 [+0.56, +1.52] |
| SB, A0 floor trees | 1.32 | 0.49 | +0.94 [+0.48, +1.45] |
| SB, A20 win trees | 1.44 | 0.49 | +0.82 [+0.37, +1.32] |
| SB, A0 win trees | 1.50 | 0.45 | +0.76 [+0.34, +1.22] |
| §419 G2 retrain | 1.84 | 0.42 | +0.42 [+0.06, +0.82] |
| §419 G3 retrain | 1.95 | 0.40 | +0.32 [−0.08, +0.74] |
| old gold (shared combats) | 1.96 | 0.42 | +0.31 [−0.17, +0.81] |
| deployed V4 (A0) | 1.98 | 0.42 | +0.28 [−0.09, +0.68] |
| heuristic (path-blind, §425) | 2.26 | 0.41 | 0 |
| random | 2.69 | — | −0.42 [−0.73, −0.11] |

A20 vs A0 floor trees inside SB: +0.07 [−0.10, +0.24] (not shown). Floor trees beat win trees only borderline
(A20: +0.19 [+0.01, +0.40]; another bootstrap seed gives [−0.00, +0.39]). Against the old gold (independent of SB2's combats, 409 decisions) the order is the same: SB A20
floor 2.86, heuristic 4.45, random 4.78; heuristic minus SB A20 floor +1.56 [+0.84, +2.28].
**Interpretation (Inference):** Gold2's best option is still noisy (16 samples), so all regrets are inflated by a
common amount; the ranking is the result. Short-branch labels with independent futures are the first A20 label source
clearly better than the heuristic, and better than the old shared-combat full-run labels. The
§419 retrains were limited by their one-sample labels. The A20 candidate trees were fit on `strategicgen` v1 runs,
whose main trajectory plays about 4.5 floors worse than `bestbench` at A20 (§431), so their absolute values are
pessimistic; here they only rank options, where they tie the A0 trees.
**Open question:** SB2 and Gold2 differ in combats (battle RNG, encounters) but still share the persistent
out-of-combat streams (card rewards, events, shops), so they are disjoint in combat only; some agreement between them
may come from those shared streams.
**Not done:** no live gameplay test; no new label corpus; trees not refit after the §431 generator fix.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/v4_a20_retrain_20261009/gold2/README.md) (`gold2_score.txt`, `sb2_vs_oldgold.txt`,
scoring scripts, rebuild recipe, A20 tree training script and log, tarball sha256s). Raw data `/mnt/project-files/v4-a20-retrain/gold2-w{0..24}.tar.gz` and
`sb2-gold-w{0..7}.tar.gz`. Seeds: reruns of the §419 gold seeds only; no new seed block.

**Knowledge impact:** §425 and §419 paragraphs in `evaluation/current-research.md` corrected (gold futures shared their
combats); new paragraph for §432; three rows in `operations/environment-variables.md`.

## §427–§430 — four one-setting rollout3 variants: fewer chance outcomes is worse, the rest not shown (2026-10-11)

**Question:** Philipp: "can you try the following things on teh same 128 seeds: 4096 simulations, different
progressing widening for the chance nodes (one cofnig for mroe and one for fewer), and rollout 5 isntead of 3". Does
any single change to rollout3 (§422: 2048 simulations, chance widening `K=2, alpha=0.5`, 3 rollout combats) win more?
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/ooc_rollout3_variants_20261011/PREREG.md). Arms, each the §422 rollout3 environment with
one change: §427 `s4096` (`SIMS=4096`), §428 `wnarrow` (`WIDEN_K=1`, `WIDEN_ALPHA=0.25`), §429 `wbroad` (`WIDEN_K=4`,
`WIDEN_ALPHA=0.75`), §430 `r5` (`LEAF_COMBATS=5`; commit `0ee840b1` makes 5 an accepted value, default unchanged).
Binary `3269ece9…`; launch gate: §422 seed 70000000 rerun byte-identical, so the §422 `rollout3` and `off` runs are the
paired controls. 32 cloud workers (8 per arm × 16 seeds 70000000–127). Smokes 72000003–005. Primary per arm: paired
bootstrap 95% CI of arm − rollout3 (seed 427); IMPROVED / WORSE / NOT_SHOWN, no multiplicity correction.
**Validity:** 512/512 units rc=0, no seed failures or restarts, tar hashes, config banners and §422 hashes checked.
**Result:**

| arm | wins | vs rollout3 (115/128) | label | vs off (101/128) | boss deaths | s/run |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| §427 `s4096` | 119/128 | +3.1 pp [−3.1, +9.4] | NOT_SHOWN | +14.1 [+6.3, +21.9] | 8 | 1,784 |
| §428 `wnarrow` | 101/128 | −10.9 pp [−19.5, −2.3], p = 0.02 | **WORSE** | 0.0 [−9.4, +9.4] | 22 | 1,290 |
| §429 `wbroad` | 117/128 | +1.6 pp [−4.7, +7.8] | NOT_SHOWN | +12.5 [+4.7, +21.1] | 9 | 988 |
| §430 `r5` | 112/128 | −2.3 pp [−10.2, +5.5] | NOT_SHOWN | +8.6 [−0.8, +18.0] | 10 | 1,458 |

rollout3 itself: 11 boss deaths, 936 s per run. V4 fallback 27.6% (`s4096`) and 37.1% (`r5`) vs 19.8%; in every arm
88–94% of fallbacks are support aborts and 98–100% of those are active Lizard Tail states.
**Interpretation (Inference):** few sampled outcomes per chance node lose the whole rollout3 gain (`wnarrow`'s WORSE
rests on p = 0.02 uncorrected; Bonferroni across the four arms gives 0.08); more simulations or
more outcomes point up but 128 pairs cannot separate them from rollout3. Five rollout combats hit Lizard Tail states
more often and fall back to V4 on 37% of decisions.
**Decision:** no default change.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/ooc_rollout3_variants_20261011/README.md). Raw: `/mnt/project-files/ooc-rollout3-variants/`
(one tar per worker). Seeds 72000003–005 are now used.

**Knowledge impact:** `LEAF_COMBATS` accepts 5 in `architecture/out-of-combat.md`; one sentence in the rollout3
paragraph of `evaluation/current-research.md`.

## §433 — fresh-seed confirmation: rollout3 at 4096 simulations with broad chance widening beats MCTS off (2026-10-12)

**Question:** Philipp, 2026-10-11 21:04Z: "yes good idea, lets do that" to a fresh-seed confirmation of the two best
§427–§430 settings combined. On fresh seeds, does rollout3 with `SIMS=4096`, `WIDEN_K=4`, `WIDEN_ALPHA=0.75` (`combo`)
win more runs than MCTS off?
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/ooc_rollout3_confirm_20261011/PREREG.md), independent plan review PASS (analysis-time nits
applied). Arms `combo`, `rollout3` (§422, 2048 simulations) and `off` (§422), all run on seeds 76000000–255 with binary
`bab14cd5…` (code `f82eeadd` = main `07a93e36` merged with the §427–§430 code). `off` is the §411 research base with
flat exact-10k Silver, not the production default stack, so its win rate is not the production win rate. 8 cloud workers × 32 seeds × 3 arms (Philipp chose 8 workers). Smokes 76009000–002.
Primary: paired bootstrap 95% CI of combo − off (seed 433); CONFIRMED / WORSE_THAN_OFF / NOT_CONFIRMED.
**Validity:** 768/768 units rc=0, 0 Silver stalls in every arm (stall-as-loss sensitivity identical), config banners
checked by grep (`off` has none), tar hashes checked twice.
**Result:** **CONFIRMED.** combo 224/256 (87.5%) vs off 199/256 (77.7%): +9.8 pp [+3.9, +16.0], discordant 45 vs 20,
p = 0.003. Secondary: combo − rollout3 (213/256, 83.2%) +4.3 pp [−1.6, +10.2], p = 0.19; rollout3 − off +5.5 pp
[−1.2, +12.1], p = 0.13. Boss deaths 15 / 32 / 42. Seconds per run 1,536 / 893 / 55; V4 fallback 27.8% / 21.6%, nearly
all Lizard Tail support aborts.
**Interpretation (Inference):** `combo`'s gain over off holds on fresh seeds; plain rollout3's §422 gain (+10.9 pp) did
not reach significance here (+5.5 pp, CI includes zero). The run does not separate the combination from plain rollout3,
which costs about half as much. All arms ran with `STS_OOC_PUBLIC_FUTURES` off, so the
native fallback reads true upcoming encounters (#397); that favours `off`, which uses it on every decision.
**Decision:** no default change from this run alone. A default proposal would weigh `combo` against plain rollout3 and
the 16–28x CPU cost.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/ooc_rollout3_confirm_20261011/README.md). Raw: `/mnt/project-files/ooc-rollout3-confirm/`
(one tar per worker). Seeds 76000000–76000255 and 76009000–002 are now used.

## §436 — Simulator and CTM speed: rollout3 −10%, default stack −2%, play bit-identical (2026-10-11)

**Question:** issue #350 follow-up. Where does CPU go on the default stack and in §422 rollout3 (936 vs 57 s per
run), and is there a speedup that keeps play bit-identical?
**Method:** baseline `491bc21b`, Release `one_combat` (no `-march`, no FMA), §422 `off` and `rollout3` environments,
one thread, `gprofng` PC sampling, seeds 74014000–74014011.
**Profile:** `off` is flat as in §360; the one new item is `BattleContext()` construction for new Silver nodes
(4.2%). In rollout3 the Silver simulator is only about 5.5% of CPU; `CompactTreeNet::predict` takes 32% (#338's
scope), the CTM encoder 28% (almost all in `CombatTransitionRuntime::linear`), the V4 network about 25%.
**Change:** (1) CTM `linear` keeps a transposed weight copy and computes the rows in parallel lanes, each row's sum
in the original order, so outputs are bit-identical. (2) Silver recycles decision states through a per-thread pool
and fills a new node with one copy instead of a three-copy `std::swap`; `nodeCount()` and the reuse cap are unchanged.
The pool keeps freed states alive between combats: the independent review measured peak memory +27–46 MB
(+7–12%); the worst case is 65,536 states, about 0.5 GB per thread.
**Parity:** result CSVs, OOC decision traces, MCTS action/support traces and all non-timing MCTS columns are
byte-identical on rollout3 seeds 74014000, 74014001, 74014003 (full) and 74014002 (act 1), on `off` seeds
74014000–74014011, and `test silver_profile` digests match.
**Speed:** rollout3 paired run −9.6% wall, −9.8% MCTS CPU (1,607 → 1,452 s); act 1 −10.7%. `off` paired 4 seeds
−2.1%; `test silver_profile 10000 4` −6.4% (median of 3).
**Decision:** adopt (pure speedup, exact parity). Batched/SIMD simulator execution not pursued: the simulator is not
where rollout3 spends its time, and the default-stack profile stays flat.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/sim_speed_issue350_2026-10-11/README.md). Seeds 74014000–74014011 and the reviewer's
74014900–903 and 74014910–911 are now used.

**Knowledge impact:** one sentence each in `architecture/combat-search.md` (state recycling) and the rollout3 cost
paragraph of `evaluation/current-research.md`.

## §437 — rollout3 leaf cost: the native shop planner, not `v_win` features; exact batching 1.13–1.7x, varies by seed (2026-10-11)

**Question:** issue #338: can OOC MCTS leaf evaluation get cheaper with exact parity? Where does rollout3 (§422) spend
its CPU?
**Design:** profile one rollout3 seed with `STS_OOC_CPU_PROFILE=1` plus gdb stack samples; then paired one-seed
`bestbench` units, baseline `main` `491bc21b` vs the candidate, §422 `rollout3` and `off` environments unchanged,
seeds 74013000–004 (rollout3) and 74013001–008 (off). Parity = byte-identical decision and MCTS action traces and
identical non-timing result and MCTS summary rows.
**Profile (baseline, seed 74013000, 937 s MCTS CPU):** `v_win` features 0.37 s (0.04%), `v_win` predict 16.6 s
(1.8%), CTM sampling 211 s (23%), V4 nets in rollout gates 146 s (16%), rollout policy steps between combats 531 s
(57%). Half of all stack samples sit in `nativeShopPlan`, which values every affordable shop subset with a full
1,256-tree floor-model prediction and repeats after each purchase.
**Change:** `CompactTreeNet::predictVariants` values candidate rows that differ from the decision's base vector only
in declared features, walking each tree once for the whole group (bitwise identical to `predict()`); used by
`nativeShopPlan`, `nativeFloorCardPick` and `nativeFloorRemovePick`.
**Result:** 13/13 paired units identical. rollout3 per-run time 1.19x–1.69x faster on these seeds and 1.13x on
the independent reviewer's seed; the gain varies by seed with how much rollout time passes through shops
(74013001–004 total 3,858 → 2,794 s, 1.38x; profiled 74013000 process CPU 1,033 → 626 s, rollout-step CPU 531 →
142 s). `off` 1.01x.
**Decision:** adopt (exact, no behavior change). Incremental `v_win` features stay rejected (as in §380). The largest
remaining rollout3 buckets are CTM sampling and the V4 gates.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/ooc_rollout_leaf_speedup_20261011/README.md). Raw:
`/mnt/project-files/issue338-leaf-speed/raw.tar.gz`. Seeds 74013000–74013008 (and reviewer seeds 74013900–74013904) are now used.

**Knowledge impact:** `predictVariants` paragraph in `architecture/out-of-combat.md`; rollout3 cost sentence in
`evaluation/current-research.md`.

## §438 — #401 feature-importance and grouped ablations of the `v_win`/`v_rich` tree inputs: relics, deck and HP carry the signal; hidden fields are recoverable; the forward map helps floor at A20 (2026-10-11)

**Question:** Issue #401 Stage 1/2 for the tree value models: which semantic input groups does each model
use, which carry unique held-out signal, and which are redundant or missing?
**Design:** analysis only, no gameplay seeds. Models: B0 `v_win_trees.txt` (`fc52c14c…`), X2-B, and the §419
A20 win and floor trees. Data: (a) A0, the four #334 collector returns on the share (122 non-TEST source
seeds, 115k MAP rows; TEST seeds dropped at load); (b) A20, the frozen `2c89ed97` `strategicgen` corpus,
half the chunks, ≤ 8 rows per run (629k rows, 78,643 runs), split by seed hash into TRAIN/ES/VAL/TEST
62/8/15/15 with TEST never used (the A20 permutation was rerun without TEST-split rows after review). Stage 1: joint permutation of each semantic group on held-out rows.
Stage 2: XGBoost refits per arm on A20 TRAIN (early stop on ES), scored on VAL for final floor (MSE) and
won (NLL), seed-cluster bootstrap 95% CIs (VAL sampling only, not refit randomness), plus three
other-seed FULL refits as the null (span 0.09 MSE / 0.0009 NLL); a small A0 refit
cross-check on #334 TRAIN → VALIDATION.
**Result:** A20 refits, Δ vs FULL (floor MSE 101.23; win NLL 0.1447): −relics +6.64 [+5.89, +7.32] /
+0.0118; −deck +5.50 / +0.0054; −HP +3.22 / +0.0018; −potions +0.93, −progress +0.45, −upgrades +0.43
(floor only); dropping all ten hidden-future/queue/RNG-counter columns +0.18 [−0.08, +0.45] / −0.0005
[−0.0014, +0.0003] (this arm also drops the four queue counters, which §371 classes as public; keeping
them gives +0.14 [−0.15, +0.42] / −0.0005); **adding the 12 forward-map columns −2.15 [−2.51, −1.80]** / −0.0008 [−0.0016, −0.0000];
refit null −0.04, +0.05, +0.03 / +0.0004, −0.0000, −0.0005. Bottled, keys, gold, potion slots, boss: no unique value.
Permutation: B0 on A0 uses the hidden future encounters (+0.0155 NLL [0.013, 0.018]), as does the A20
floor tree (+4.3 MSE). Relics are the largest permutation group in every model, spread over many relics.
The A0 cross-check resolves nothing (training-seed spread up to 0.013 NLL; −relics points better,
−0.033 [−0.073, +0.004]). B0 underpredicts #334 wins (mean 0.58 vs 0.76; NLL 0.611).
**Interpretation (Inference):** B0 and the A20 floor tree use the hidden fields (the A20 win tree does
not), but no loss from a public-only refit is detected at A20 (at most about 0.45 floor MSE), consistent
with §371. The forward map, the only missing group tested, helps the floor target at A20; §418's A0
result stays `INCONCLUSIVE`. All results are offline prediction-error changes on the generators' own
runs, not win-rate changes.
**Decision:** no model, default or contract change. Recommendations: keep relics, deck, HP, potions,
progress, upgrades; include the forward-map block in the next A20 value-model retrain (off by default
until gated); no cost of a public-only contract is detected at A20 (#397); test cyclic relic counters
as presence (floor −0.19 [−0.38, +0.01]) on the next retrain; no deletions of cheap low-value groups.
**Not done:** MLP, #379, #399, #400, CTM; live test; TEST split; feature-build timing; full #334 corpus.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/feature_audit_401_20261011/README.md) (scripts, permutation and ablation
JSON, scored tables). No seeds used (the 74016000–74016999 block stays unused).

**Knowledge impact:** one paragraph after the #397/#396 paragraphs in `evaluation/current-research.md`.

## §439 — CTM in rollout3: about a quarter of CPU, almost all DeepSets token MLPs; exact per-token memo 2.8x on the CTM, 1.20–1.24x per run (2026-10-12)

**Question:** where does the combat transition model spend its time in §422 rollout3 on current `main` (after
§436/§437), how large is its share, and can it get cheaper with bit-identical play?
**Method:** baseline `main` `b039e846`, Release `one_combat`, §422 `rollout3`/`off` environments plus
`STS_OOC_CPU_PROFILE=1`, `gprofng` PC sampling, seeds 74022000–74022005 (one rollout3 unit with
`STS_OOC_MCTS_PRIOR=uniform`).
**Profile:** CTM `combat_resolve` 150 s of 619 s process CPU (24%; uniform prior 118 of 479 s, 25%), 304k
unprepared samples in leaf rollouts at 0.49 ms each. Each sample ran four DeepSets encoders (survival, max_hp,
hp, potion), each a two-layer MLP per card, relic and potion token. Other large rollout3 costs:
`predictVariants` in the native shop planner 23%, the V4 network about a quarter, real Silver combats 12%.
**Change:** (1) a per-thread memo of each token's MLP output, keyed by runtime instance, encoder group and the
token's integer fields, with pools still summed in token order; (2) the pathb-r2 fast artifact's `max_hp`
encoder is a byte-identical copy of its `hp` encoder (checked at load), so the unprepared near-full sampler
takes maxHP from the hp encoding, as the prepared path already did.
**Parity:** result, OOC decision, MCTS action/support traces and non-timing MCTS columns byte-identical on rollout3
74022000, 74022002, 74022003, uniform-prior 74022001 and `off` 74022004–005 (final binary re-checked on 74022002
and `off` 74022004–005). New ctest `ctm_encoder_memo_parity`: two DeepSets artifacts, memoized and interleaved, against the
unmemoized reference on 62 fixture inputs (1,240 bitwise comparisons); removing the encoder group, the runtime
instance or any key field from the memo key makes it fail.
**Speed:** CTM CPU 2.8x lower (150–193 → 42–69 s on the four rollout3 seeds); per run 1.20x (paired 74022002,
74022003), 1.23x (74022000 process CPU, both profiled), 1.24x (uniform prior); `off` unchanged. The CTM is now about
10% of rollout3 CPU.
**Decision:** adopt (pure speedup, exact parity). Pointer pre-resolution for the remaining CTM `linear` calls is not
worth a change at about 10% share; the next rollout3 levers are the shop planner and the V4 network, not the CTM.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/ctm_encoder_memo_20261012/README.md). Raw: `/mnt/project-files/ctm-speed-439/raw.tar.gz`.
Seeds 74022000–74022005 are now used.

**Knowledge impact:** CTM cost sentence in the rollout3 paragraph of `evaluation/current-research.md`; memo sentence
in `architecture/out-of-combat.md`.

## §434 — #397 live: the hidden encounter queue in the native OOC fallback is not shown to change wins (2026-10-11)

**Question:** when the V4 gates decline a card, shop, removal or campfire choice, the native fallback scores it with
the tracked floor/win trees on a rich row that holds the realized unrevealed `nextEliteId` and `nextFight0..2`;
`STS_FAIR=1` does not remove them (§371 left this live dependence untested). How much playing strength does that
hidden information carry on the current research base?
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/vwin_hidden_queue_live_397_20261011/PREREG.md), frozen at launch (share copy 21:46:21Z, first unit
21:46:17Z, about 54 s per seed; its "~21:55Z" line is wrong). Code main
`491bc21b`, Release binary `bab14cd5…`. Both arms are the §422 `off` environment (exact-10k fair Silver, V4 gates
margin 1.0, OOC MCTS off, `STS_REST_WIN=0`, keys off, act-3 stop); sole difference `STS_OOC_PUBLIC_FUTURES` 0
(legacy) vs 8 (public8: average over 8 public-history-conditioned encounter samples). Seeds 74015000–127, smoke
74015900, one 4-CPU cloud container. Primary: paired bootstrap 95% CI of Δwin (public8 − legacy); LEAK_HELPS if the
upper bound < 0, PUBLIC8_BETTER if the lower bound > 0, else LEAK_NOT_SHOWN.
**Validity:** 8/8 units rc=0, every seed once per arm; public scorer receipts `futures=8` on all 128 public8 seeds
(mean 23 scorer calls per run), none in legacy.
**Result:** **`LEAK_NOT_SHOWN`.** legacy 103/128 (80.5%), public8 104/128 (81.2%); Δwin +0.8 pp [−4.7, +6.3],
discordant 6 vs 5 (McNemar p = 1.0); Δfloor −0.18 [−1.13, +0.83]; 54.1 vs 53.2 s per run. 73/128 trajectories
diverged, but 112/128 seeds ended with the same outcome and floor. Deaths by act legacy 1/7/17, public8 0/10/14.
**Interpretation (Inference):** the hidden queue changes many fallback choices but no strength advantage is visible;
128 pairs cannot resolve effects below about ±8 pp (pre-registered); the observed CI still allows the leak to be
worth up to 4.7 pp. Public8 costs no measurable time. Baselines measured with the legacy fallback (e.g. the §422
`off` arm) are therefore not shown to be inflated by it, within that bound.
**Decision:** no default change in this entry. Making `STS_OOC_PUBLIC_FUTURES=8` the default (an
information-boundary correction, not a strength change) is Philipp's call.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/vwin_hidden_queue_live_397_20261011/README.md). Raw:
`/mnt/project-files/vwin-hidden-397/s434-raw.tar.gz`. Seeds 74015000–127 and 74015900 are now used.

**Knowledge impact:** one sentence each in the rich `v_win` information-boundary section of
`operations/ooc-label-pipeline.md`, the `STS_OOC_PUBLIC_FUTURES` row of `operations/environment-variables.md` and the

## §435 — Lizard Tail support in the default OOC MCTS CTM stack (2026-10-11)

**Question:** Philipp: "settle a lizard tail support for a0. Then we don't need the fallback." The default OOC MCTS
CTM stack (#418 pathb-r2) refuses imagined combats with an unused Lizard Tail plus a Fairy Potion
(`active_unqualified_lizard`: the correction steps aside at `fairy_potion_exact_boundary` and the ordinary CTM rejects
the active Tail) or plus Entropic Brew (`active_lizard_entropic_brew_unsupported`). Each refusal aborts the whole root
search and V4 decides; in §427–§430 these were 98–100% of the support aborts. §423 (A0) and §426 (A20) showed that the
§423 candidate fast artifact prices those states and removes the aborts (NOT_SHOWN on wins and regret).
**Change (no new model):** the §423 candidate becomes the default fast artifact of the automatic OOC MCTS stack:
`combat_transition_deepsets_pathb_r2_lizard.native` (`c6d56bbc…`, the #418 pathb-r2 tensors with `lizardFairy` and
`lizardBrew` in its header), pinned by a built-in copy of its manifest (`64da1776…`, byte-identical to
`candidate-v3-lizard.json`), as #418 did for pathb-r2. The #418 manifest (`d9d8377e…`) stays built in, so the #418 fast
artifact (`90806c25…`) still loads as `production` (rollback, reproduction of earlier runs); a load picks the built-in
manifest that lists the artifact's bytes. The §423 env (`arm_env.sh`, explicit model plus manifest) still loads the
same bytes, now reported as research candidate `pathb-r2` as before. OOC MCTS stays off by default (ADR-0027), so
default play is unchanged.
**Support census:** [packet](evidence/ooc_lizard_default_20261011/README.md). rollout3 at 256 simulations, A0, seeds
74011000–007, old (#418 stack, explicit) vs new (automatic default): support aborts 47 → 0 (Fairy + Tail 41 → 0,
Brew + Tail 6 → 0), V4 fallback 7.1% → 2.5%; the remaining 25 fallbacks per arm are `root_boundary`, not support
failures. 7/8 old runs hit a Lizard abort. Wins 7/8 vs 8/8 (descriptive only).
**Interpretation:** active Lizard Tail no longer forces a V4 fallback at A0 on the default stack. Mark of the Bloom +
Tail stays on its exact path (supported). This settles support, not strength: §423 found no win-rate gain from
pricing these states (−3.1 pp [−10.9, +4.7]) and §426 none on A20 regret. Other boundaries (`hp_envelope`,
Writhing Mass + Ritual Dagger) are unchanged (#369).
**Decision:** default OOC MCTS CTM stack switched; OOC MCTS remains off by default. Runs pinned to earlier commits are
unaffected; a run on this commit with the automatic stack now matches the §423 arm's CTM. Reproducing §422 or
§424–§430 on a later commit needs the explicit #418 settings (`STS_OOC_MCTS_COMBAT_MODEL=…pathb_r2.native`,
`STS_OOC_MCTS_BREW_FALLBACK_MODEL=…near_full_escape_pathb_r2.native`, `STS_OOC_MCTS_ACTIVE_LIZARD=1`). §433 also
measures the #418 model; a rollout3 promotion on that evidence that runs on this stack also adopts the Lizard model,
whose win-rate effect §423 left open (wide CI), so the promotion note must name the CTM.

**Evidence:** raw `/mnt/project-files/ooc-lizard-default-435/`. Seeds 74011000–74011007 are now used.

**Knowledge impact:** default stack in `architecture/out-of-combat.md` and `operations/environment-variables.md`; one
sentence in the rollout3 paragraph of `evaluation/current-research.md`.

## §441 — deep OOC MCTS with uniform prior and uniform leaf policy: worse than the V4-guided `combo`, ties plain rollout3 at lower CPU (2026-10-12)

**Question:** Philipp, 2026-10-12 08:51Z: "uniform prior and uniform leaf policy on 128 seeds with 4096 ooc simulations
on 8 workers". §433's `combo` uses V4 as the tree prior and as the policy between the rollout combats; how does it play
with both replaced by uniform choices?
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/ooc_uniform_441_20261012/PREREG.md). One arm, `uniform` = §433 `combo` (4096 simulations,
`WIDEN_K=4`, `WIDEN_ALPHA=0.75`, 3 rollout combats, native leaf, pathb-r2 CTM, flat exact-10k Silver) with
`STS_OOC_MCTS_PRIOR=uniform` and `STS_OOC_MCTS_LEAF_POLICY=uniform`, `STS_OOC_PUBLIC_FUTURES=0` pinned (as §433). Code
`b039e846` (main after #494), binary `8f5edf76…`. Seeds 76000000–127, paired with the §433 `combo`, `rollout3` and `off`
units: §433 `combo` seed 76000000 reproduces byte-identically on this binary (result row, decision, action and support
traces). 8 cloud workers × 16 seeds. Smokes 77009000–002. Primary: paired bootstrap 95% CI of uniform − combo (seed
441); BETTER / WORSE / NOT_SHOWN.
**Validity:** 128/128 units rc=0, no Silver stalls, config banners checked by grep, tar hashes checked.
**Result:** **WORSE.** uniform 109/128 (85.2%) vs combo 119/128 (93.0%): −7.8 pp [−15.6, −0.8], discordant 7 vs 17,
McNemar p = 0.064 (borderline); Δfloor −1.54 [−3.08, −0.15]; boss deaths 14 vs 4. Secondary: vs rollout3 (109/128)
0.0 pp [−8.6, +8.6]; vs off (96/128) +10.2 pp [0.0, +19.5], p = 0.06. MCTS CPU per run 376 s (combo 1,495, rollout3 811,
both on the pre-§436/§437 binary); V4 fallback 23.1%.
**Interpretation (Inference):** V4 guidance is worth wins at 4096 simulations; the run does not say whether the prior or
the leaf policy carries it. Without V4 the search is cheaper (the uniform leaf skips the native shop planner and V4
gates) and matches plain rollout3 at lower cost (**Inference** across binaries: 376 s on this binary vs 811 s for rollout3 on the pre-§436/§437 binary; the gate seed ran 0.71x and §437 reports 1.13–1.7x for rollout3, so on equal binaries uniform likely costs about 0.5–0.8x of rollout3). `combo` did better on this half of the §433 cohort (93.0%) than on all 256 seeds (87.5%).
**Decision:** no default change.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/ooc_uniform_441_20261012/README.md). Raw: `/mnt/project-files/ooc-uniform-441/`
(one tar per worker). Seeds 77009000–002 are now used; 76000000–127 reused on purpose.

## §443 — Production CTM at A20 (Stage 0) and the out-of-combat policy for an A20 corpus (G0) (2026-10-12)

**Question:** Philipp: "Can we do the same for A20 ctm?" The production CTM (pathb-r2, A0 Path B only) gets
`ascension` straight from the game (`combat_predictor_input.cpp`). §416 saw it predict death 0 at ASC 20. Stage 0 of
the A20 CTM plan (`/mnt/project-files/ctm-a20/PLAN.md`, rules written before the run) asks whether clamping the input
to 0 is enough, or whether an A20 corpus and retrain are needed. G0 asks whether the Path B generator reaches later
acts at A20.
**Setup:** [packet](evidence/ctm_a20_stage0_20261012/README.md). Stage 0: main `fcd253f1`, learned-stop Path B
teacher, `combattransitiongen 10000 20` on seeds 78100000–78100999 (1000/1000 completed, 9,351 rows, about 5.4
CPU-s and 9.35 rows per seed). Every row was scored by production `ctmscorerows` as generated and with ascension set
to 0, against the observed Silver outcome (death = outcome 2); 9,349 scored, 2 refused
(`writhing_ritual_intersection`).

| rows | n | observed death | ASC 20 predicted | clamped predicted | clamped survival NLL | clamped win-HP bias / MAE |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all | 9,349 | 0.105 | 0.005 | 0.031 | 0.268 | +4.8 / 7.2 |
| normal | 6,104 | 0.023 | 0.004 | 0.006 | 0.079 | +3.6 / 5.3 |
| elite | 2,431 | 0.191 | 0.007 | 0.046 | 0.548 | +9.3 / 12.6 |
| boss | 724 | 0.493 | 0.005 | 0.191 | 0.894 | +0.1 / 10.5 |

Death bias (predicted − observed), source-seed bootstrap 95% CI: ASC 20 as given [−0.104, −0.096] (win-HP bias
+15.4, survival NLL 1.447); clamped [−0.078, −0.070].
**Stage 0 decision (rule: clamp is enough only if |bias| ≤ 0.01 overall and on elites and bosses, and HP bias within
±3): FAILS.** Clamping underestimates death about 3.4x overall (4x on elites, 2.6x on bosses) and overestimates win HP
by about 5. An A20-trained CTM is needed for A20 OOC MCTS. **Inference:** A20 OOC MCTS runs so far (§425, §426) priced
imagined combats with a model that sees almost no death risk.
**G0 (rule: switch the generator's out-of-combat policy if acts 2–3 hold under 25% of rows): FAILS** at 19.7%
(act 1/2/3: 7,505 / 1,538 / 306 rows); the copied Path B map/reward chain dies early at A20.
**Change:** opt-in `STS_CTM_GEN_DEPLOYED_OOC=1` for `combattransitiongen` plays every non-battle screen with
`deployedOocPolicyStep` (§431) instead of the copied chain; off by default, refused in the Lizard candidate mode, recorded as
`oocPolicy` in the manifest. With the flag on, the teacher must pin the effective OOC policy (`ooc_policy`: gate
flags, margins, V4 net sha256, public futures) and the manifest records it as `policy`. With the flag off, the generator reproduces the Stage 0 rows for seeds
78100000–78100002 exactly (31 rows, only `teacherId` differs).
**G0 smoke** (commit `c67ba2db`, flag on with the deployed V4 settings, seeds 78009004–78009043): 40/40 completed,
695 rows (17.4 per seed), act 1/2/3 357 / 213 / 125 (acts 2–3 49%), 76 boss rows, last floor median 33 (8–51), about
10.6 CPU-s per seed (0.61 s per row, vs 0.58 with the old chain). Descriptive only.
**Decision:** an A20 corpus uses the deployed step. At 17.4 rows per seed, a corpus the size of the A0 union (537k
rows) is about 31k seeds and about 92 CPU-h (Inference, from 40 seeds). Stage 1 (corpus) needs Philipp's worker count.
No default play changes.

**Evidence:** raw `/mnt/project-files/ctm-a20/`. Seeds used: 78009000–78009043 (smokes), 78100000–78100999.

**Knowledge impact:** new generator variable in `operations/environment-variables.md`; the A20 limit of the production
CTM is recorded here (current understanding unchanged otherwise, since OOC MCTS is off by default).

## §444 — X2-B without the hidden next-fight fields: the E1 public arm exported as a native win model (2026-10-12)

**Question:** Philipp wants X2-B to replace `v_win` (via `STS_WIN_NET`) as the rollout3 leaf, but X2-B reads
the four HIDDEN_FUTURE fields `nextEliteId` and `nextFight0..2` (§371, §438). Is there a public-information X2-B,
and does it run natively with the same values as in Python?

**Design:** offline, no game seeds, no retraining, TEST closed. No new model was fitted: E1 (§394) arm P0 is
exactly the X2-B recipe on the 457 public features (X2-B's 461 minus the four hidden fields; the 12 forward-map
columns and the public queue counters stay), seeds 0/1/2, on the frozen 1,024-source #334 corpus
(`ae56f963…`), unchanged 696/155 TRAIN/VALIDATION split. The three checkpoints (all 21 E1 `SHA256SUMS`
entries verified) were exported as one margin-averaged CompactTreeNet with `tools/vwin_export_ensemble.py`
(the §396 F2 route). A forward-map variant is not separate: X2-B and P0 already contain the map block.

**Result:** `models/candidates/v_win_x2b_public_trees.txt` (sha256 `e2d3aa65…ca90`, 1,006 trees, 428 used
features, no hidden field). Native `winnettest` parity on the §379 selection (1,780 rows): max |native − Python|
**2.46e-7** (gate < 1e-5, pass); explicit `STS_WIN_NET` load passes `oocmctsconfigselftest`. VALIDATION (141,566
MAP rows, 155 sources):

| Model | NLL | Brier | AUC |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| this file (margin mean) | 0.42362 | 0.13850 | 0.7919 |
| P0 probability mean (E1) | 0.42370 | 0.13848 | 0.7918 |
| frozen X2-B (461) | 0.42261 | 0.13777 | 0.7907 |

Paired ΔNLL vs X2-B, source-clustered bootstrap: **+0.0010 [−0.0041, +0.0058]** (reproduces E1's −0.0011 with
the sign flipped); vs the P0 probability mean −0.00008 [−0.00031, +0.00018].

**Verdict:** `PUBLIC_X2B_READY` as an engineering candidate. Dropping the hidden fields costs no resolvable
held-out accuracy (consistent with §371, §394, §438). No gameplay effect is claimed. No default changes: the
default `models/v_win_trees.txt` and the pinned `models/candidates/v_win_x2b_trees.txt` (anchor of the
`screengbm` leaf and its residual GBM) are untouched. The new file is opt-in through `STS_WIN_NET` or
`STS_OOC_MCTS_LEAF_WIN_MODEL`. A rollout3 A/B with it as the leaf needs Philipp's go.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/vwin_x2b_public_444_20261012/README.md) (local run on Philipp's machine; bulky
parity CSV under `~/Documents/sts/artifacts/vwin-refresh-334/x2b-public-444-20261012/`).

**Knowledge impact:** candidate listed in `operations/environment-variables.md` (`STS_OOC_MCTS_LEAF_WIN_MODEL`).

## §445 — A20 short-branch label corpus (53.5k decisions): learned OOC models beat the heuristic but are not shown better than V4; more labels barely help (2026-10-12)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-11 20:59Z "Label run", 21:20Z "8 hours per worker"):** do short-branch labels with independent futures (§432), generated at scale on fresh A20 seeds, train an OOC model that picks better than the deployed V4?
**Design:** 25 cloud workers, 8 h each. Brief and per-worker setup are in the packet. Frozen main `07a93e36`, Release `one_combat` sha256 `ea307e30…`. The commit and binary hash are self-reported by the workers (the provenance JSONs carry an empty git sha and no binary or tree hashes); the recorded config is identical across all 534 seeds.
- Labels: `strategicgen2` ASC 20, Silver 2k with the natpert prior (weight 400), `STRATEGIC_SAMPLE_ALL=1`, `STRATEGIC_BRANCH_FIGHTS=3`, `FUTURES=8`, `RESEED=1`, `BRANCH_SIMS=2000`.
- Bootstrap trees: A0 (`labelFloor`) and A20 full-data trees `v_{rich,win}_a20_full` (sha256 `d8ab1349…` / `6f5fbfd0…`; 157k `strategicgen` v1 runs; held-out floor R² 0.509, win AUC 0.851) via `STS_CF_ALT_BOOT_*` (`labelFloorAlt`).
- Seeds: 75000000+10000*W+k; smoke 75009000-75009001. Per-seed timeout 4 h.
- Corpus: 534 finished seeds, 252,015 rows, 53,535 labelled decisions, 42,137 with ≥2 options. 83 seeds were cut by the timeout or the 8 h stop and are excluded; this drops the longest runs, so late-run decisions are under-represented. 75110003 crashed with the Silver depth bound.
- Training target: the A20 floor-tree label, with an 80/20 run-grouped split (428/106 seeds).
- Models:
  - (a) V4 Q-head warm-started from the deployed checkpoint, absolute floor target (`STRAT_Q_ONLY=1`).
  - (b) Same as (a) with `STRAT_Q_TARGET=fallback_centered`.
  - (c) Full network with the centered target.
  - (d) XGBoost on 1,015 strategic-row columns: all except label/meta columns and 10 encounter or chance fields (`nextEliteId`, `nextFight0-2`, `remElites`, `remFights`, `monOffset`, `eliteOffset`, `potionChance`, `cardRarityFactor`). Regression on the within-decision centered label.
  - (e) Same features as (d), `rank:pairwise` on within-decision ranks.
- Scoring: the §432 Gold2 set (16 independent futures, 260 seeds), mean floor regret on the 397 decisions every picker covers, paired decision bootstrap (10,000 samples).

**Result (Gold2 regret in floors; heuristic minus picker):**

| Picker | Regret | Heuristic − picker |
|---|---|---|
| SB labels themselves, A20 floor trees (§432) | 1.25 | +1.01 [+0.56, +1.52] |
| (d) GBM, centered regression | 1.73 | +0.53 [+0.25, +0.84] |
| (e) GBM, pairwise ranking | 1.76 | +0.50 [+0.18, +0.87] |
| (c) V4 full net, centered | 1.86 | +0.40 [+0.03, +0.81] |
| (b) V4 Q-head, centered | 1.96 | +0.30 [−0.04, +0.67] |
| (a) V4 Q-head, absolute | 1.98 | +0.28 [−0.06, +0.66] |
| deployed V4 | 1.98 | +0.28 [−0.09, +0.68] |
| heuristic (path-blind, §425) | 2.26 | 0 |

- V4 minus GBM (d): +0.25 [−0.20, +0.69]; V4 minus (e): +0.22 [−0.18, +0.64]. Not shown.
- The absolute-target Q-head does not learn the ranking: on held-out SB labels its strict Q top-1 stays at 0.33, versus 0.36 with the centered target.
- Learning curve for (d), trained on 25 / 50 / 100% of the training seeds: held-out SB regret 1.19 / 1.14 / 1.10; Gold2 regret 1.77 / 1.71 / 1.72 (406 decisions).
- Side result: refitting the A20 floor/win trees with the 12 forward-map columns and without the 4 hidden futures (§438) on the same 157k runs and split gives floor RMSE 9.82 vs 9.90 (R² 0.517 vs 0.509). Win is unchanged (AUC 0.851, log loss 0.1440 vs 0.1439).

**Interpretation (Inference):** the labels rank options well (1.25), but models that see only the pre-decision state and the action ids recover about half of that gain over the heuristic (GBM 0.53 of 1.01 floors). More labels give small held-out gains (held-out regret 1.19 / 1.14 / 1.10 at 25 / 50 / 100%) that Gold2 cannot resolve (25% vs 100%: +0.05 [−0.09, +0.20]) (Inference). Held-out label regrets use the split that picked early stopping, so they are slightly optimistic; Gold2 is unaffected. A learned A20 OOC policy from these labels is not shown better than V4 offline. A live test was not run. **Open question:** whether scoring options online with short branches (the label procedure itself, about 45 s per decision on one core) is worth its cost at chosen decision types.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/a20_sb_labels_20261012/README.md). Raw data: `/mnt/project-files/v4-a20-retrain/sblabels-w{0..24}.tar.gz` (sha256s in the packet). Seeds 75000000–75249999 (block reserved; used k < 1000 per worker) and smoke 75009000–75009001 are now used.

**Knowledge impact:** one paragraph in `evaluation/current-research.md`.

## §446 — rollout5 with the Lizard-capable CTM: no more V4 fallback, not shown better than rollout3 (2026-10-12)

**Question:** Philipp: "can we try again with the lizard capable ctm? on 8 workers on the same 128 seeds?" §430 rollout5
(`LEAF_COMBATS=5`) won 112/128 vs rollout3 115/128 on the #418 CTM but fell back to V4 on 37% of decisions, almost all
Lizard Tail support aborts. With the Lizard-capable `pathb_r2_lizard` CTM (§423, §435), does rollout5 win more than
rollout3 with the same CTM?

`STS_OOC_MCTS_LEAF_COMBATS=5`; control `lizard` = the §423 environment rerun on the same commit; both pin
`STS_OOC_PUBLIC_FUTURES=0`. Run commit `b6d00dd0` (code `3b06c924`, main after #496), binary `10dc2616…`, seeds
70000000–127, 16 cloud workers (8 per arm; Philipp chose the control arm on a decision card). Launch gate: §423 seed
70000000 diverged at OOC decision 8 on this commit; a bisect found `c7641b07` (#480, Face of Cleric now fires after
event fights), a simulator rule fix ([note](evidence/ooc_rollout5_lizard_20261012/RERUN-423-70000000.md)), hence the
same-commit control. Smokes 80009000–001. Primary: paired bootstrap 95% CI of `r5liz` − same-commit `lizard`;
IMPROVED / WORSE / NOT_SHOWN.
**Validity:** `lizard` 128/128 rc=0; `r5liz` 127/128, seed 70000087 a listed Silver stall (dropped from all pairs as
pre-registered); tar hashes, banners and old-control hashes checked.
**Result:** **NOT_SHOWN.** 113/127 (89.0%) vs 111/127 (87.4%), +1.6 pp [−4.7, +8.7], discordant 10 vs 8, p = 0.81.
Boss deaths 8 vs 13; Δfloor +0.13 [−0.70, +0.94]. V4 fallback 2.9% vs 2.4% (§430: 37.1%). 887 vs 592 s per run.
Cross-commit (descriptive): vs §430 r5 +1.6 pp, vs §422 rollout3 −1.6 pp, vs §422 off +10.2 pp [+1.6, +18.9].

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/ooc_rollout5_lizard_20261012/README.md). Raw: `/mnt/project-files/ooc-rollout5-lizard-446/`
