**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-12 10:54Z "Live test", 11:30Z "Run it"):** does the §445 A20 GBM ranker, best learned picker on the Gold2 set (1.73 floors regret vs V4 1.98, heuristic 2.26), win more floors than the current A20 stack when it plays every out-of-combat decision?
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/a20_gbm_ranker_20261012/PREREG.md), pushed before the run (`77c85b52`, renumbered `ef5af7c7`). Code `5cb1e86d`, Release `one_combat` sha256 `752e1e76…`. Model `models/candidates/ooc_gbm_ranker_a20_sbl.txt` (sha256 `372431c1…`, 1,157 trees). Both arms: the §419 stack (`silver_learned_stop/live_env.sh` V4 gates, learned stop, keys off, `STS_STOP_AFTER_ACT=3`), `bestbench 10000 128 20 79000000`. Treatment adds `STS_OOC_GBM_RANKER`, which takes every real OOC decision with ≥ 2 candidates after the chest, reward-relic and Match and Keep rules. Primary: mean paired floor difference with a 95% paired bootstrap CI (10,000 reps, RNG 20261012).
**Parity:** on 628 live decisions of 8 smoke seeds the C++ scores match xgboost within 4.2e-6 and the argmax agrees everywhere.

**Result:**

| Arm | Wins | Mean floor | Reached Act 3 | Deaths Act 1 / 2 / 3 | s per run |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Current stack (C) | 16/128 | 35.09 | 59 | 23 / 46 / 43 | 14.2 |
| GBM ranker (T) | 3/128 | 32.88 | 43 | 13 / 72 / 40 | 10.7 |

- Floor T − C: −2.21 [−5.29, +0.80]. Verdict by the pre-registered rule: `NOT_SHOWN`. Play differs on 118 of 128 seeds.
- Wins (secondary, not pre-registered as a decision rule): T − C −10.2 pp [−16.4, −3.9]. Discordant pairs 16 C-only vs 3 T-only, exact binomial p = 0.004.

**Interpretation (Inference):** the ranker survives Act 1 more often but loses far more runs in Act 2 and almost never wins. A one-step argmax over Gold2-style short-branch labels (three fights, then a value-tree bootstrap) does not price long-horizon run strength, and Gold2 regret on single decisions did not predict play over a whole run. The live result is worse than the offline ranking suggested; the GBM should not replace the V4 gates or the heuristic.
**Decision:** no default change. `STS_OOC_GBM_RANKER` stays off. Seeds 79000000–79000127 and smokes 79009000–79009008 are now used.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/a20_gbm_ranker_20261012/) (PREREG, parity check, smoke, `run.sh`, `analyze.py`, both result CSVs with bestbench sidecars, `result.txt`).

**Knowledge impact:** this entry, its `EXPERIMENTS.md` index line and one sentence in `evaluation/current-research.md`; `STS_OOC_GBM_RANKER` is documented in `operations/environment-variables.md`.

## §442 — Native shop planner and floor-model cost in rollout3: packed trees and column candidates, bitwise identical, 1.13–1.19x per rollout3 run (2026-10-12)

**Question:** after §437, how much rollout3 CPU do the native shop planner and the other floor-model tree calls in
leaf rollouts take, with the V4 and with a uniform rollout policy, and can they be made faster with bit-identical
play?
**Design:** performance only. Baseline `main` `b039e846` (Release `8f5edf76…`). §422 `rollout3` and `off` arms
unchanged, plus one uniform-prior, uniform-leaf rollout3 unit; seeds 74024000–74024004, one guarded one-seed
`bestbench` per unit; `gprofng` on 74024000 (V4 leaf) and 74024001 (uniform leaf); an offline replay of every 61st
tree call from rollout3 74024002. Parity = byte-identical decision and MCTS action traces and identical non-timing
result and MCTS summary rows (§437's `compare.py`).
**Profile (baseline):** V4 leaf, 546 s process CPU: floor/`v_win` tree evaluation 110 s (20%; `nativeShopPlan`
45.7 s, card-reward pick 51.1 s, removal pick 6.1 s inclusive), V4 shop gate 39.7 s. About 365,000 floor-model calls
per run, 80% one-change rankings with a median of 4 rows, 20% shop subset enumerations with 66 rows on average;
each call walked all 1,256 trees, so small calls were bound by the per-tree walk. Uniform leaf, 332 s: trees 8%, of
which the batched floor-model calls are only 8.0 s.
**Change:** `CompactTreeNet` keeps a packed copy of its trees (8-byte nodes, preorder with the yes child next to
its parent) for `predict()` and a new batched `predictDeltas()`, which takes candidates as their values at the
varying features only and follows the base path until the first varying split. The shop plan, card pick and
removal pick pass column values instead of full 1,017-float rows; the shop plan values all subsets in one call and
skips ranking removal targets when the removal is unaffordable (no candidate could include it).
**Result:** 11/11 units identical across the three builds (final build: rollout3 74024002–003, uniform leaf
74024001, `off` 74024004). Replay: 118,385 rows identical, about 1.9x faster than §437. Tree CPU 110 → 51 s on
74024000. Per-run time: rollout3 1.19x and 1.13x (paired), 1.15x (both profiled); uniform leaf 1.04x; `off` 1.00x.
**Decision:** adopt (exact, no behavior change). After this the largest rollout3 costs are the V4 network in the
rollout gates (`prepareState` 20%; the shop gate now costs more than the shop plan) and the CTM (§439).

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/shop_planner_speedup_20261012/README.md). Raw:
`/mnt/project-files/shop-planner-442/raw.tar.gz`. Seeds 74024000–74024004 are now used.

**Knowledge impact:** `predictDeltas` paragraph and tree-storage item in `architecture/out-of-combat.md`, compact
tree row in `CODE_MAP.md`, rollout3 cost sentence in `evaluation/current-research.md`.

## §450 — V4 token network in rollout3: cached deck tokens and transposed layers, bitwise identical, 1.29–1.41x per rollout3 run (2026-10-12)

**Question:** after §442 the V4 token network in the rollout gates was the largest rollout3 cost; can its forward
pass be made faster with bitwise-identical outputs?
**Design:** performance only. Baseline `main` `94f78fbb` (after #497). §422 `rollout3` and `off` arms unchanged, plus
one uniform-prior, uniform-leaf rollout3 unit; seeds 74024005–74024009, one guarded one-seed `bestbench` per unit;
`gprofng` on rollout3 74024005. Parity = §437's `compare.py`.
**Profile (before):** 450 s process CPU: V4 `prepareState` 95.9 s inclusive (21%; deck encoder 52.4 s), card-reward
V4 gate 78.3 s inclusive, V4 shop gate 29.6 s; GELU `tanhf` 64.3 s.
**Change:** `OocStrategicTokNet::load()` builds derived tables: every deck token (card × upgrade × count 0–9) with
its qkv row (about 3.8 MB) and transposed copies of the dense layers, which compute several output units side by
side in each unit's original float order. `prepareState` also keeps the Q head's first-layer sum over the state
inputs, as `PolicyPrefix` does for the policy head. Nets filled in directly keep the original loops.
**Result:** new `ooc_tok_net_fast` test (400 states, 2,400 actions on the deployed model) bitwise equal; three hand
mutations fail it. Full runs identical: rollout3 74024005–007, uniform leaf 74024009, `off` 74024008. Per-run
time: rollout3 1.41x and 1.29x; uniform leaf 0.98x and `off` 1.02x (noise). Profiled: `prepareState` 95.9 → 34.1 s,
card-reward gate 78.3 → 27.1 s, shop gate 29.6 → 11.3 s.
**Decision:** adopt (exact, no behavior change). The per-action V4 encoders and GELU are now the largest V4 costs.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/v4_net_speedup_20261012/README.md). Raw:
`/mnt/project-files/v4-speedup-450/raw.tar.gz`. Seeds 74024005–74024009 are now used.

**Knowledge impact:** derived-table paragraph in `architecture/out-of-combat.md`, rollout3 cost sentence in
`evaluation/current-research.md`.

## §448 — A20 V4 at A0 with V4 deciding everything, a V4 margin sweep, and where V4 and OOC MCTS beat the heuristic on the gold decisions (2026-10-12)

**Question (Philipp):** play 128 A0 seeds with the A20-trained V4, no OOC search, no fallback to the heuristic;
then sweep the gate margin; then show on the gold decisions where V4 (and OOC MCTS) choose better or worse than
the heuristic. Descriptive, not pre-registered.
**Design:** [evidence packet](evidence/a20_v4_margin_sweep_20261012/README.md). Main `4a407a0c`, binary `f085352b`.
A20 V4 = §419 round 1 + 2 Q-head retrain `v4_a20_r12.native` (`08d239f9`); A0 V4 = deployed (`e62abd83`).
§422 `off` base with every V4 gate on **including the map gate** (not part of the default stack); margin =
required Q gap between V4's best and second-best option. Seeds 81000000–127 (A0), paired across all arms;
smoke 81009000.

**Coverage at margin 0:** V4 made every gated decision; only non-upgrade card selections (shop removal, Living
Wall, Drug Dealer, Duplicator, Transmogrifier, Cleric, Library, Astrolabe, bottled relics; 132 in 128 runs) went
to the heuristic; free rewards, chest opening, the reward-relic rule and the forced boss node stay rules.

**Result (wins of 128):**

| margin | 0 | 0.25 | 0.5 | 1 | 2 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A20 V4 | 55 | 64 | 83 | 94 | 98 | 90 |
| A0 V4 | 70 | 76 | 78 | 78 | 96 | 98 |

Heuristic only (margin 1e6): 86. Best arms vs heuristic only: A20 margin 2 and A0 margin 4, both +9.4 pp
[+0.8, +18.0]. A20 − A0 at equal margin: −11.7 pp [−21.9, −1.6] at 0, +12.5 pp [+1.6, +23.4] at 1, within
±10 pp elsewhere (13 arms; no multiplicity correction). At margin 0, 3 (A20) and 4 (A0) runs died outside
combat (Knowing Skull HP payments). The A20 margin-0 sweep arm reproduced the single-container first run on all
128 seeds. A0 V4 at margin 1 with the map gate (78/128) is below the usual default-stack rate without it
(§422 off 101/128, §433 199/256, other seeds).

**Gold decisions (Gold2, §432; A20; floors per decision, label of the picked option minus the heuristic's):**
A0 V4 +0.28 [−0.09, +0.67] over 397 decisions (no chest/relic rules applied): events +2.60 (Neow: heuristic option 3 vs V4 option 1, about +14
floors on 6 decisions), shop +1.17, rest vs smith +0.62, rewards screen +0.01 (214), map −0.24, upgrade target −0.54.
V4 overrides gained reliably only when V4's Q for its pick exceeded its Q for the heuristic's pick by ≥ 2. §419 retrains:
+0.42 (G2) and +0.32 (G3), better on map, worse on upgrade and treasure. §425 OOC MCTS picks on the same labels
(387 decisions, with the chest and reward-relic rules applied as in live play): `prod` +0.49 [+0.12, +0.87],
`rollout3` +0.41 [+0.16, +0.70], A0 V4 +0.31 [−0.05, +0.71] on the same basis; both MCTS arms gain on events and map, rewards screen ≈ 0.

**Interpretation (Inference):** the gate margin, not the training ascension, decides how V4 plays at A0: both V4s
lose many runs when every argmax is played and peak at margin 2–4; the A20 retrain is not consistently better at A0. Gold
single-decision gains (largest at small margins and on events) do not predict whole-run wins (as in §447; `prod`
MCTS is also positive on gold but −21.9 pp live, §384). The map gate may cost wins at margin 1 (Inference; no
same-seed map-off arm was run).
**Decision:** no default change.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/a20_v4_margin_sweep_20261012/README.md). Raw: `/mnt/project-files/a20-v4-at-a0-448/`.
Seeds 81000000–127 and 81009000 are now used.

**Knowledge impact:** one paragraph in `evaluation/current-research.md`.

## §452 — Silver prior inside the search tree: fight score up at 2k sims, not CPU-matched (2026-10-12)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-12):** the v1 Silver prior (§397, §406) acts only at the search root
(`SilverSearcher::evaluateEdge` applies the bonus only when `&parent == root`). If the same prior also
guides nodes below the root, does a 2k search play fights better than plain 2k? This is the precondition
for an AlphaZero-style loop: prior-guided search must be a stronger teacher than plain search.
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/silver_tree_prior_20261012/PREREG.md), frozen after independent review
(PASS at `655aa915`; code `17ddaa67`, binary `704b81d9…`). Research-only `SilverSearcher::nodePrior`:
a non-root decision node with at least K simulations is scored once by the v1 prior, its visited edges
get `400 · P / (n + 1)`, and untried edges (root included) are tried in prior order. `ctmsilvergen` with
`STS_CTMSILVER_ARMSET=treeprior452`: an exact-10k plain source run per seed (production V4 OOC policy,
A0, project-fair), every fight replayed by a 10k control (must reproduce the source) and by four arms at
2k, 2 replicates each, with combat RNG redrawn per (fight, replicate) identically for all arms: `plain2k`,
`root2k` (§406), `tree8_2k` (K = 8), `tree1_2k` (K = 1). Seeds 84000000–84000127, 16 cloud workers × 4
cores. Metric: fight score 0 on death, else 53 + HP + 11·potions + 0.25·gold + 2·maxHP; paired per fight,
95% CI by bootstrap over source seeds. Primary: `tree8_2k − plain2k`.
**Result: `TREE_PRIOR_HELPS`.** 3,361 of 3,372 fights valid (the 11 control mismatches are Smoke Bomb
escapes, quarantined).

| contrast (score, all fights) | Δ [95% CI] | boss (n = 368) | elite (n = 817) |
|---|---|---|---|
| tree8 − plain2k (primary) | +1.17 [+0.53, +1.79] | +6.15 [+0.79, +11.33] | +1.41 [+0.67, +2.24] |
| root2k − plain2k | +0.63 [+0.18, +1.12] | +5.58 [+1.25, +10.07] | −0.20 [−0.88, +0.39] |
| tree8 − root2k | +0.54 [+0.01, +1.05] | +0.58 [−3.25, +4.66] | +1.61 [+0.74, +2.67] |
| tree1 − plain2k | +1.67 [+1.15, +2.22] | +8.84 [+4.35, +13.49] | +1.55 [+0.74, +2.42] |
| tree1 − tree8 | +0.50 [+0.12, +0.90] | +2.69 [−0.50, +5.87] | +0.14 [−0.27, +0.54] |

- Death rate per fight: plain 0.64%, root 0.57%, tree8 0.51%, tree1 0.45% (tree1 − plain −0.17 pp
  [−0.30, −0.01]; boss −1.5 pp [−2.8, −0.3]).
- Where the score comes from (descriptive): mostly potions kept (11·potions: plain 18.27, tree8 19.06,
  tree1 19.11 per fight) and fewer deaths; end HP is nearly unchanged (73.37 / 73.40 / 73.66).
- CPU per fight (thread CPU, 4 runs per worker): plain 0.37 s, root 0.39 s, tree8 1.09 s (2.9x),
  tree1 4.09 s (11x); 10k control 2.02 s.

**Interpretation:**
- The prior does guide the search usefully below the root: at equal simulations, K = 8 beats plain and the
  root-only prior, and K = 1 beats K = 8. Part of `tree8 − root2k` is the root's untried-action order,
  which `root2k` does not change.
- **Not CPU-matched.** tree8 costs 2.9x and tree1 11x plain 2k per fight. No plain arm at matched CPU
  (about 6k for tree8) was run, and §406 found plain 2k ≈ plain 10k in win rate. **Open question:** does
  tree8 beat plain search at equal CPU? Until that is shown, this does not prove a stronger teacher per
  unit of compute.
- The effect is small in absolute terms: about one fight-score point per fight (≈ 0.07 potions kept and
  0.1–0.2 pp fewer deaths); win-rate impact is **Unverified**.
- Per the pre-registered rule the next step is an iteration-1 loop design and a run-level confirmation;
  a CPU-matched fight-level check is the cheaper first step (Inference).

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/silver_tree_prior_20261012/README.md). Seeds 84000000–84000127 (run) and
84009000–84009001 (smoke) are now used; reviewer seeds 74035000–74035004.

**Knowledge impact:** tree-prior paragraph in `architecture/combat-search.md`.

## §453 — Silver tree prior vs plain Silver at matched CPU: not shown (2026-10-12)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-12, "Run check"):** §452 found the in-tree v1 prior (K = 8) better than plain
2k at equal simulations, at 2.9x the CPU. Does it still beat plain Silver given the same CPU? Only then is
prior-guided search a stronger teacher per unit of compute, which an AlphaZero-style loop needs.
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/silver_cpumatch_20261012/PREREG.md), frozen after independent review
(PASS at run commit `94110b53`; code `9b74de14`, binary `d459a654…`). Same harness, sources, pairing and
metric as §452, with `STS_CTMSILVER_ARMSET=cpumatch453`: arms `plain2k`, `tree8_2k` (K = 8, w = 400) and
`plain6k`, 2 replicates each, combat RNG redrawn per (fight, replicate) identically for all arms. Fresh
seeds 84000200–84000327, 16 cloud workers × 4 cores. Primary: `tree8_2k − plain6k`, all fights, score.
**Result: `NOT_SHOWN`.** 3,325 of 3,345 fights valid; the 20 excluded are escape states (the 17 control
mismatches are Smoke Bomb escapes with an invalid source, the rest escape-quarantined arm rows).

| contrast (score) | all (n = 3,325) | boss (n = 368) | elite (n = 818) |
|---|---|---|---|
| tree8 − plain6k (primary) | +0.46 [−0.02, +0.97] | +3.88 [+0.38, +7.69] | +0.10 [−0.85, +1.20] |
| tree8 − plain2k (§452 replication) | +1.84 [+1.40, +2.30] | +11.41 [+7.76, +15.25] | +1.39 [+0.37, +2.45] |
| plain6k − plain2k | +1.38 [+0.94, +1.82] | +7.53 [+4.28, +10.86] | +1.29 [+0.51, +2.10] |

- CPU per fight (thread CPU): plain2k 0.41 s, tree8 1.17 s, plain6k 1.30 s (tree8 / plain6k = 0.90,
  within the pre-registered 20%); 10k control 2.21 s.
- Death rate per fight: plain2k 0.84%, plain6k 0.71%, tree8 0.54% (tree8 − plain6k −0.2 pp
  [−0.3, −0.0]; boss −1.4 pp [−2.6, −0.3]).

**Interpretation:**
- §452 replicates on fresh seeds (tree8 − plain2k +1.84, larger than §452's +1.17).
- Most of that gain is what the same CPU buys plain search: plain 6k recovers about three quarters of it
  (+1.38). The rest, +0.46, has a CI that just touches zero, so by the pre-registered rule the prior is
  not shown to beat plain search at matched CPU, and no loop design follows.
- The leftover points the same way as before: fewer deaths, concentrated in boss fights (boss +3.88,
  CI above zero; a secondary subset, not the decision). **Inference:** if the prior's per-node cost
  fell, the same search could beat plain at matched CPU; whether profiling can make that happen is §454.
- Contrary to §406's win-rate result (plain 2k ≈ plain 10k), more plain sims still raise the fight score
  from 2k to 6k, mostly in boss fights. Win-rate impact is **Unverified**.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/silver_cpumatch_20261012/README.md). Seeds 84000200–84000327 (run) and
84009002 (smoke) are now used.

**Knowledge impact:** one sentence in the tree-prior paragraph of `architecture/combat-search.md`.

## §454 — Silver tree prior cost: batched exact prior scoring, bitwise identical, K = 8 from 2.7x to 1.7x of plain 2k (2026-10-13)

**Question:** §452's tree prior (K = 8) cost 2.9x the CPU of plain 2k per fight. Where does the overhead go, and how
much can be removed without changing search results?
**Design:** performance only. Baseline `main` `33d03b25` (#508 head; rebased on merge `93011ed1`, no Silver code
change). Native Silver 2k with the §452 environment (`env.sh`, prior `prior-natpert.compact.txt`, weight 400),
`ctmsilvergen` with `STS_CTMSILVER_ARMSET=treeprior452k8` (seed 74038000) and `treeprior452` (74038001–74038002),
R = 1, one guarded one-seed run per binary; old and new binaries ran side by side on the same 4-core machine.
Parity: `arms.csv` and `states.csv` without CPU columns, `samples.csv` whole. Profile: `gprof` (-O3, no LTO)
with one arm at a time, and walk-step counters in a throwaway build.
**Profile (before):** tree8 65 ms vs plain 28 ms per 2k decision. Almost all of the difference is the prior: at
K = 8 about 74 nodes per decision are scored, 5.6 distinct edges each, every edge walking all 1,997 trees
(depth about 9.5, 23% of splits on the 22 action features; 53% of trees reach a leaf on state features alone).
Search-shape effects (copies, node creation, rollouts) were below 1 s of the 14 s extra in the profile.
**Change:** `CombatValueNet::predictPolicyActions` scores all edges of one state: `load()` keeps a compact copy of
a policy tree ensemble (8-byte nodes, siblings adjacent, canonical feature indices), each tree's state-only prefix
is walked once per state, and the edges then finish that tree in lockstep. Per-edge sums keep `predictVec`'s tree
order, so scores are bit for bit equal. `nativeSilverPolicyPrior` extracts the state once and scores edges with
bit-identical action features once. Ensembles whose children do not follow their parents keep `predictVec`.
Tried and dropped: walking blocks of 8 trees in lockstep (slower than per-tree lockstep).
**Result:** new `silver_searcher` checks (batched equals `predictVec` on a mixed state/action fixture and on the
fallback) pass; three hand mutations fail them. All three seeds identical in every non-CPU field, including on the
rebased binary. CPU per decision relative to plain 2k in the same run
([timing.csv](evidence/silver_tree_prior_speedup_20261013/timing.csv)):

| arm | 74038001–002 before (57 fights) | after | 74038000 before (27 fights, 2 runs) | after (3 runs) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| tree8_2k | 2.73x | 1.67x | 2.35x, 2.44x | 1.57x–1.61x |
| tree1_2k | 10.5x | 4.8x | — | — |
| root2k | 1.01x | 1.01x | 0.99x–1.01x | 0.96x–0.97x |

The ratio varies by seed (74038001: tree8 3.69x → 2.10x); about 55–60% of the extra cost over plain 2k is removed for both K.

**Decision:** adopt (exact, no behavior change; the tree prior itself stays research only). **Inference**
(plain cost about linear in simulations): at equal CPU a tree8 search now matches about plain 3.3k instead of
5.5k; §453 matched tree8 against plain 6k at the old cost. Further gains need a cheaper prior (fewer or shallower trees, a higher K), which changes results and would
need its own test.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/silver_tree_prior_speedup_20261013/README.md). Raw:
`/mnt/project-files/silver-tree-prior-speedup-454/raw.tar.gz`. Seeds 74038000–74038002 are now used.

**Knowledge impact:** prior-scoring sentences in the tree-prior paragraph of `architecture/combat-search.md`.

**Question:** Philipp, 2026-10-12 19:58Z: "Can we do rollout3 with the parameters that won 224/256 games but with 8192
sims? And another one which has even more chance nodes but with 4096 nodes? Do 128 seeds. On 8 workers." Does

**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/ooc_r3_s8192_wide_451_20261012/PREREG.md), committed before any cohort seed. `wide` sets
`STS_OOC_MCTS_WIDEN_K=8` (α stays 0.75): twice wbroad's outcome cap, so at ≤4096 visits every chance-node visit samples
a fresh outcome (0 particle revisits in the run vs 9.7M for `combo`). Same-commit control `combo` on the same seeds
(§433 runs do not reproduce after #480). Code `19cfc1ae`, binary `015c90e2…`, `STS_OOC_PUBLIC_FUTURES=8`, B0 `v_win`
leaf (before ADR-0029). Seeds 83000000–127, 8 cloud workers × 16 seeds × 3 arms. Smokes 83009000–001.
Primary, per variant: paired bootstrap 95% CI of Δwin vs `combo` (seed 451); BETTER / WORSE / NOT_SHOWN.
**Validity:** 384/384 units rc=0, no Silver stalls, all configs checked in `.env` and `[ooc-mcts-config]`, tar and CSV
hashes checked; one container restart (worker 6) reran four interrupted units whole.
**Result:** **both NOT_SHOWN.** `combo` 118/128 (92.2%), `s8192` 117/128 (91.4%), `wide` 119/128 (93.0%).
s8192 − combo −0.8 pp [−7.0, +5.5], discordant 8 vs 9; wide − combo +0.8 pp [−5.5, +7.0], 8 vs 7; McNemar p = 1.0
for both. Δfloor +0.46 [−0.62, +1.62] and +0.37 [−0.81, +1.62]. Boss deaths 9 / 8 / 7. MCTS CPU per run 477 / 977 /
472 s.
**Interpretation (Inference):** more search than 4096 simulations buys nothing visible at twice the CPU, and drawing a
fresh chance outcome on every visit is neither better nor more expensive than wbroad. With §428 (fewer outcomes WORSE)
the widening knob matters only on the narrow side. `combo` won 92.2% here, so the room above it is small and 128 pairs
resolve about ±6 pp; NOT_SHOWN does not mean equal.
**Decision:** no change; `combo` (4096, wbroad) stays the reference rollout3 configuration.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/ooc_r3_s8192_wide_451_20261012/README.md). Raw:
`/mnt/project-files/rollout3-8192-wide-451/` (one tar per worker). Seeds 83000000–83000127 and 83009000–001 are now
used.

**Knowledge impact:** one sentence in the rollout3 paragraph of `evaluation/current-research.md`.

## §455 — Silver AZ MLP prior generation 1 vs plain Silver at matched CPU: helps, loop continues (2026-10-13)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-13, "Could we now throw some compute at 'build MLP prior gen 1'?"):** the
generation-1 kill gate of the Silver AlphaZero-style loop (`/mnt/project-files/silver-az-mlp/PLAN.md`
§2.6). Does the random-init MLP tree prior trained on the §397 + §404 corpora (#517, offline fold-4 CE
1.220 vs v1 GBM 1.230) at 2k simulations beat plain Silver given at least the same CPU?
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/silver_az_mlp_gen1_eval_20261013/PREREG.md), frozen after independent
review (code `4f0cfb4c`, binary `fdc44395…a52f`, model `a5f4505a…64d2`). §452/§453 harness and metric
with `STS_CTMSILVER_ARMSET=mlpprior`: arms `plain2k`, `plain_cpu` (plain 2,300 sims, chosen above the
reviewer's measured CPU match of about 2,100-2,150) and `mlp8_2k` (MLP prior at 2k, K = 8, w = 400),
2 replicates each on a shared combat-RNG redraw. Fresh seeds 85000000–85000127, 16 cloud workers × 4
cores. Primary: `mlp8_2k − plain_cpu`, all fights, score; kill if the CI lower bound is ≤ 0.
**Result: `MLP_PRIOR_HELPS`, kill rule `CONTINUE`.** 3,409 of 3,423 fights valid (9 escape-quarantined,

| contrast (score) | all (n = 3,409) | boss (n = 374) | elite (n = 825) |
|---|---|---|---|
| mlp8 − plain_cpu (primary) | +0.91 [+0.43, +1.40] | +3.33 [−0.49, +7.31] | +1.41 [+0.66, +2.25] |
| mlp8 − plain2k | +1.38 [+0.89, +1.88] | +7.17 [+3.19, +11.12] | +1.41 [+0.64, +2.25] |
| plain_cpu − plain2k | +0.46 [−0.06, +0.98] | +3.84 [−0.38, +8.00] | −0.00 [−0.65, +0.68] |

- Realised CPU per fight (thread CPU): plain2k 0.450 s, mlp8 0.472 s (1.05x), plain_cpu 0.523 s
  (1.16x); 10k control 2.43 s. The plain comparison arm had about 11% more CPU than the MLP arm.

  [−0.20, +0.09]; mlp8 − plain2k −0.18 pp [−0.33, −0.03], boss −1.3 pp [−2.6, −0.1]).

**Interpretation:**
- The gen-1 MLP is the first Silver prior shown to beat plain search at matched CPU (§453's GBM tree

- The offline margin over GBM came from one training run (review retrains 1.2299 / 1.2230); this live
  result is for the frozen file only.

## §457 — OOC MCTS `combo` at A20: with today's CTM it loses 6 floors; with the A20 CTM it mostly falls back to V4 and is not shown different from off (2026-10-13)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-13 16:05Z):** "How the ooc MCTS A20 doing? Can we try 128 seeds A/B?" (16:06Z "Just do it
on your own, use 8 workers"; 16:56Z "Just upload the files for the ctm?? Then do it in the cloud?"). Every earlier live
OOC MCTS A/B ran at A0; §425/§426 only scored single A20 decisions.
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/ooc_a20_ab_457_20261013/PREREG.md), independent pre-launch and delta review PASS. Run
commit `6679d0cd` (code `52e605fd`, binary `fdc44395…`), 8 cloud workers, seeds 87000000–87000127, ascension 20,
`STS_OOC_PUBLIC_FUTURES=8`, `STS_WIN_NET` unset (public X2-B leaf, ADR-0029). Arms, all with the §433 base:
- `off`: §433 `off` (exact-10k Silver, V4 OOC gates, act-3 stop).
- `combo`: §433 `combo` with the §443 A20 escape candidate `pathb-a20` (fast `34870815…`, standard `b489e537…`,
  manifest `7274c5c3…`, from `claude/ctm-a20-data` `34d4dfac`), `STS_OOC_MCTS_ACTIVE_LIZARD=0`. The §443 Stage 4 Lizard
  refit could not run (the fast artifact has no `activeLizardCorrection` header), so this CTM refuses every combat
  with an active Lizard Tail.
- `combo_def`: §433 `combo` with today's default CTM stack (§435 Lizard-capable pathb-r2, which gets raw ascension 20;
  §443 Stage 0: it predicts 0.5% deaths where 10.5% happen). Added before launch, after the smoke showed `combo`
  falling back to V4 on 25–67% of decisions (Philipp's decision card, recommended option; unanswered at launch).

Primary, per treatment vs `off`: mean paired floor difference, paired bootstrap 95% CI (10,000 reps, seed 457);
IMPROVED / WORSE / NOT_SHOWN. Wins are the key secondary.
**Validity:** 384/384 units rc=0, no seed failures; every `combo` log shows `candidate_id=pathb-a20`, no other arm's
does; tar hashes checked.

| arm | wins | mean floor | reached act 3 | deaths act 1 / 2 / 3 | boss deaths | V4 fallback | s per run |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| off | 9 | 32.5 | 55 | 35 / 38 / 46 | 43 | — | 36 |
| combo (A20 CTM) | 12 | 32.0 | 52 | 34 / 42 / 40 | 37 | 64.6% | 97 |
| combo_def (default CTM) | 7 | 26.3 | 31 | 42 / 55 / 24 | 24 | 1.9% | 284 |

- `combo − off`: floors −0.50 [−2.69, +1.65], **NOT_SHOWN**; wins +2.3 pp [−2.3, +7.0], discordant 6 vs 3, p = 0.51.
- `combo_def − off`: floors −6.20 [−9.40, −2.90], **WORSE**; wins −1.6 pp [−7.0, +3.9], discordant 5 vs 7, p = 0.77.
- `combo − combo_def` (descriptive): floors +5.70 [+2.22, +9.10].
- Support aborts: `combo` 51.3 per run (6,556 `active_unqualified_lizard`, 9 `writhing_ritual_intersection`);
  `combo_def` 3 `hp_envelope` in all 128 runs.

**Interpretation:**
- OOC MCTS as it exists today does not help at A20; with the default CTM it is clearly worse (−6.2 floors) at about
  8x the CPU of `off`.
- **Inference:** the default CTM's blindness to A20 death risk is the likely cause. `combo_def` dies far more often in
  acts 1–2 (97 vs 73) and reaches act 3 in 31 runs vs 55, consistent with a search that treats risky fights as safe.
  Its fewer boss deaths only reflect fewer runs reaching bosses.
- The A20 CTM package as it stands (mostly V4 fallback) avoids that loss (+5.7 floors over `combo_def`,
  descriptive); this cannot separate a better-calibrated CTM from simply searching less. The search owned only 35% of
  decisions: imagined futures that pick up a Lizard Tail reach a refused combat and abort the whole root search (51
  aborts per run, even on runs that never own a Tail), so `combo` mostly played V4 and is not shown different from
  `off`. This run says nothing about OOC MCTS with a fully supported A20 CTM.
- The searched decisions are not a random subset. Share of decisions the search kept, by screen (from
  `*.mcts.csv.actions.jsonl`, `executed`): map 57% (2,210 of 3,909), rewards 23%, shop 32%, rest 24%, events 20%,
  card select 8%, boss relic 6%, treasure 0%; map decisions are 60% of all searched decisions.
- "How many decisions differ between arms" (a PREREG descriptive) was not computed at decision level; 60 of 128
  seeds reach a different floor in `combo` than in `off`, 115 in `combo_def`.
- Floors are a better metric than wins here: 7–12 wins of 128 per arm.

**Decision:** no default change; OOC MCTS stays off (ADR-0027). A meaningful A20 test needs Lizard support in the A20
CTM (an `activeLizardCorrection` header and an A20 refit, a new pre-registered §443 step) and then a rerun of `combo`
on these seeds.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/ooc_a20_ab_457_20261013/README.md). Raw: `/mnt/project-files/ooc-a20-ab/` (one tar
per worker, smoke tar). Seeds 87000000–87000127 and smokes 74047000–74047003 are now used.

**Knowledge impact:** one sentence in the rollout3 paragraph of `evaluation/current-research.md`.

## §458 — OOC MCTS `combo` at A20 with a Lizard-capable A20 CTM: +6.0 floors over off, V4 fallback 2% (2026-10-13)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-13 19:31Z):** "Okay add the lizard support then? I want no fallbacks to v4". §457's A20
CTM lacked Lizard Tail support, so 64.6% of `combo`'s decisions fell back to V4.
**Lizard step (§443 Stage 4 Step 1b, pre-registered in `/mnt/project-files/ctm-a20/lizard/PREREG-LIZARD.md`, built on
Philipp's machine, CPU only):** the A20 fast artifact got the mechanical-q `activeLizardCorrection` header
(`package_deepsets_lizard_artifact.py`, the step chain B skipped), was restamped, and its escape head was refit on the new
file (amended before any Lizard output, because `ctm_escape.py extend` refuses a checkpoint fit on another file; the
refit reproduced the old escape weights byte for byte). Both artifacts got the Writhing+Ritual capability; `ctm_lizard.py`
refit r at A20 on the Stage 1 Lizard slices and main corpus and added Fairy and Brew. Output on `claude/ctm-a20-data`
`c507cebb`: fast `ae785ec2…`, standard `e338506d…`, manifest `704f2a58…`.
- Keep rule: criterion 1 PASS (VALIDATION r NLL vs the TRAIN base rate: fast 0.300 vs 0.384, standard 0.244 vs 0.327);
  criterion 2 FAIL as written (composed survival on Tail-fired VALIDATION rows: fairy +0.070 on 44 rows, brew −0.014
  on 21 rows, bar ±0.01; over all VALIDATION rows of each cohort −0.0003 and −0.0013). **Inference:** a 0.01 bar on
  21–44 rows is far inside the noise (about ±0.07), so criterion 2 was badly chosen; it stands as NOT_QUALIFIED. Philipp
  chose "Rerun anyway" (19:58Z) for a research arm. The §443 re-gate stays blocked.
- Writhing+Ritual has no cohort gate at A20 (too few rows).

**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/ooc_a20_lizard_458_20261013/PREREG.md), independent pre-launch review PASS. One arm,
`combo_liz` = §457 `combo` with the CTM above and `STS_OOC_MCTS_ACTIVE_LIZARD=1`; run commit `800fe39f`, built at the
§457 code `52e605fd` (binary `fdc44395…`, checked by every worker), 16 cloud workers × 8 seeds, seeds 87000000–127,
ascension 20. `off`, `combo` and `combo_def` are §457's rows (same binary and seeds). Primary: `combo_liz − off` mean
paired floor difference, paired bootstrap 95% CI (10,000 reps, seed 458).
**Validity:** 128/128 units rc=0, no seed failures; every `combo_liz` log shows `candidate_id=pathb-a20` and
`"activeLizardEnabled":true`; tar hashes checked.

| arm | wins | mean floor | reached act 3 | deaths act 1 / 2 / 3 | boss deaths | V4 fallback | s per run |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| off (§457) | 9 | 32.5 | 55 | 35 / 38 / 46 | 43 | — | 36 |
| combo, A20 CTM without Lizard (§457) | 12 | 32.0 | 52 | 34 / 42 / 40 | 37 | 64.6% | 97 |
| combo_def, default CTM (§457) | 7 | 26.3 | 31 | 42 / 55 / 24 | 24 | 1.9% | 284 |
| **combo_liz, Lizard A20 CTM** | **12** | **38.5** | **72** | **14 / 42 / 60** | 50 | **2.2%** | 387 |

- `combo_liz − off`: floors **+6.03 [+2.69, +9.37], IMPROVED**; wins +2.3 pp [−3.9, +9.4], discordant 11 vs 8,
  p = 0.65.
- Descriptive: vs `combo_def` floors +12.23 [+9.07, +15.33]; vs §457 `combo` +6.53 [+3.40, +9.71], wins equal (11 vs 11
  discordant).
- Support aborts: 0 in all 128 runs. The 2.2% fallback is 277 `root_boundary` decisions (no model refusal).

**Interpretation:**
- With a CTM that is calibrated for A20 and supports every imagined combat, OOC MCTS at A20 reaches 6 floors further
  than off. Most of the gain is surviving act 1 (14 vs 35 deaths); 72 vs 55 runs reach act 3.
- Wins are not separated (12 vs 9 of 128): at A20 most runs die in act 3 or at its boss, and the win difference
  would need far more seeds.
- **Inference:** §457's −6.2 floors with the default CTM and this +6.0 with the A20 CTM point at CTM calibration as
  what decides OOC MCTS at A20; this run does not isolate it (the CTMs also differ in training data and Lizard r).
- Cost: about 11x the CPU of `off` per run (387 vs 36 s).

**Decision:** no default change. OOC MCTS stays off by default (ADR-0027), and the A20 CTM stays a research candidate
(Stage 3a NOT_QUALIFIED on boss bias; Lizard keep rule criterion 2 failed as written). A default for A20 would need the
§443 re-gate on the fresh Stage 4 corpus, which Lizard support now makes possible except for the keep-rule decision.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/ooc_a20_lizard_458_20261013/README.md). Raw: `/mnt/project-files/ooc-a20-lizard/` (one
tar per worker). Seeds 87000000–87000127 reused; smokes 74047010–74047011 and reviewer seeds 74055000–099 used.

**Knowledge impact:** one sentence in the rollout3 paragraph of `evaluation/current-research.md`.

## §460 — Silver AZ MLP prior generation 3: still beats plain Silver at matched CPU, not shown better than generation 1; loop continues (2026-10-13)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-13, "Can we do a gen 3 silver prior?"):** the generation-3 milestone
of the Silver AlphaZero-style loop (`/mnt/project-files/silver-az-mlp/PLAN.md` §2.5, §7). Generation
2 and generation 3 each came from 1,024 self-play runs at 2k with the previous MLP as tree prior
(root bonus off) plus warm-started training on the window
([gen-2 packet](evidence/silver_az_mlp_gen2_20261013/README.md),
[gen-3 packet](evidence/silver_az_mlp_gen3_20261013/README.md); offline gen 3 vs gen 2: orig
fold-4 CE 1.2192 vs 1.2196, own held-out teacher 1.3313 vs 1.3375, mean TV 0.036). Does gen 3
still beat plain Silver at matched CPU, and does iteration beat gen 1?
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/silver_az_mlp_gen3_eval_20261013/PREREG.md), frozen after independent
review (code `37b7d33e`, binary `9098ee11…b0f7`, gen 3 `f57b7fdd…5315`, gen 1 `a5f4505a…64d2`).
§455 harness and metric with an added arm `mlp_prev8_2k` (gen 1): arms `plain2k`, `plain_cpu`
(plain 2,300), `mlp8_2k` (gen 3) and `mlp_prev8_2k`, all MLP arms at 2k, K = 8, w = 400, 2
replicates each on a shared combat-RNG redraw. Fresh seeds 90000000–90000127, 16 cloud workers ×
4 cores. Primary: `mlp8_2k − plain_cpu`; iteration: `mlp8_2k − mlp_prev8_2k`, both all fights,
score. Rule: continue to gen 6 unless the primary is NOT_SHOWN/HURTS and the iteration contrast
is not GEN3_BEATS_GEN1.
**Result: primary `MLP_PRIOR_HELPS`, iteration `NOT_SHOWN`; loop continues.** 3,275 of 3,303
fights valid (24 escape-quarantined, 4 with invalid control replays; no stall, all shards rc 0).

| contrast (score) | all (n = 3,275) | boss (n = 367) | elite (n = 791) |
|---|---|---|---|
| gen3 − plain_cpu (primary) | +1.50 [+0.94, +2.09] | +8.31 [+3.82, +13.04] | +1.24 [+0.53, +2.04] |
| gen3 − gen1 (iteration) | +0.14 [−0.39, +0.66] | −0.18 [−4.39, +4.14] | +0.03 [−0.47, +0.62] |
| gen1 − plain_cpu | +1.36 [+0.87, +1.88] | +8.49 [+4.63, +12.64] | +1.21 [+0.59, +1.93] |
| gen3 − plain2k | +1.76 [+1.18, +2.39] | +9.89 [+5.18, +14.91] | +1.18 [+0.37, +2.01] |
| plain_cpu − plain2k | +0.27 [−0.25, +0.78] | +1.58 [−2.73, +5.97] | −0.06 [−0.82, +0.65] |

- Realised CPU per fight: plain2k 0.386 s, gen 3 0.409 s (1.06x), gen 1 0.404 s (1.04x),
  plain_cpu 0.448 s (1.16x); 10k control 2.13 s. Plain at 2,300 again had about 10% more CPU
  than the MLP arms.
- Death rate per fight: plain2k 1.10%, plain_cpu 1.07%, gen 3 0.81%, gen 1 0.85% (gen3 −
  plain_cpu −0.26 pp [−0.45, −0.09]; boss −1.8 pp [−3.3, −0.4]; gen3 − gen1 boss 0.0 pp
  [−1.2, +1.2]).
- PLAN §2.6 "converged" rule (iteration point estimate < +0.3 with CI including 0, and offline
  TV < 0.03): not met, because TV is 0.036.

**Interpretation:**
- The §455 result replicates on fresh seeds: both MLP generations beat plain Silver given more
  CPU, with the gain concentrated in boss fights.
- Two generations of self-play did not measurably improve play over the bootstrap-trained gen
  1 (+0.14, CI ±0.5). **Inference:** consistent with the small offline gains (orig fold-4 CE
  1.2204 → 1.2192); the iteration signal, if any, is below this design's resolution.
- By the pre-registered rule the loop continues toward the gen-6 milestone. **Open question:**
  whether to keep the PLAN recipe or change it (for example a stronger teacher or a larger
  model), since the policy is close to converged offline (TV 0.055 → 0.036).
- Fight score, not run win rate; win-rate impact is **Unverified**.

## §461 — A20 internal leaf capture: one-seed observational parity PASS (2026-10-13)

**Question:** can #507 capture genuine internal leaf input/target pairs without
changing the search? Existing §458 run summaries, §445 decision-root labels and
CTM transition/gate corpora do not contain these pairs.

**Design:** independently reviewed, frozen [protocol and evidence](evidence/ooc_leaf_capture_461_20261013/README.md).
One sequential capture-off/on pair on historical seed 87000000, A20 Act 3/no keys,
fair play, exact-10k native Silver, 4096 OOC simulations, K=4/alpha=.75, three CTM
combats, V4 prior/continuation and public X2-B. Source `252db2a7`, Release binary
`b4586cfc…`, exact PR #524 / §458 CTM from data commit `c507cebb` (NOT_QUALIFIED).
Both arms pin old shop deck-size behavior, planner rollout shops and Silver loop
guard off. This is current-source parity with the selected historical settings,
not historical reproduction. One worker, 900 CPU / 1200 wall seconds per arm;
no retries, extra seeds or training. §459 remains reserved for the separate
preregistered greedy-shop experiment.

**Result: collector-canary PASS**, independently reproduced from raw artifacts.
Both runs rc=0 and runtime/backend provenance validated. All deterministic
results, decision/action/support traces and 136 root / 54 floor profiles match;
only preregistered timing fields are excluded. The first 64 roots produced
286 structurally valid samples, with zero input/evaluation/observer errors or
captured-root aborts. Coverage: 207 Act 1 and 79 Act 2, no Act 3; MAP 112, rewards
111, rest/shop 18 each, boss relic 10, treasure 8, event 6, card select 3. All
inputs were decision boundaries; five continuations ended terminal. 285 samples
completed three CTM combats and one completed one. Capture size: 4,509,533 bytes.

CPU off/on: 267.779914 / 270.934469 seconds, ratio 1.01178; wall 267.815354 /
270.948831 seconds. This is descriptive timing from one ordered pair alongside
an unrelated Debug test process, not a qualified overhead estimate. Both
trajectories died at floor 51; their matching outcome is parity evidence only.

**Decision:** bounded collector behavior is demonstrated on this seed. No
compression, stability, training-suitability or gameplay verdict. Next inspect
MAP inputs and prove exact in-process replay with original state ID, full initial
state/path, pre-evaluation policy state and copied RNG; JSONL does not supply
replay custody. Then separately bound independent-future repeats. Keep #506's
public-input/belief qualification and the research teacher's gates separate.

**Evidence:** the packet includes the frozen manifest/protocol, machine-readable
report and compressed raw observations/traces/receipts/analyzer with hashes.
The complete executable/model bundle is retained locally at the path in its
README. Seed 87000000 was reused for diagnostics and cannot become a holdout.

**Knowledge impact:** update the maintained #507 status in `evaluation/current-research.md`;
no production default or model change.

## §459 — Greedy rollout shops in rollout3 `combo`: wins not shown different, about 11% less CPU (2026-10-13)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-13):** "I think we can just buy the best greedily in the rollout", then "test
on fresh seeds with 8 workers". Inside OOC MCTS leaf rollouts, does replacing the bundle planner
(`nativeShopPlan` scores every affordable subset and executes the first item of the best bundle) with
`STS_OOC_MCTS_ROLLOUT_SHOP=greedy` (#523: single best purchase, removal or leave per decision) change how
§433 `combo` plays, in wins and in CPU?
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/ooc_greedy_shop_459_20261013/PREREG.md), frozen after independent review
(code `440cf556`, binary `16426481…7527`). Arms `planner` and `greedy`: §433 `combo` with pinned
`STS_OOC_PUBLIC_FUTURES=8`, X2-B public `STS_WIN_NET` and `STS_OOC_SHOP_DECK_SIZE_FIX=1`, differing only
in `STS_OOC_MCTS_ROLLOUT_SHOP`. Fresh seeds 89000000–89000127, 8 cloud workers. Primary: Δwin greedy −
planner, paired seed bootstrap; BETTER / WORSE / NOT_SHOWN.
**Result: NOT_SHOWN.** 128/128 pairs valid, all units rc=0, no stall.

| | greedy | planner | greedy − planner |
|---|---|---|---|
| wins / 128 | 103 | 101 | +1.6 pp [−5.5, +8.6]; McNemar p = 0.83 (12 vs 10 discordant) |
| mean floor | 48.41 | 49.12 | −0.70 [−1.77, +0.23] |
| boss deaths | 21 | 23 | |
| seconds per run | 496.5 | 558.2 | paired ratio 0.889 [0.859, 0.922] |

- MCTS CPU per run 426 vs 483 s; simulations per run 241.5k vs 248.1k; owned share 97.6% in both.
- Live shops (descriptive, per run): greedy buys fewer cards (1.62 vs 1.88), potions (1.06 vs 1.24) and
  removals (0.44 vs 0.55), slightly more relics (2.33 vs 2.20).

**Interpretation:**
- Greedy rollout shops cost about 11% less wall time per run at no detectable win-rate cost; the CI
  excludes a loss larger than 5.5 pp. NOT_SHOWN does not mean equal.
- The CPU ratio was not a pre-registered statistic. **Inference:** most of the saving is the bundle
  planner's subset enumeration that §437/§442 measured inside rollouts.
- `combo` with planner shops won 78.9% here, below §433's 87.5% and §449's 86.7–89.1% on other seeds.

  default.

## §462 — A20 one-leaf inherited-memory replay: exact parity PASS (2026-10-14)

**Question:** before measuring #507 target stability, can one actual internal
MAP leaf reproduce its scheduled teacher evaluation from the same complete
inherited process state? §461 JSONL is an incomplete observation, not a replay
snapshot; reconstructing it as root zero would change evaluator semantics.

**Design:** independently reviewed [protocol and evidence](evidence/ooc_leaf_replay_462_20261014/README.md).
Source `1125d07db5f5d6597759af291d2fdc4c6981f066`, Release binary `abd6f14d…`.
Historical seed 87000000, A20, decision 0, ordinal 1025; initially nonterminal
MAP required, no replacement. Exact §461 / PR #524 CTM and teacher settings,
with unrelated trace/profile outputs disabled. One additional child evaluation
forked before the parent's scheduled evaluation preserves the original model,
state ID, path, callbacks, policy, caches and RNG. Verified single OS thread;
child evaluates and exits before parent evaluates. A private completion signal
stops the root prefix before real action execution. Limits: parent 20 plus
child 10 CPU seconds, 60 wall seconds; bounded 64 KiB transport and 10-second
child wall timeout. No retries or independent-future repetitions.

**Result: PASS**, independently checked against the frozen raw report. Both
evaluations returned exactly **0.6771143269743937**, nonterminal, with endpoint
floor 5 / HP 66 / max HP 75, three resolved CTM combats and 21 projection steps.
Complete final planner RNG matched and source state/path stayed unchanged.
State ID, initial/final RNG and all recorded target fields also matched the
historical §461 sample (descriptive cross-build check, not another pass gate).
One header and one replay report were written; no completed root or game result.
Return code 0; total CPU **0.907232 s**, wall **0.966319 s**. All loaded CTM,
effective policy, full STS environment, binary/source and artifact checks passed.

**Decision:** inherited-memory deterministic repeatability is demonstrated for
this single leaf. This is not serialized replay, target stability, public-input
sufficiency, CTM qualification or gameplay quality. Next preregister a bounded
independent-future stability study before fitting a student. No training,
teacher/default promotion, additional seed or #506 contract change occurred.

**Knowledge impact:** document the diagnostic interface in the OOC architecture
and CODE_MAP; update #507's current status in `evaluation/current-research.md`.

## §467 — Collector-specific Silver MLP prior (fine-tuned gen 4): offline CANDIDATE, −0.0125 CE on held-out Collector roots (2026-10-14)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-14, "investigating fight specific silver prior … fine tune a net to a specific
hard fight"):** does a Silver tree prior fine-tuned on one hard fight beat the general gen-4 MLP on that fight?
**Pilot (no new data):** fine-tuning gen 4 on the gen-4 window's own roots of one boss gave only −0.002 to
−0.003 fold-4 CE on each act-2/3 boss (Collector −0.0030 [−0.0039, −0.0020]); half the Collector seeds gave
−0.0010, a Collector-only net from scratch +0.059. On the Collector, gen 3 → gen 4 was −0.0062. The encounter
reaches the MLP only as a raw scalar id (state feature 1).
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/silver_fight_specific_collector_20261014/PREREG.md), reviewed before launch.
New mode `one_combat silverazfocusgen` (PR #531, code `1518989b`, binary `ad90e698…5493`): the Collector is
forced as act-2 boss, earlier fights play unrecorded at 2k with the gen-4 prior, the first Collector fight is
recorded at 10k with the gen-4 prior (K = 8, w = 400, root bonus off) as 4 copies (1 unperturbed, 3 perturbed),
then the run ends. Seeds 95000000–95002559, 4 cloud workers (Philipp 09:23Z). Fine-tune gen 4 on old + new
Collector roots (folds seed % 5; lr 2e-4, wd 1e-2, dropout 0.35, LR halving, patience 8). Primary: fold-4 CE
on the 9,711 old Collector test roots, fine-tuned − gen 4, seed-cluster bootstrap; CANDIDATE if ≤ −0.0062 with
CI below 0.
**Result: CANDIDATE.** 640/640 units rc 0, no stalls; 282,417 roots in 7,968 Collector fights (0 invalid);
261,348 multi-action roots.

| fine-tune | old Collector fold 4 (9,711) | new fold 4 (53,867) |
|---|---|---|
| **primary, lr 2e-4, all new data** | **−0.0125 [−0.0157, −0.0094]** (1.4411 → 1.4287; top-1 46.3 → 46.8%) | −0.0189 [−0.0207, −0.0173] |
| lr 1e-4 / 5e-4 | −0.0123 / −0.0110 | −0.0188 / −0.0193 |
| 25% / 50% of new train seeds | −0.0063 / −0.0086 | −0.0108 / −0.0135 |
| no new data (pilot) | −0.0030 | — |

- The gain keeps growing with fight-specific data (−0.003 → −0.006 → −0.009 → −0.0125); not flat at 260k roots.
- New-root CIs count unperturbed and perturbed copies of a seed as 2 clusters, so they are slightly narrow.
- Earlier fights at 2k change the HP/deck distribution at the Collector relative to the 10k-teacher old roots.
- Native export `combat_policy_mlp_collector467.txt` passes parity (164 roots, max |Δlogit| 1.3e-6).

**Interpretation:** fight-specific data, not specialization alone, is what moves the prior: about two
generations' worth of offline gain on the Collector for ~20 core-hours. **Open question:** whether it shows in
play; offline gains of a similar order have not always transferred (§460). The pre-registered next step is an
online Collector-only paired check (needs Philipp's go). No default change.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/silver_fight_specific_collector_20261014/README.md). Raw:
`/mnt/project-files/silver-prior-fight-specific/`. Seeds 95000000–95002559 and smokes 74067000–74067055
(author) and 74069050–74069062 (reviewer) are now used.

**Knowledge impact:** `architecture/combat-search.md` documents `silverazfocusgen`.

## §471 — A20 four-leaf conditional target stability: STABILITY_MEASURED (2026-10-14)

**Question:** how variable are repeated outputs of the existing three-combat
CTM teacher from four fixed inherited MAP snapshots? This extends §462 exact
same-RNG repeatability to new planner streams; it does not establish a value
conditioned only on public input.

**Design:** independently reviewed [protocol and evidence](evidence/ooc_leaf_stability_471_20261014/README.md).
Reviewed producer `c822cfbf6e4a03fba512c6a081442ec856f03691`, actual Release
binary `36127ba9…`. Exact §461 / PR #524 teacher, historical seed 87000000,
A20, first four distinct candidate MAP inputs in the first two roots:
`(0,1025)`, `(0,2049)`, `(1,1)`, `(1,513)`. All are Act 1/floor 0
Neow-transform variants, selected on inputs before new results. Each fresh
child inherits the unchanged original full state/callback/policy/cache context.
One original-RNG control and sixteen independently seeded children precede
one original parent evaluation. All 64 uint64 seeds were frozen from SHA256
of the specified selector/replicate string. Root 0's ordinary action executes;
root 1 completes and stops before its real action. No actual combat or full
run result is collected. Limits: 30 parent plus 30 cumulative child CPU
seconds, 90 wall seconds; each child 10 CPU/wall seconds and 64 KiB transport.
No retries, replacement leaves, extra samples or seed extension.

**Result: STABILITY_MEASURED.** All four same-RNG controls matched exactly;
all original leaf identities, results and RNG strings matched §461, and both
complete ordinary parent-root records were identical (2519 and 3903 completed
simulations, preserving visit-lock early stopping). All 64 planned new-stream
results were valid and nonterminal. Exactly 72 records were emitted. Source,
binary, full environment, effective teacher policy, loaded CTM identity and
artifact custody passed. Return code 0; aggregate CPU **4.389738 s**, including
**0.167306 s** in diagnostic children; wall **7.777792 s**. Concurrent regression
checks and one narrow cohort make timing descriptive only.

| Decision / ordinal | K | Mean | Sample SD | Estimated SE16 | Min–max | Terminal |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 / 1025 | 16 | 0.698576 | 0.087282 | 0.021820 | 0.566860–0.908407 | 0/16 |
| 0 / 2049 | 16 | 0.692093 | 0.043348 | 0.010837 | 0.620063–0.805293 | 0/16 |
| 1 / 1 | 16 | 0.711904 | 0.050231 | 0.012558 | 0.569240–0.782159 | 0/16 |
| 1 / 513 | 16 | 0.712064 | 0.063552 | 0.015888 | 0.564222–0.819237 | 0/16 |

All four meet the preregistered descriptive `SE16 <= 0.05` flag. Across-leaf
mean range is **0.01997094**, sample SD **0.00997039**; these describe four
correlated selected snapshots, with no confidence interval or significance
test. The full report retains unbiased sample variance and subgroup counts.
Zero observed terminals does not establish rare-event coverage.

**Decision:** target precision is now measured for this narrow conditional
teacher kernel. Single draws vary materially; sixteen-draw mean estimates
have roughly 0.01–0.02 estimated standard error here. The small between-leaf
mean spread does not show reliable action ranking. Broader coverage across
independent source runs/later MAP states, terminal/support boundaries and
public-input sufficiency need their own reviewed protocol before a student
fit. No broader run, training, CTM qualification, gameplay quality or default
promotion follows. The CTM remains NOT_QUALIFIED.

**Knowledge impact:** document the explicit stability command in OOC
architecture/CODE_MAP and update #507's current status in the maintained
research page. This entry and its evidence packet retain the frozen experiment.

## §472 — OOC MCTS without leaf rollout combats vs rollout3 on the current defaults: WORSE, −12.5 pp (2026-10-14)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-14 14:59Z):** "With the new ooc MCTS, we explore deeper. Maybe we don't need the
rollouts anymore. Can we test on 128 seeds rollout 3 vs no rollout?" With tree rules and outcome merging on
(ADR-0031) and the greedy rollout shop (ADR-0032), does `STS_OOC_MCTS_LEAF_COMBATS=0` (leaf valued at the next map
screen, no extra combats) win as many runs as `LEAF_COMBATS=3`?
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/ooc_rollout0_472_20261014/PREREG.md), frozen after independent pre-launch review
(code `aedbd473`, binary `207ddb6a…`, run commit `1e386af2`). Arms `rollout3` (§433 `combo` with the ADR-0028 to
ADR-0032 defaults pinned) and `rollout0` (only `LEAF_COMBATS=0`). Ironclad A0, fresh seeds 101000000–101000127,
16 cloud workers. Primary: Δwin rollout0 − rollout3, paired seed bootstrap; BETTER / WORSE / NOT_SHOWN; secondary
non-inferiority at 10 pp.
**Result: WORSE.** 128/128 pairs valid, all units rc=0, no stall.

| | rollout0 | rollout3 | rollout0 − rollout3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| wins / 128 | 92 | 108 | −12.5 pp [−21.9, −3.1]; McNemar p = 0.014 (11 vs 27 discordant) |
| mean floor | 47.41 | 48.95 | −1.54 [−3.23, +0.04] |
| boss deaths | 30 | 16 | |
| seconds per run | 237 | 639 | sum ratio 0.37 |
| MCTS CPU per run | 165 s | 561 s | ratio 0.29 |
| per-search max depth, median / p90 / max | 4 / 8 / 12 | 4 / 8 / 13 | |
| pick = top prior / top Q | 78.2% / 50.2% | 75.9% / 50.8% | |

**Interpretation:**
- Dropping the leaf combats loses runs (NOT_NONINFERIOR_AT_10PP too) while saving about 63% of wall time; rollout3
  stays, per the prereg rule.
- Aggregate tree depth, simulations per run and root pick agreement are about the same in both arms, so the loss does
  not come from a shallower search. **Inference:** the leaf value at the next map screen, without the three combats,
  is the likely cause; it misses consequences that show up in the next few fights. Leaf-value quality was not
  measured, and on the 38 discordant seeds the arms play different games. Boss deaths 30 vs 16 are descriptive, not
  pre-registered.
- No change; `LEAF_COMBATS=3` stays in the OOC MCTS research configuration (the code default of the knob remains 0,
  and OOC MCTS stays off by default, ADR-0027). Philipp decides what comes next.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/ooc_rollout0_472_20261014/README.md). Raw: `/mnt/project-files/ooc-rollout0-472/`
(one tar per worker). Seeds 101000000–101000127 and smoke 74070600 are now used.

**Knowledge impact:** the `LEAF_COMBATS` row in `architecture/out-of-combat.md` now cites §472.

## §466 — Final-fight Silver leaf: potions no longer hoarded, act-3 boss win rate unchanged (2026-10-14)

**Question:** in the run-ending fight Silver's leaf still pays 11 per potion on a win and 5.5 on a
loss. Does a leaf that values nothing after that fight (`STS_SILVER_FINAL_FIGHT_LEAF=1`: every win
scores `winBonus + root maxHp`, a loss keeps damage/survival/energy/draw shaping without potion or
cheat-death credit) win the act-3 boss more often? Background (descriptive, §460 replays): 8/18
act-3 boss deaths of exact-10k Silver still held potions.

**Design:** pre-registered fight-level replay ([evidence](evidence/silver_final_fight_leaf_466_20261014/README.md)).
Run commit `8d8eeb3c`, binary `c92c0297…`. `ctmsilvergen` arm set `finalleaf`: one plain exact-10k
A0 source run per seed (frozen V4 OOC policy, MCTS off), then every act-3 boss state replayed by
`base10k` (default leaf) and `final10k` (final-fight leaf), R = 8 paired redraws of the six combat
RNG streams. Seeds 96000000-96000255, 8 workers × 4 cores. Primary: paired per-fight win-rate
difference, 95% bootstrap over source seeds (10,000 resamples, RNG 0).

**Result: `NOT_SHOWN`.** 236 act-3 boss fights, none excluded (control replay 236/236, 32/32 shards
rc 0). Win rate base 0.8633, final 0.8639: **+0.05 pp [−1.27, +1.38]**. Per boss: Awakened One −1.21
(62), Donu and Deca +0.88 (85), Time Eater +0.14 (89). The option changed behavior as intended:
deaths holding a potion 105/258 → 0/257, potions held per win 1.19 → 0.14. CPU per fight 9.18 →
10.05 s.

**Interpretation:** **Inference:** the potions Silver kept in losing final fights were not what
decided those fights; spending all of them leaves the act-3 boss win rate within ±1.3 pp. A gain
larger than about 1.4 pp per act-3 boss fight is excluded at exact 10k. Production learned-stop
Silver and A20 were not tested.
**Decision:** no default change; the option stays default off and this candidate stops per the
pre-registration (no whole-run confirmation).

**Knowledge impact:** `STS_SILVER_FINAL_FIGHT_LEAF` documented in
`operations/environment-variables.md`; the situational-leaf investigation (including an A20
first-boss heal mis-credit, not fixed here) recorded in
`knowledge-base/investigations/2026-10-14-silver-situational-leaf.md`.

## §468 — Situational Silver leaf bundle in whole runs: A0 not shown, A20 floors worse but more wins (2026-10-14)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-14 11:18Z, after §466):** "Keep it in. Fix the bug for the A20 boss. Add the smaller idea
and test again with all those things." Does Silver with all situational leaf changes together play better whole runs
than the legacy leaf?

**Design:** pre-registered paired whole runs ([evidence](evidence/silver_leaf_combo_468_20261014/README.md)). Code
`f41ec4d3`, run commit `7fc41609`, binary `a45ef01e…`. Both arms are the §422 `off` environment (exact-10k live Silver,
V4 OOC policy, OOC MCTS off, `STS_STOP_AFTER_ACT=3`). `base` sets `STS_SILVER_A20_BOSS_HEAL_FIX`,
`STS_SILVER_FINAL_FIGHT_LEAF`, `STS_SILVER_NO_LOSS_POTION_CREDIT` and `STS_SILVER_RELIC_HEAL_LEAF` to 0, `all` sets all
four to 1. A0 seeds 98000000–98000499 and A20 seeds 98000500–98000999, 8 workers (Philipp's pick). Primary A0: Δwin;
primary A20: Δfloor; paired seed bootstrap 95% CI (10,000 resamples).

**Result:** valid, 2,000/2,000 units rc=0, 500 pairs per cohort, no seed dropped.
- **A0: `NOT_SHOWN`.** Wins 370 → 357, **Δwin −2.6 pp [−6.4, +1.2]** (discordant 41 vs 54, McNemar p = 0.22);
  Δfloor −0.18 [−0.74, +0.39]; deaths at the act-3 boss 59 → 69.
- **A20: `WORSE` on the primary.** **Δfloor −1.29 [−2.42, −0.19]**. Wins 52 → 71, Δwin +3.8 pp [+0.6, +7.0]
  (discordant 44 vs 25, McNemar p = 0.029).
- Descriptive (not pre-registered): at A20 the bundle dies more in act 1 (96 → 120; paired 50 vs 26, p = 0.008) and
  less at the two final bosses (floor 50 deaths 51 → 42, second boss 74 → 48). Of the 113 seeds where both arms reached
  floor 50, wins 38 → 52. Cost unchanged (42.8 vs 41.1 s per A20 run, 62.4 vs 62.8 s per A0 run).

**Interpretation:** **Inference:** the bundle mixes two kinds of change. The end-of-run parts (A20 heal fix, final-fight
leaf) act only at floors 50–51, where the A20 bundle wins more often. The every-fight parts (no loss potion credit, relic
heal leaf) are the only ones active in act 1, where the A20 bundle dies more, so they likely cause the floor loss; this
run cannot separate the terms. At A0 the every-fight parts may also cost wins (point estimate −2.6 pp, not shown).

**Decision (pre-registered):** A0 NOT_SHOWN and A20 WORSE: all three opt-ins stay off. The A20 heal fix is a correctness
fix whose A20 cohort was WORSE in the bundle, so whether it stays default on is Philipp's call.

**Knowledge impact:** situational-leaf investigation page updated with the §468 result; option rows in
`operations/environment-variables.md` unchanged (defaults unchanged pending the decision). Seeds 98000000–98000999 and
smokes 74070100–74070101 are used.

## §474 — End-of-run Silver leaf parts alone (A20 heal fix + final-fight leaf): not shown at A0 or A20 (2026-10-14)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-14 13:43Z, card "Split test" after §468):** do the two end-of-run leaf changes alone
(`STS_SILVER_A20_BOSS_HEAL_FIX=1`, `STS_SILVER_FINAL_FIGHT_LEAF=1`) play better whole runs than the legacy leaf?

**Design:** as §468 ([evidence](evidence/silver_leaf_split_471_20261014/README.md); the evidence folder, analyzer
`tools/analyze_silver_leaf_471.py` and pre-registration carry the planning number 471, renumbered to §474 after main's
§471 landed), arms `base` (all four leaf options
0) vs `end` (those two 1, `NO_LOSS_POTION_CREDIT` and `RELIC_HEAL_LEAF` 0). Code `7a6c6bb9` (§468 code plus main with
#532; OOC MCTS off in both arms), run commit `965000fa`, binary `6b2bca17…`. Fresh A0 seeds 100000000–100000499 and A20
seeds 100000500–100000999, 8 workers (Philipp's pick). Primary A0 Δwin, A20 Δfloor, paired seed bootstrap 95% CI.

**Result:** valid, 2,000/2,000 units rc=0, 500 pairs per cohort.
- **A0: `NOT_SHOWN`.** Wins 402 → 406, **Δwin +0.8 pp [−1.2, +3.0]** (discordant 17 vs 13).
- **A20: `NOT_SHOWN`.** **Δfloor 0.00 [−0.02, +0.02]**; wins 42 → 47, +1.0 pp [−0.4, +2.4] (discordant 10 vs 5,
  McNemar p = 0.30).
- Descriptive: both arms play every seed identically until floor 50 (the options act only in the A20 first act-3
  boss and the run-ending fight). At A20, deaths at floor 50 rise 52 → 57 and second-boss deaths fall 66 → 56.

**Interpretation:** the end-of-run parts change only the final one or two fights. The intervals exclude gains above
about 3.0 pp (A0) and 2.4 pp (A20); the point estimate (+5 A20 wins) is about a quarter of §468's A20 win gain (+19),
but the intervals (and the different seeds) cannot rule out that the end-of-run parts made up most of it.
**Inference:** the §468 act-1 deaths (paired 50 vs 26) came from the every-fight parts (no loss potion credit, relic
heal leaf), since the `end` arm leaves play before floor 50 unchanged.

**Decision (pre-registered):** NOT_SHOWN in both cohorts: no default change; the A20 heal fix stays default on (A20
not WORSE), the final-fight leaf and the two every-fight options stay off.

**Later decision:** Philipp made all four leaf terms the default the same day (ADR-0035), not on a passed gate.

**Knowledge impact:** investigation page updated with §474. Seeds 100000000–100000999 and smokes 74070450–74070451
are used.

## §465 — Silver AZ MLP prior generation 4: 10k teacher, offline orig CE 1.2192 → 1.2103; a bigger net is not worth its cost (2026-10-14)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-13 22:04Z, "if the bigger net doesn't give us anything, do a stronger teacher for
10k sims"):** after §460 showed no measurable gain from gen 1 to gen 3, does a larger net or a stronger self-play
teacher move the prior?
**Design:** first an offline net-size check on the gen-3 window (fold-3 validation CE). Then generation 4 as in §460
but with a 10k flat exact Silver teacher: frozen brief and worker (main `f73e6ad7`, binary `b4586cfc…`, gen-3 prior,
K = 8, weight 400, root bonus off), 1,024 A0 runs on 4 cloud workers, warm-started 128/64 training on the window
orig + x5 + g2 + g3 + g4 with arms written down before the data. Offline monitors only.
**Result: generation 4 passes every monitor; the gain is the largest so far.**
- Net size on the gen-3 window: 512/256 1.2838 vs 128/64 1.2869 at 4.5x native cost per root (28.5 vs 6.4 µs).
  Judged not worth it, so the 10k teacher ran.
- Self-play: 255/256 units, 400,128 roots. Unit natural-91000228 was lost: seed 91000228 looped forever in
  `SilverSearcher::rolloutToEnd` (draw/shuffle; not covered by the #522 decision loop guard), killed after 1 h 40 min,
  not rerun.
- Training window 2,124,899 roots. Run B (40 epochs, patience 8, LR halving) 1.2678 vs A (2 passes) 1.2730; B is gen 4.

| fold-4 monitor | gen 3 | gen 4 |
|---|---|---|
| orig (plain 10k teacher) CE / top-1 | 1.2192 / 56.8% | **1.2103** / 57.2% |
| g4 held-out self-play | 1.2148 | 1.2052 |
| x5 | 1.2420 | 1.2363 |
| mean TV vs previous generation | 0.036 | 0.041 |

- Native parity max |logit diff| 1.3e-6; same 128/64 cost.
- Net sizes on the gen-4 window, from scratch (validation CE; µs per root): 32/16 1.3123 (3.4), 64/32 1.2891 (4.7),
  128/64 1.2718 (8.8), 512/256 1.2616 (29.8); warm-started gen 4 1.2678.

**Interpretation:**
- The per-generation orig CE change went from −0.0008 and −0.0004 (2k teacher) to −0.0089 with the 10k teacher.
  **Inference:** teacher strength, not more iterations at 2k, is what moves this prior.
- Play strength of gen 4 was not measured online (PLAN changed to offline gating per generation, Philipp
  2026-10-14 07:40Z); it is **Unverified**.
- The `rolloutToEnd` loop is a native bug, reported separately (GitHub issue).

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/silver_az_mlp_gen4_20261014/README.md). Raw: `/mnt/project-files/silver-az-mlp/gen4/`.
Seeds 91000000–91000511 and 91001000–91001511 are now used.

**Knowledge impact:** covered by the sentence for §465, §477 and §478 in `architecture/combat-search.md`.

g2–g5. Arms written before training, all warm-started from gen 4: A 2 passes, B the gen-4 recipe (dropout 0.35),

## §478 — Silver AZ MLP prior generation 6: 40k teacher; recipe now matters more than data; embedding net E chosen (2026-10-14)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-14 11:14Z, "Yeh let's do gen 6 with 40k"):** generation 6 with a 40k teacher, gated
offline as §477.
**Design:** as §477 with a 40k teacher and the gen-5 prior (worker: gdb backtrace and kill after 7,200 s), seeds
97000000–97000511 and 97001000–97001511, 8 workers. Window orig + x5 + g3–g6 (2,531,313 roots). Arms written before
the data: A/B/C as §477, warm-started from gen 5 on CPU. Arm D was added before any gen-6 data arrived, from the
net-architecture sweep (`silver_prior_arch_20261014`): 128/64 from scratch, dropout 0.15, cosine LR 1e-3, 25 epochs,
target 0.5 visit shares + 0.5 softmax of a 512/256 teacher net trained on the same pack. On Philipp's request the
teacher and D ran on his GPU (about 20x faster than 4 CPU cores), together with the offline-only embedding arms E
(encounter + monster id + monster incoming damage tables) and Eenc (encounter only), which need the v2 loader (#541).
Selection among the current-format arms: lowest fold-3 validation CE.
**Result: 256/256 units, 407,179 roots, no stalls. Gate PASS with D; Philipp chose E (17:13Z, "yes switch to E").**

| arm | validation CE | orig fold-4 CE | all fold-4 CE | TV vs gen 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gen 5 | 1.2128 | 1.1954 | 1.2091 | 0 |
| A | 1.2104 | 1.1927 | 1.2072 | 0.045 |
| B (dropout 0.35) | 1.2135 | 1.1964 | 1.2104 | 0.055 |
| C (dropout 0.15) | 1.2056 | 1.1877 | 1.2026 | 0.064 |
| D (distilled, cosine) | 1.2029 | 1.1831 | 1.1982 | 0.078 |
| teacher 512/256 | 1.2044 | 1.1852 | 1.2012 | |
| **E (enc + monster tables), gen 6** | **1.1937** | **1.1749** | **1.1905** | |
| Eenc (enc table) | 1.1955 | 1.1769 | 1.1929 | |

- All rows evaluated on the same pack and splits; teacher, E and Eenc by the training script, which reproduces D's
  values exactly. Native parity: D 2.3e-6; E 2.4e-6 (v2 export, #541). Same per-root cost within noise.
- Each arm is a single seed.

**Interpretation:**
- B, the recipe of gens 4 and 5, no longer improves on gen 5 (+0.0010 orig). **Inference:** at this point the
  training recipe (distillation, cosine schedule, encounter and monster embeddings) moves the prior more than another
  generation of stronger-teacher data.
- Gen 6 is E (`combat_policy_mlp_v2`); it loads only in binaries built from main `531db3e3` or later. D stays as the
  current-format fallback.
- No online evaluation since §460 (gen 3); whether gens 4–6 play better is **Unverified**.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/silver_az_mlp_gen6_20261014/README.md). Raw and models:
`/mnt/project-files/silver-az-mlp/gen6/`; pack on branch `claude/silver-gen6-gpu-data` (never merged). Seeds
97000000–97000511 and 97001000–97001511 are now used.

## §473 — Silver Smoke Bomb escape penalty 12,35 vs escape scored as a win: NOT_SHOWN at A0 and A20 (2026-10-14)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-14 15:26Z, after the default-off flag audit):** "5 können wir gerne testen". Silver
scores a Smoke Bomb escape like a win although the escape forfeits the fight's rewards. Does charging them
(`STS_SILVER_ESCAPE_PENALTY=12,35`, normal and elite-trigger fights, capped at half the HP left) play better whole
runs?
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/silver_escape_penalty_473_20261014/PREREG.md), committed before any cohort seed ran
(code `e221fcac`, binary `bafcdf80…`, run commit `ef53c823`, 8 cloud workers). Both arms are the §422/§433 `off`
stack (exact-10k live Silver, V4 OOC policy, OOC MCTS off) on the ADR-0034 defaults; `base` sets `0,0`, `escape`
sets `12,35`. The values were fixed from Silver's own weights, not tuned. Fresh seeds: A0 102000000–102000499, A20
102000500–102000999. Primary: A0 Δwin, A20 Δfloor, paired seed bootstrap (10,000 resamples); BETTER / WORSE /
NOT_SHOWN.
**Precondition found while preparing:** before PR #540, `one_combat` rejected any `STS_SILVER_ESCAPE_PENALTY` value at
startup because the name was missing from its accepted `STS_SILVER_*` list, so no earlier `one_combat` run can have used the
penalty. PR #540 (`e221fcac`) accepts it; the first smoke failed with rc=2 before that fix.
**Result: NOT_SHOWN in both cohorts.** 500/500 pairs valid per cohort, all 2,000 units rc=0, no dropped seed, no
stall. All 8 worker tars were verified against their DONE hashes and frozen provenance from a second container.

| | A0 base | A0 escape | A20 base | A20 escape |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| wins / 500 | 414 | 414 | 67 | 66 |
| Δwin (escape − base) | | 0.0 pp [−1.0, +1.0]; 3 vs 3 discordant, McNemar p = 1.0 | | −0.2 pp [−1.0, +0.4]; 1 vs 2 discordant, p = 1.0 |
| mean floor | 49.59 | 49.57 | 36.11 | 36.13 |
| Δfloor | | −0.018 [−0.128, +0.088] | | +0.024 [−0.168, +0.234] |
| boss deaths | 67 | 66 | 257 | 256 |
| reached floor 50 | 459 | 458 | 209 | 209 |
| seconds per run | 58.4 | 58.2 | 38.9 | 38.8 |
| pairs whose rows differ at all | | 46 | | 21 |

**Interpretation:**
- No effect is detectable. The penalty changes a run only after an escape decision; 46 of 500 A0 pairs and 21 of 500
  A20 pairs differ at all, and among them wins and floors move both ways. The intervals are much narrower than the
  prereg's power estimate because most pairs are identical, so they bound the average effect over all runs, not the
  effect on runs that hold a Smoke Bomb. Escape counts per arm were not measured. No CPU difference.
- Per the prereg decision rule, Philipp decides on principle whether `12,35` becomes the default; the values are not
  tuned further on these seeds. Until then the default stays `0,0`.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/silver_escape_penalty_473_20261014/PREREG.md), analyzer
`tools/analyze_silver_escape_473.py`. Raw: `/mnt/project-files/silver-escape-473/` (one tar and DONE file per
worker). Seeds 102000000–102000999 and smokes 74070750–74070767 are now used.

root bonus on), 2 replicates each on a shared combat-RNG redraw. Fresh seeds 104000000–104000095, one cloud
container. §460 fight score, paired per fight, bootstrap over seeds. Primary: `mlp<b> − plain<b>` (G6_HELPS /

no multiplicity correction. Every arm used the legacy Silver terminal score (the run predates ADR-0035).

budgets.** 1,080 of 1,088 fights valid (8 with escape-quarantined or control-state-invalid rows); 96/96 seeds, all
shards rc 0, no stall. Fights: 194 boss, 510 elite, 339 normal, 37 event.

  +4.6 pp [+0.5, +8.9], HP lost −2.32 [−4.00, −0.73]), +4.78 [−3.78, +13.46] at 625. Boss win rate per replicate:
  plain 75.5 / 70.9 / 70.9%, gen 6 76.0 / 75.5 / 71.6%, gen 5 75.3 / 74.2 / 73.5% at 10k / 2.5k / 625 (control
  77.8%). Boss fights contribute about 0.58 of +0.73 (10k), 2.87 of +3.85 (2.5k) and 0.86 of +2.56 (625) to the
  all-fight gen6 − plain score; at 625 elites contribute about 1.48 (+3.14 [−0.09, +6.15]). Among the prior − plain
  and gen6 − gen5 score contrasts, no elite or normal CI excludes 0 except gen5 − plain elite at 625 (+3.47
  [+0.59, +6.59]); the budget contrasts and some win-rate contrasts do.
- Mean win rate per fight: plain 93.0 / 92.1 / 91.5%, gen 6 93.0 / 93.1 / 92.0%, gen 5 92.8 / 92.7 / 92.4%.
- CPU per fight vs plain at the same budget: gen 6 1.046x / 1.040x / 1.045x, gen 5 1.038x / 1.044x / 1.051x; plain
  at 10k 2.72 s, 2.5k 0.62 s, 625 0.15 s per fight. Contrasts are at equal simulations, not equal CPU.

**Interpretation:**
- At A20 the gen-6 prior helps plain Silver at reduced budgets. At 2,500 it is not distinguishable from plain
  10,000 (+1.04 [−1.43, +3.46]; equivalence was not tested, and the CI is as wide as the plain 2.5k − 10k gap of
  −2.81) at about 0.24x the CPU per fight; gen 5 shows the same pattern at 2,500 (+2.51 vs plain 2.5k). At 2,500 the
  gain sits mainly in boss fights, as at A0 (§460); at 625 it is spread over bosses and elites.
  **Inference:** a strong prior substitutes for simulations; at 10,000 the search no longer needs it, so an effect
  there, if any, is below this design's resolution (±2.2 score).
- Gen 6 is not shown better than gen 5 in play, at any budget, despite the offline CE gain; at 625 the point estimate
  favours gen 5. **Open question:** whether the offline gains of gens 4–6 transfer to play at all; no fight-level
  comparison against gen 3 or gen 4 has been run.
- `NOT_SHOWN` at about 1,000 A20 fights means inconclusive, not "no effect". Six labels at 95% without correction;
  both HELPS CIs exclude 0 (the 625 one narrowly, lower bound +0.40) and agree with gen 5's vs plain, so they are not
  a single borderline result.
- Fight score and per-fight win rate, not run win rate: the run-level effect of a lower combat budget with the prior
  is **Unverified**. The source policy is A0-trained, so the fight mix is where that policy reaches at A20. No default
  changes; the MLP prior stays opt-in.
