## §479 — Silver leaf rollouts: uniform random WORSE, learned card table and rollouts per leaf not shown better, at A20 fight level (2026-10-15)

**Question:** can Silver's leaf rollout be made cheaper or better than the greedy `SilverRolloutAgent` playout?
Philipp asked whether random rollouts save CPU, with and without the gen-6 tree prior (2026-10-14 21:24Z, "no prior
in the rollouts"), then for any improvement on the greedy rollout (card "Both": a learned card-play table and
several rollouts per leaf). Pre-registration:
[`PREREG.md`](evidence/silver_rollout_policy_2x2_20261014/PREREG.md); 8 workers and the two 10k uniform arms dropped
by Philipp (2026-10-15 06:44Z).

**Design:** `ctmsilvergen` armset `rollout479` at A20 (code `7a413622`, base main `2195b648`, ADR-0035/0036
defaults). 64 source runs (seeds 105000000–105000063, plain Silver 10k); all boss, elite and event fights plus one
normal fight in three replayed from the same pre-fight states with R = 2 combat-RNG redraws per arm, every arm in the
same process. The source run and control use production rollouts; each arm's replays set its rollout config through
a per-thread override. Arms, each without and with the gen-6 tree prior (K = 8): greedy at 2,500 and 10,000
simulations; uniform random playouts at 2,500; 2 greedy playouts per leaf at 1,250 and 4 at 625 (the same playouts
per decision as 1 × 2,500); greedy with a card-play table fitted offline to gen-6 Silver choices at 2,500. Fight
score 0 on death, else 53 + HP + 11·potions + 0.25·gold + 2·maxHP; paired 95% bootstrap over source seeds. Frozen
pre-registration: [`PREREG.md` at run commit `df88c0f4`](https://github.com/pherrman1/sts_ai/blob/df88c0f4bbb2e6566b15ff9662c3c79da12e6962/docs/experiments/evidence/silver_rollout_policy_2x2_20261014/PREREG.md).

**Result:** 689 valid fights (125 boss, 334 elite, 206 normal, 24 event); 14 excluded (7 escapes; 7 control-replay
mismatches on act-3 bosses: 4 Time Eater, 2 Awakened One, 1 Donu and Deca, seeds 105000025, 031, 036, 049, 050, 054,
056). Replaying those 7 seeds with main's binary (`2195b648`, §476 `mlpsweep` armset) gives the same 7 control
mismatches with the same outcome and HP, so they predate this change. Fewer fights per seed than in the smoke, so 689 instead of ~1,000.

| Contrast (fight score) | Δ score [95% CI] | Δ win pp | Δ HP lost | CPU per fight | Label |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| uniform 2.5k − greedy 2.5k | −22.80 [−27.87, −18.18] | −5.7 [−7.5, −4.1] | +4.84 [+4.02, +5.69] | 0.92x | UNIFORM_HURTS |
| table 2.5k − greedy 2.5k | +0.33 [−2.28, +2.81] | −0.3 [−1.2, +0.6] | −0.48 [−1.02, +0.03] | 0.89x | NOT_SHOWN |
| 2 per leaf 1,250 − greedy 2.5k | −1.10 [−3.64, +1.54] | −0.4 [−1.2, +0.5] | +0.40 [−0.15, +0.93] | 0.76x | NOT_SHOWN |
| 4 per leaf 625 − greedy 2.5k | −4.19 [−7.21, −1.46] | −1.2 [−2.2, −0.2] | +1.19 [+0.59, +1.79] | 0.58x | PERLEAF4_HURTS |

- CPU per simulation vs greedy 2.5k: uniform 1.02x [0.97, 1.08], table 0.92x [0.90, 0.93], 2 per leaf 1.52x, 4 per
  leaf 2.27x. Mean playout length: greedy 13.6 actions, uniform 10.1, table 11.7. Greedy 2.5k: 1.18 s per fight for both
  replicates (0.59 s per replicate), 12.5 µs per simulation.
- Uniform loses most in boss fights (−52.5 [−69.8, −35.7], win −16.8 pp) and elites (−21.6); normal −8.4.
- Descriptive (no label): gen 6 − plain +1.67 [−0.72, +3.94] at 2.5k and +3.33 [+1.29, +5.55] at 10k (boss +9.59
  [+1.62, +17.93]); gen 6 with uniform playouts − plain uniform +3.81 [+0.31, +7.76], still −20.66 below gen 6 with
  greedy; table with gen 6 − gen 6 −0.77 [−3.32, +2.09]; 2 per leaf with gen 6 at 1,250 − gen 6 2.5k −1.98 [−3.81,
  −0.21]; 4 per leaf with gen 6 at 625 −3.29 [−5.85, −0.75]; greedy 2.5k − 10k −0.68 [−3.13, +1.87].

**Decision rules (pre-registered):** uniform `UNIFORM_HURTS` and no CPU saving per simulation (1.02x [0.97, 1.08]; per fight 0.92x [0.87, 0.97]) → greedy stays (negative). Table
`NOT_SHOWN` → no follow-up on this table. 2 per leaf `NOT_SHOWN` with per-fight CPU ratio upper bound 0.78 ≤ 0.8 but
score lower bound −3.64 < −1.0 → no follow-up. 4 per leaf `PERLEAF4_HURTS` → no follow-up. No default changes; the
`STS_SILVER_ROLLOUT_*` options stay research-only and off.

**Interpretation:**
- Uniform random playouts save no CPU per simulation in this engine (per fight 0.92x [0.87, 0.97]),
  although they are 26% shorter. **Inference:** each uniform step enumerates every legal action, which costs about what
  the shorter playout saves. A uniformly random continuation is a much worse value estimate,
  above all in boss fights. The gen-6 tree prior recovers only a small part (+3.8) of the loss. This agrees with §441
  (uniform OOC rollouts −7.8 pp).
- The learned table plays 14% shorter playouts and is 11% cheaper per fight, with no score change shown; a gain of
  more than about +2.8 is excluded at this resolution. **Inference:** the greedy priority list is close enough to the
  gen-6 move choices that matter for leaf values.
- Averaging several greedy playouts per leaf does not buy back the lost tree simulations: at 4 per leaf it is worse,
  at 2 per leaf the CI still allows a loss of 3.6. **Inference:** in Silver, tree depth matters more than leaf-value
  variance at these budgets.
- Four labels at 95% without correction; the two HURTS CIs are far from 0 (uniform) or clear of it (4 per leaf,
  upper −1.46). The gen-6 effect at 10k (+3.33) differs from §476 (+0.73 n.s.) but is descriptive here; fight score
  and per-fight wins, not run wins.

**Evidence:** [packet](evidence/silver_rollout_policy_2x2_20261014/README.md),
[`analysis.json`](evidence/silver_rollout_policy_2x2_20261014/analysis.json). Raw:
`/mnt/project-files/silver-rollout-2x2/w01.tar` … `w08.tar` (sha256 in the packet, checked from the lead container).
Seeds 105000000–105000063, smokes 74071450–74071495 and reviewer seeds 74071550–74071551 are now used.

**Knowledge impact:** `architecture/combat-search.md` (leaf rollouts) and `operations/environment-variables.md` list
the three research options and the §479 result.

## §486 OOC MCTS with heart1 vs V4 as the tree prior at A20 (2026-10-15)

**Verdict:** primary (A20 floors) `NOT_SHOWN`, −0.09 [−3.64, +3.23]; key secondary (act-3 clears) `IMPROVED`,
25 vs 10 of 64, +23.4 pp [+9.4, +37.5], McNemar p = 0.0026 (19 vs 4 discordant pairs). Per the pre-registered rule
this is reported as such and the decision is Philipp's; no default change.
[Pre-registration](evidence/heart1_ooc_ab_486_20261015/PREREG.md), [report](evidence/heart1_ooc_ab_486_20261015/report.json).

Philipp asked for the comparison (09:12Z, 10:08Z) and chose A20 only, 64 seeds, 32 workers on the cost card
(11:57Z). Both arms: §433 `combo` OOC MCTS with the automatic A20 CTM (ADR-0033), chain rollouts
(`STS_OOC_MCTS_LEAF_POLICY=v4`), run-commit defaults (ADR-0030..0040). The `heart1` arm uses silverbot's released PPO
policy (`heart1.bin` `1e92f2a6…`) as the tree prior (`STS_OOC_MCTS_PRIOR=heart1`), the `v4` arm the V4 prior. Run
commit `3f8acc98`, code `d094e012`, binary `7fa2a7e9…`; seeds 107000000–107000063, one unit per seed and arm. The
pre-launch review caught that at the first run commit (`ec19d1e`) the tree's skip-card-reward primitive had no heart1
token, so every node with a card reward kept V4 (about 20% of sampled reward nodes at A0, nearly all at A20 in a
probe); `d094e012` maps it (and gold and potion discards), and the act-1 coverage smoke and the run both show heart1
scoring 100% of prior builds (6.82M, 0 fallbacks).

All 128 units rc=0, no dropped seeds, all 32 worker tars verified from the lead container (`worker_tars.txt`).
Reached act 3: 42 (heart1) vs 43 (v4); clears given act 3 reached 59.5% vs 23.3%; boss deaths 23 vs 38; deaths by
act 1/2/3: 4/18/17 vs 2/19/33; end HP +12.8 per pair. Mean floor 42.27 vs 42.36: with the act-3 stop a clear and an
act-3 boss death end on nearly the same floor, so floors barely register the clears. Cost: 4,310 vs 494 s per run
(8.7x; MCTS CPU 4,170 vs 430 s), about 85 core-h in all; the heart1 forward pass dominates.

**Interpretation (Inference):** heart1's prior changes what the search builds toward rather than how far early runs
get: similar act-1/2 survival, many more act-3 boss kills. 64 seeds and one secondary endpoint; the clear effect is
large but not yet replicated, and the floor endpoint chosen as primary was a poor fit for an act-3-stop run.
A0 (107001000–127, reserved) was not run. Cost makes the heart1 prior impractical as is; a distilled fast prior is
being investigated separately.

**Knowledge impact:** `docs/knowledge-base/architecture/out-of-combat.md` (heart1 prior result line).

## §487 OOC MCTS with the V4 policy inside the rollouts at A20 (2026-10-15)

**Verdict:** primary (A20 act-3 clears) `NOT_SHOWN`, 12 vs 10 of 64, +3.1 pp [−9.4, +15.6], McNemar p = 0.81
(10 vs 8 discordant pairs); key secondary (floors) `WORSE`, −5.70 [−9.33, −2.17]. The chain rollouts stay; no
default change.
[Pre-registration](evidence/v4_rollout_policy_487_20261015/PREREG.md), [report](evidence/v4_rollout_policy_487_20261015/report.json).

Philipp asked (16:19Z) for the §486 seeds with the V4 prior also used inside the rollouts, on 32 workers. Both arms
are the §486 `v4` arm (§433 `combo` with the automatic A20 CTM, V4 tree prior, run-commit defaults ADR-0030..0040);
`v4roll` adds `STS_OOC_MCTS_LEAF_POLICY=prior` (new, default off): at each non-combat rollout step the tree's fixed
rule steps run first, then V4's policy-head argmax decides every screen V4 encodes (card rewards, map except the boss
row, shops, rest, upgrades, events except Match and Keep, treasure, boss relics); the chain decides the rest. Before,
rollouts used the chain: heuristics with V4 Q-head one-ply gates at margin 1.0, and the room-value map heuristic. Run
commit `9f1ae0f8`, code `8ffa30a9`, binary `2779f937…`; seeds 107000000–107000063, one unit per seed and arm;
independent pre-launch review PASS.

All 128 units rc=0, no dropped seeds, all 32 worker tars verified from the lead container (`worker_tars.txt`). The
control reproduces the §486 `v4` rows on 64/64 seeds (won, floor, act, end HP), so the option leaves the chain
rollouts unchanged. `v4roll` took about 1.67M V4 rollout steps per run. Reached act 3: 29 (v4roll) vs 43 (v4);
clears given act 3 reached 41.4% vs 23.3%; deaths by act 1/2/3: 5/30/17 vs 2/19/33; boss deaths 27 vs 38; end HP
−1.5 per pair. Cost: 339 vs 462 s per run (MCTS CPU 286 vs 403 s): about half from fewer MCTS-owned decisions per run (76 vs 90,
shorter runs) and half from cheaper decisions (MCTS CPU per MCTS-owned decision 3.74 vs 4.50 s, about 17% less).

**Interpretation (Inference):** greedy V4 policy-head rollouts make the search build differently: many more runs die
in act 2. Clears given act 3 reached are 41.4% vs 23.3%, but on different subsets of seeds (29 vs 43), so this is
not a paired effect. The clear difference is small and not separated; the floor loss is clear. Whether sampling from the prior instead of argmax, or V4 on fewer screens (for example without
the map, where V4 gating lost in §91/§93/§100), would do better is an **Open question**; the per-screen effect was
not measured.

**Knowledge impact:** `docs/knowledge-base/architecture/out-of-combat.md` (`LEAF_POLICY=prior` and the §487 result
line).

agreement with heart1 is the lowest, about 87%) is an **Open question**.

## §489 Sibling OOC MCTS leaves: learned leaf values vs rollout3 at A20 (2026-10-15)

**Verdict:** descriptive offline measurement, no gameplay A/B. Within parent nodes, correlations with the expected
rollout3 return (noise-corrected) are: one rollout3 0.24, X2-B at the leaf 0.57, heart1's value head 0.30
(0.56 on card-reward parents, where X2-B is 0.18), and the mean of 4 rollout5 evaluations 0.34. A small CPU value net
trained on 8-rollout means reached 0.56 vs X2-B 0.53 on held-out seeds. No learned leaf is promoted, nothing is trained on the GPU, no
default changes. [Evidence](evidence/ooc_sibling_leaf_capture_20261015/README.md).

Philipp asked (18:03–18:09Z) for an offline test of a model that "distills rollout3 without having to do rollout3",
with GPU use only after asking him. New default-off option `STS_OOC_SIBLING_CAPTURE` writes tree leaves (depth ≤ 2,
≤ 256 per root, every 4th searched decision) with their parent node and action, the search's own rollout3 value and,
from a forked child (play unchanged: smoke 74072220 trace and action log byte-identical with capture on/off), 8
repeat rollout3 and 4 rollout5 evaluations on fresh RNG, X2-B at the leaf and heart1's value and record. Stack: §486
`v4` arm (§433 `combo`, V4 prior, automatic A20 CTM, 4096 simulations). Run commit `8df8b9b7`, binary `6eded1e2…`;
seeds 109000000–063 (A20; 16 lead container, 48 on 8 workers on Philipp's word, pre-launch review PASS); all 64 units
rc=0, tars verified from the lead container; 221k leaves.

Metric: within each parent, demean leaf values; signal variance of E[rollout3] = var(T) − mean SE(T)², with T the mean
of the 8 repeats; corr(c, E[rollout3]) = cov(c, T)/sqrt(var(c)·signal). Signal is only 33% of within-parent var(T).
By parent screen (X2-B / heart1 / one rollout3): map 0.57 / 0.32 / 0.26 (157k leaves), event 0.71 / 0.31 / 0.22,
rewards 0.18 / 0.56 / 0.22, shop 0.46 / 0.27 / 0.18, boss relic 0.52 / 0.27 / 0.28. Two independent single rollout3
evaluations order a sibling pair the same way 53% of the time (smoke). Held out (seeds % 4 == 3, 59.6k leaves): linear
X2-B + heart1 blend 0.556 vs X2-B 0.534; CPU net (deck/relic/potion/offer bags, fixed observation, rooms ahead, X2-B
logit; within-parent loss, 12 fixed epochs) 0.561 at the last epoch, 0.539–0.561 over epochs 6–12 (`tv_within_x2b.log`).
An earlier plain-MSE run of the same net on a 46-seed subset (different held-out set) stayed at 0.47–0.51 over epochs
4–15. About 71% of within-parent leaf pairs are chance outcomes of the same action; at the action level (per-action
means) every candidate sits near 0.53–0.56 pair concordance (`metrics64.json`). heart1 encodes 99.5% of leaves; its
score uses only parents whose leaves are all encoded. Capture cost is not measured reliably (smoke +43% wall time with 1 repeat + 1 rollout5; the
reviewer saw 2.2x on shared cores).

**Interpretation (Inference):** one X2-B call carries about as much sibling-ranking information as the mean of 8
rollout3 calls (the mean of n independent rollouts with single-call correlation ρ = 0.24 has correlation
sqrt(n·ρ²/(1+(n−1)·ρ²)), which equals 0.57 at n ≈ 7.8), but it is a fixed estimate, while averaged rollouts converge; with thousands of simulations the
search averages enough to pass it, consistent with §472/§475 (rollout0 −10 to −12 pp). rollout3 itself ends in X2-B,
which flatters X2-B here. heart1's value head is a weak target outside card rewards, so fine-tuning the distilled
students on it is not justified. A net trained on 8-rollout means gained little over X2-B (0.561 vs 0.534); label
noise (signal share 0.33) is one plausible limit, untested against features, architecture or data size (one net, about
5k training parents). Rollout3 is not
ground truth either (Philipp); comparisons to it say nothing about true win probability.

**Knowledge impact:** `docs/knowledge-base/architecture/out-of-combat.md` and
`docs/knowledge-base/operations/environment-variables.md` (the capture option).

## §490 CPU value net on 64-rollout leaf labels vs X2-B at A20 (2026-10-15)

**Verdict:** descriptive offline measurement, no gameplay A/B. With 64 rollout3 evaluations per leaf as labels, the
§489 CPU value net with X2-B as an input reaches a within-parent correlation with the expected rollout3 return of
0.645 at the last of 20 epochs (0.624–0.659 over epochs 5–20) on held-out seeds, vs X2-B 0.596, one rollout3 0.238 and
heart1's value head 0.354. Without the X2-B input the net reaches 0.570 (0.492–0.577). No learned leaf is promoted
or ported; no default changes. Philipp closed this line here and continues it in Codex.
[Evidence](evidence/ooc_sibling_leaf_capture64_20261015/README.md).

Capture: `STS_OOC_SIBLING_CAPTURE` as in §489 with every 2nd searched decision, ≤ 128 leaves per root, depth ≤ 2,
64 repeat rollout3 per leaf, no rollout5, heart1 annotation; option cap for `_REPEATS` raised from 16 to 256 (capture
only). Stack: §486 `v4` arm. Run commit `12b7a055`, binary `992f5cdc…`; seeds 110000000–063 (A20), 32 workers × 2
seeds on Philipp's word, pre-launch review PASS; smoke 74072240 (rc=0, 2,440 leaves all with 64 repeats); all 64 units
rc=0, tars verified from the lead container; 225k leaves; unit wall time 7–41 min (median 21).

Metric as §489 (`sib_signal.py`). Signal is 80% of within-parent var(T) (33% with §489's 8 repeats). All 64 seeds
(X2-B / heart1 / one rollout3): 0.56 / 0.36 / 0.24, matching §489. Held out (seeds % 4 == 3, 57.0k leaves), the epoch with the best
held-out correlation (epoch 10, selected on the held-out seeds), net with X2-B vs X2-B by parent screen: map 0.67 vs 0.61 (38k leaves), card rewards 0.72 vs 0.19 (heart1 0.57), event
0.54 vs 0.54, shop 0.51 vs 0.48, rest 0.75 vs 0.82, boss relic 0.60 vs 0.58. Same net and training script as §489
(selection bug fixed there): bags of deck/relic/potion/offer tokens, fixed observation, rooms ahead, X2-B logit;
within-parent loss; seed 0; training is deterministic (a repeat run reproduced the no-X2-B log exactly).

**Interpretation (Inference):** by §489's formula, the net's 0.645 matches the mean of about 12 independent rollout3
calls, X2-B's 0.596 about 9; the gain over X2-B comes mostly from card-reward parents, where X2-B barely ranks
siblings. The fresh 64-label corpus produced 0.645 versus 0.561 in §489 (8-label corpus); the label-count effect
was not isolated from the new source seeds and capture sampling. Whether more data, features or a larger net move
it further is untested. The held-out ranking says nothing yet about play: a C++ port and a paired
run with the net as (or blended into) the OOC MCTS leaf are needed, and the net's per-call cost is not measured.
Rollout3 itself ends in X2-B and is not ground truth (Philipp).

**Knowledge impact:** `docs/knowledge-base/architecture/out-of-combat.md` (result line) and
`docs/knowledge-base/operations/environment-variables.md` (`_REPEATS` cap).

[frozen protocol](evidence/heart_rollout_distill_20261016/PROTOCOL.md),
[machine-readable classification](evidence/heart_rollout_distill_20261016/result.json).

Frozen source `cbded890a06f4ec76ad72c8333d07df25ad54e5f` follows the user's
clarification: distilled heart1 **Arm C as tree prior only**, V4 rollout chain
held fixed. A20 Ironclad collects keys and targets the Heart after separate
PR #562. Exact-10k native Silver real combat, calibrated A20 CTM, OOC source
budget 512, rollout3, every fourth searched decision, at most 64 captured leaves
at depth one, and 64 repeat returns per leaf. These are surrogate targets,
not observed Heart-win probabilities. No AlphaZero-style learning loop.

Canaries `110159994/995` passed exact capture-off/on decision/action parity and
347/347 plus 528/528 valid rows (14/22 complete multi-action groups). Independent
source/design and canary/custody reviews passed before cohort analysis. All
64 sources `110161000..063` returned zero in 2,751.97 seconds of collection wall
time on three local workers. Every source's attempted model-prior calls were
scored by Arm C, with zero fallback and zero prior-leaf steps. Its exact native
hash is pinned in the freeze. Historical Opus §490 is an out-of-domain reference
only; its raw cloud corpus was unavailable. No historical data was pooled.

TRAIN (`..000..039`): 18,009 accepted rows, 656 groups, all 40 sources.
VALIDATION (`..040..047`): 3,847 accepted rows, 122 groups, all 8 sources.
Both retained 100% of captured rows. Counts/pooling/attention, two initializations
each, completed 180 total epochs in 144.24 seconds on the local RTX 3060 Ti.
Validation selected the count MLP (849,281 parameters, 6,504 input features),
initialization 0, epoch 22, blended 50/50 with X2-B.

**Validation-only selection evidence:** source-mean MSE 0.019057 versus X2-B
0.039653, per-action concordance 0.681960 versus 0.647172, and regret 0.021319
versus 0.023182. These eight sources selected the model/epoch/blend; they are
not untouched TEST. They establish neither encoding superiority nor a passing
candidate. The selected checkpoint and vocabulary custody are preserved.

The evaluator reused `a` for per-source baseline metrics, overwriting the token
attribute tensor. Its latency warmup then raised `KeyError: slice(None, 1,
None)` after TEST opening. The frozen bundle remains unchanged. A repository-only
name repair gives the tensor and metrics distinct names; a synthetic end-to-end
regression reproduces the original failure, passes after the repair, and checks
that reopening is rejected before another data load. All 18 Python tests pass.
The repair is for future invocations; it does not recover or rerun this TEST.

Earlier attempts remain preserved: v1 failed its support canary before any
cohort, exposing unresolved BATTLE and Match and Keep record gaps. The leaf-only

potion type. [Pre-registration](evidence/potion_price_probe_20261017/PREREG.md), independent pre-launch
review PASS. New research mode `potionpriceprobe` at `5dfabf90`. Each A20 source run (exact-10k Silver,
V4 OOC policy, OOC MCTS off) samples up to 8 battle-start states that hold potions. Paired copies of each
state share all RNG and the policy state: unchanged, one per held potion type with that potion removed,
and HP −12. Each copy plays the next 3 fights, then the A20 floor model values it. Seeds
111110000–111110999 on two cloud containers, 3 h each: 498 seeds ran, the unstarted rest stay unused.
3,550 states, 5,220 potion rows, 0 invalid, 7 terminal states dropped.

Primary (A20 floor model): 1 HP = 0.092 floors [0.074, 0.111]. The pooled potion price is **9.9 HP-eq
[7.9, 12.3], CONSISTENT_WITH_11**; the §385 range of 2-8 is not excluded (lower bound 7.9). The production
floor model gives 8.6 [6.7, 11.0]. Public X2-B after the same continuation gives 11.2 [8.7, 14.4]. The A20
win model gives 16.6 [12.0, 23.4]. Per type (descriptive; 26 of 33 types with n ≥ 100): Fairy 44 [33, 58];
Attack 21, Blood 18, Skill 15, Fear 14 and Power 13 (CIs above 0). Weak, Block, Speed, Swift, Essence of
Steel and Liquid Bronze price near 0 (−6 to +1, with wide CIs).

Post hoc (review): Silver already scores Fairy separately, as 11 + 0.3 × max HP through its death-save
term. Without Fairy (4,916 rows) potions price at 7.8 HP-eq [6.1, 9.8] (production floor model 7.8
[5.8, 10.1], X2-B 8.5 [6.3, 10.9]; A20 win model 10.1 [6.7, 15.0]).
**Inference:** the flat 11 may overprice non-Fairy potions at A20; this split was not pre-registered.
§385's low X2-B prices may have come from static post-fight pricing, since X2-B after play gives 8.5-11
(§385 lives on closed PR #422). Per-type weights are untested in play. No default change. Reproducing
needs `5dfabf90`, since #592 changed Silver rollouts on main (its `STS_SILVER_ROLLOUT_ZERO_COST_CAP=0`
switch is still rejected by `one_combat`'s option allow-list on main).
Seeds 111110000–111110999 and smokes 111119900–111119905 are used; the reviewer reserved 111119950–959.
[Result](evidence/potion_price_probe_20261017/RESULT.md), [analysis.json](evidence/potion_price_probe_20261017/analysis.json).
Raw: `/mnt/project-files/potion-price-probe/ppp-w0{0,1}.tar.gz`.
**Knowledge impact:** potion-weight paragraph in `architecture/combat-search.md`.

**Question:** does the current selected A0 CTM stack reproduce the old
Writhing/Ritual exposure failure? Reviewed source `f2d0dbd3`, actual fast

143 rows / 68 sources, 142 fast + 1 standard. Conditional NLL 0.0033221452,
mixture NLL 0.0033055260, gap -0.0000166192; source-bootstrap 95% interval
[-0.0001389866, 0.0001026931], zero missing masses. Independent result review
recomputed all scores and bootstrap exactly. Native loader parity on synthetic
public inputs passed within 1.67e-6.

TRAIN/VALIDATION census found just three +5 increments in 1,095 TRAIN rows

Awakened budget. These repairs do not qualify models trained on the old
labels; old rows lack the history needed for reliable relabeling.

**ELI5:** the model predicts “the Dagger does not grow” accurately on these
examples, but none shows the Dagger growing. We must verify the label producer
before training it to predict growth.

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-17, thread "Silver leaf evaluation"):** "yes set that up", on testing per-type potion

student C as the OOC policy, **pre-#594 shop rules** (RUN_COMMIT `56e03b29`, based on `da1ce052`; binary

prices shrunk toward 7.8 (3.5 Swift … 12.3 Attack), Fairy and Smoke Bomb 11. Whole runs, so the score is not Silver's

container. Mean floor base 36.65, level 35.85, type 35.28; act-3 clears 36 / 30 / 35 of 128. Type − base Δfloor

## §514 — Fixed OOC rules before and inside the search, with keys on (2026-10-17)

**KEEP_RULES; opt-in potion leave, default off.** Offline count on the 1,408 open §503 A20 runs (TRAIN + VALIDATION,
student C prior `STS_OOC_MCTS_PRIOR=heart1`, keys on; SEALED-confirm not opened). Firings: chest 3,380, reward relic
10,077, gold 30,148, potion pickup 13,158, potion swap by rank 1,452, empty-screen leave 4,439 (key rule 4,778 belongs
to the keys thread). The relic rule matches heart1's own take-free-rewards convention. The 7 reviewed relics went to
search and were left 291 of 760 times. The swap rank dropped a Fairy 4 times.

Every REWARDS root with a "discard potion" candidate had a uniform prior: 1,281 roots in 553 runs. Search discarded
there 505 times and then took the declined reward potion, 455 times a lower-ranked one (mean keep-value loss 1.32 HP-equivalent
per fight over all 505, ADR-0039 units). On the 758 such roots that also offered cards, search left the screen 171 times, forgoing the card reward. A PR #591 (`7fb7933`, heart1full) smoke on 22 seeds per arm (111155002–023, 128 sims)
gives the prior back to discard roots that still offer cards. The remaining "leave or discard" root stays uniform
(10 of 19), with 6 discards. New research option `STS_POTION_REWARD_DECLINE_LEAVE=1` makes the tree rules leave
such a screen. In a 16-seed-per-arm smoke (binary from `b771aa1` plus this change, as committed in `c528115`; seeds 111155024–039), cards-less discard roots went 1 → 0, with 1 vs 1 win;
this is a smoke, not an A/B. **Inference:** the effect is about one slightly worse potion per three runs, too small to
test; the default is Philipp's call. If Sapphire becomes a search decision, the relic rule must stand down while a
Sapphire is offered (keys thread). Seeds 111155000–039 used (000–001 failed at startup, no gameplay).
[Report](evidence/ooc_fixed_rules_20261017/REPORT.md).

## §515 — Heart leaf: TD-fitted tree leaf on §503 rollout tails, VALIDATION gate and CONFIRM (2026-10-17)

**td1 GATE_FAIL (act-3 calibration); retrained td2 CONFIRM_FAIL (act-1 calibration), better BCE
and AUC than X2-B on CONFIRM**, offline, research-only, no default change (issue #605). New
opt-in leaf `STS_OOC_MCTS_LEAF_HEART_MODEL=<manifest>` (requires `STS_OOC_MCTS_LEAF_VALUE=native`):
value = sigmoid(0.799 · margin(public X2-B) + residual), the residual a 204-tree XGBoost margin
model over the rich vector plus Act-4-correct boss distance, keys held and key reachability,
HP fraction, Ritual Dagger damage and Searing Blow level (`heart-leaf-features-v2`). Targets:
fitted TD on 16 live-configured rollout3 tails per root (`one_combat heartleaftail`, salt
111159000; non-terminal ends valued by the previous round), mixed 50/50 with the real Heart
outcome. Rows: 27,114 §503 TRAIN+VALIDATION MAP roots with native snapshots; CONFIRM and §497
TEST unopened.

On VALIDATION (320 runs, run-weighted) against X2-B with a TRAIN Platt map: BCE 0.3065 vs 0.3133
(PASS), AUC 0.724 vs 0.699 (PASS), mean prediction vs Heart rate 0.085/0.103, 0.132/0.119 and
**0.240/0.202 in Act 3** (|Δ| 0.038 > 0.03, FAIL; X2-B Platt 0.090; raw X2-B 0.898). Act 4 (78
roots, not gated) 0.592 vs 0.423. TD rounds 2–3 did not improve VALIDATION BCE. Native parity
2.8e-7; a one-seed A20 Act-1 smoke (111159001) ran cleanly. The key inputs carry ≤ 0.1% of the
gain: **Inference:** §503 has little key-timing variation; the #611 key-flag runs are planned
training data.

Descriptive, for Philipp's question: heart1's value head (`heart1.bin` `1e92f2a6`) on the same
roots ranks within an act better than X2-B (AUC acts 1–4: 0.60, 0.74, 0.78, 0.74 vs 0.56, 0.68,
0.68, 0.65) but pooled only 0.53, because its level barely changes between acts.

Retrain td2 (Philipp: "Retrain, then CONFIRM"; PREREG amendment 2, reviewed at `91bf3e28`): adds
`hlCritic`, a 600-tree regression of the heart1 value head on the same features (schema v3,
evaluated natively), and an Act-4 logit offset (−0.713) from out-of-fold TRAIN, because the
rollout tails overrate Act 4. VALIDATION BCE 0.3038, AUC 0.735, act 3 0.233/0.202. Scored once on
the §503 CONFIRM set (640 runs, 83 Heart kills, 12,458 MAP roots): BCE 0.3345 vs Platt X2-B
0.3479 (paired −0.0134 [−0.0189, −0.0073]), AUC 0.750 vs 0.726, acts 2-3 within 0.023, Act 4
0.438/0.459, but **act 1 0.093/0.130 (|Δ| 0.037 > 0.03, FAIL**; X2-B 0.040). No A/B on td2;
CONFIRM is spent. **Inference:** the act-1 under-prediction is systematic (TRAIN out of fold 0.093
vs 0.136). The §497 TEST stays sealed.
td3 (Philipp, 22:34Z: fix the hidden-queue leak): td2's recipe with feature schema v4, which zeroes the
ADR-0029 hidden queue columns (`nextEliteId`, `nextFight0..2`) the §503 real-game roots carried. VALIDATION BCE
0.3034, AUC 0.731, act 3 0.228/0.202, about td2's numbers (no held-out test left).

## §516 — A20 Silver budget: learned stopping matches flat 10k at 0.41x CPU; gen-6 prior adds Act-4 reaches, not Heart kills (2026-10-17)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-17, thread "Audit performance and throughput"):** "yes set up a20 silver budget test";
card "Add learned+prior"; 16:32Z: "maybe do 512 seeds then on 8 workers." Can learned stopping (ADR-0026) replace
the flat exact 10k Silver budget of the A20 research stack, and does the gen-6 MLP prior (§476) on top change that?
**Design:** [PLAN](evidence/silver_budget_a20_20261017/PLAN.md), pre-launch review PASS. Plain A20 full runs (keys,
Heart objective, no OOC MCTS), student C `policyStep` out of combat, no V4 net loaded. Arms `F` flat exact 10k,
`L` learned stopping, `LP` L + g6_E as root prior (weight 400) and tree prior K=8 (new research flag
`STS_SILVER_TREE_PRIOR_MIN_VISITS`, PR #603). RUN_COMMIT `d83b4ab9` (code main `e413c1f3`, binary `a6ad3c56…`).
Seeds 111135100–111135611. Primary: reached Act 4, paired Newcombe 95% interval, non-inferior if the lower bound
> −5 pp.
**Result.** 1,536/1,536 units rc=0, 512 seeds valid; 8 tars verified from a second container.
- **Heart kills:** F 27, L 30, LP 27 of 512. L − F +0.6 pp [−1.7, +2.9]; LP − F 0.0 [−2.3, +2.3].
- **Reached Act 4 (primary):** F 77, L 75, LP 97.
  - L − F −0.4 pp [−3.4, +2.6], NON_INFERIOR.
  - LP − F +3.9 pp [+0.4, +7.4], McNemar p = 0.035, NON_INFERIOR. The gain is not a pre-registered hypothesis.
- **CPU per run:** F 53.5 s, L 21.9 s (0.41x), LP 28.2 s (0.53x).
- **OOC decisions:** student C 96.6–96.7% in every arm, the key rule 2.6–2.8%, Match and Keep 0.5–0.7% (850
  decisions). Match and Keep's card choices come from the native GBM card-reward fallback (`serverCardRewardPolicy`),
  since no V4 net is loaded; #616 moves them to student C.
**Interpretation:** at A20, learned stopping plays as well as flat 10k on both endpoints at 0.41x the CPU, which
makes it the cheaper Silver budget for student-C self-play. The prior's extra Act-4 reaches did not convert: Heart
kills per Act-4 run were 28% for LP against 35% for F and 40% for L. **Inference:** the prior helps Acts 1–3 combats
but not the Act-4 fights; that needs a targeted check before any claim. Defaults are unchanged (research stacks set
the budget explicitly). Seeds 111135100–111135611 are used; performance-audit smokes used 111135000–111135004.
[Result](evidence/silver_budget_a20_20261017/RESULT.md), [report.json](evidence/silver_budget_a20_20261017/report.json).

## §519 — Silver rollout card table rebuilt per root by the gen-6 prior: NOT_CPU_MATCHED, score NOT_SHOWN (2026-10-17)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-17, thread "Distilled Silver playout picker"):** "we could still do the distilling more
harshely i think. or runt he models once for each root / turn, value all cards and just play the highest value
cards"; 17:04Z: "4 workers, 128 seeds on 4 cores".
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/silver_rollout_root_table_20261017/PREREG.md), independent pre-launch review PASS
(PR #612). New research option `STS_SILVER_ROLLOUT_ROOT_TABLE` (unset = ADR-0040 g6 table): at each searched root the
gen-6 E policy MLP (`ca9bd7f2…`) scores every distinct card in hand, draw and discard once, and the greedy playout
uses those scores as its card table. Fight-level `ctmsilvergen` at A20, armset `roottable`: arms `greedy`/`roottable`
at 2500 and 2650 simulations, R = 2 redraws, hallway every 3rd, §479 score and bootstrap. Source runs use student C
(`eff2f74f…`), keys off (student C still collects keys, so 43 fights are in Act 4). RUN_COMMIT `6d597adc` (code
`0f5e81cf`, binary `aa0e78dd…`), seeds 111158100–111158227. Primary: `roottable2500 − greedy2650` score, label
valid only if the per-fight CPU ratio point estimate is ≤ 1.00.
**Result: NOT_CPU_MATCHED; the score contrast is NOT_SHOWN as well.** 128/128 seeds, 16/16 shards rc=0, 4 tars
verified from a second container; 1,426 valid fights (6 excluded for escapes, 3 control-replay mismatches). Primary
`roottable2500 − greedy2650`: score +1.87 [−0.15, +3.94], win +0.6 pp [−0.1, +1.2]; CPU per fight ratio 1.007
[0.987, 1.027]. The root table costs 5.1% more CPU per simulation (1.051 [1.039, 1.064]; table build plus playouts
of 17.0 vs 15.8 actions), less than the 6% extra simulations at 2650; the CPU miss comes from decisions per fight:
the root-table arm takes 1.4% more search decisions (72,277 vs 71,257), so at equal simulations it costs 1.066x CPU
per fight against 1.059x for greedy2650, hence 1.007. Descriptive, not pre-registered, equal simulations:
`roottable2500 − greedy2500` score +2.69 [+0.61, +4.80], win +0.8 pp [+0.1, +1.6] at 1.066 CPU per fight;
`roottable2650 − greedy2650` +0.92 [−1.00, +2.94]; `greedy2650 − greedy2500` +0.83 [−0.85, +2.49]. Win rates
92.0 / 92.8 / 92.3 / 92.5% (greedy2500 / roottable2500 / greedy2650 / roottable2650). Bosses (269 fights)
`roottable2500 − greedy2650` +5.4 [−2.0, +13.0]; Act 4 (43) +10.2 [−7.7, +28.1].
**Interpretation:** a per-root distilled table is descriptively a better playout picker than the fixed ADR-0040
table at equal simulations (+2.69 [+0.61, +4.80], not pre-registered), but the gain is about the size of what its own CPU overhead would buy as extra simulations, consistent
with §479 (simulations beat playout quality). Pre-registered decision: stop; the option stays research-only and off.
**Inference:** a cheaper build (cache per turn, or fewer scored cards) could turn the equal-sims edge into a CPU-matched
one; not tested.
[result.json](evidence/silver_rollout_root_table_20261017/result.json). Raw:
`/mnt/project-files/silver-rollout-root-table/w0{1..4}.tar` (sha256 `8fb4460d…`, `73428220…`, `991356f1…`,
`e0f75673…`). Seeds used: 111158000–111158024 (smokes) and 111158100–111158227 (run); 111158025–111158099 unused.
The pre-launch reviewer used 111139400–111139411.
**Knowledge impact:** result added to the option's paragraph in `architecture/combat-search.md` and its row in
`operations/environment-variables.md`.

## §518 — Silver chance-node widening per category at A20 (spire-mentor constants): all three labels NOT_SHOWN (2026-10-17)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-17, thread "spire-mentor engine ideas"):** after reading tfriedel/spire-mentor (STS2,
MIT), which uses separate progressive-widening constants for end-of-turn and other chance nodes and reports
+6.35 pp full-run win rate from that: "yes lets try"; 20:01Z: "use the gen6 prior thing with 2.5k simulations and
the 4 arms. then use 8 workers."
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/silver_widening_a20_518_20261017/PREREG.md), independent pre-launch and delta review
PASS (PR #622). Research-only armset `widen518` of fight-level `ctmsilvergen` sets the existing per-arm
`g_nativeSilverSearchParamOverride`; no production path changes. All arms Silver at exact 2,500 simulations with
g6_E (`ca9bd7f2…`) as root prior (weight 400) and tree prior (K = 8): `base2500` both categories C 3.7028,
alpha 0.52389; `endwide2500` end-turn C doubled (7.4056); `othernarrow2500` other chance nodes C 2, alpha 0.5;
`spire2500` othernarrow plus end turn C 5.79, alpha 0.44. A20, sources by plain exact-10k Silver with student C
(`eff2f74f…`) out of combat, keys flag off, `STS_SILVER_LEARNED_STOP=0`, hallway every 3rd, R = 2 redraws paired
across arms, §479 fight score, bootstrap over source seeds. RUN_COMMIT `90133e7e` (code `32bb3552` = main
`14845363` incl. #613, binary `49a3e18a…`), seeds 111180100–111180355, 8 workers × 32.
**Result: NOT_SHOWN on all three labels.** 256/256 sources, 32/32 shards rc=0, 8 tars verified from a second
container; 3,043 valid fights (615 boss, 1,310 elite, 982 normal, 136 event; 108 in Act 4), 14 excluded for
escapes. The 11 control-replay mismatches are all escape fights among those 14. Source 111180117 contributed no
replayed fight. Win rate 93.49 / 93.51 / 93.33 / 93.31% (base / endwide / othernarrow / spire).
- `endwide2500 − base2500`: score +0.20 [−1.02, +1.37], win +0.02 pp [−0.40, +0.42], HP lost −0.16 [−0.42, +0.09].
- `othernarrow2500 − base2500`: score −0.44 [−1.55, +0.73], win −0.16 pp [−0.55, +0.24].
- `spire2500 − base2500`: score −0.40 [−1.80, +1.03], win −0.18 pp [−0.64, +0.30].
- Subsets (descriptive): bosses +1.37 / +1.34 / +0.42 with CIs about ±5; elites +0.24 / −1.21 / −0.94; Act 4
  (108 fights) endwide +6.99 [−4.07, +18.19], spire −3.93 [−18.75, +10.24], spire − endwide −10.92
  [−23.14, +0.93].
- CPU per fight vs base: endwide 0.992 [0.976, 1.005], othernarrow 0.980 [0.965, 0.992], spire 0.976
  [0.962, 0.987]; narrower other nodes save about 2% CPU.
**Interpretation:** at A20 with the gen-6 prior at 2,500 simulations, splitting the widening constants per category
does not change fight results detectably: every all-fight score CI lies within about ±1.8 points (well under one
potion, 11) and every win CI within ±0.7 pp. This matches §369 (A0, both categories together): Silver's constants
sit on a flat region. spire-mentor's +6.35 pp does not transfer as a fight-level effect here (**Inference**: their
narrower end-turn setting was the baseline that gained; Silver's single setting is already wider). The labels are
not corrected for multiplicity. The final-fight leaf was off in every arm, and event fights count in the normal
subset (reviewer notes). Pre-registered decision: no default changes and the per-category idea is closed for this
setting; the armset stays research-only.
[result.json](evidence/silver_widening_a20_518_20261017/result.json). Raw:

## §521 — Silver rollout root table at 10k simulations: NOT_CPU_MATCHED, score NOT_SHOWN (2026-10-17)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-17 19:59Z, thread "Distilled Silver playout picker"):** "can you compare on 10k
simulations?" after §519; 20:03Z "8 workers"; 20:13Z "merge 612 and go".
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/silver_rollout_root_table_10k_20261017/PREREG.md), independent pre-launch review PASS
(PR #626). §519 unchanged except `STS_CTMSILVER_SWEEP_SIMS=10000,10700`: arms `greedy`/`roottable` at 10,000 and
10,700 simulations, R = 2, gen-6 E table model and tree prior, student C source runs, keys flag off. RUN_COMMIT
`72066f46` (code `42e54fac`, binary `bb117ec2…`), A20 seeds 111190500–111190627, 8 cloud workers. Primary
`roottable10000 − greedy10700` score, label valid only if the per-fight CPU ratio point estimate is ≤ 1.00.
**Result: NOT_CPU_MATCHED; the score contrast is NOT_SHOWN as well.** 128/128 seeds, 32/32 shards rc=0, 8 tars
verified from a second container; 1,403 valid fights (7 excluded for escapes, 6 control-replay mismatches; 25 in Act
4). Primary `roottable10000 − greedy10700`: score +1.79 [−0.40, +3.99], win +0.5 pp [−0.2, +1.1], HP lost −0.45
[−0.98, +0.08]; CPU per fight 1.008 [0.991, 1.025]. The root table costs 5.8% more CPU per simulation (1.058 [1.044,
1.072]; playouts 16.9 vs 15.5 actions) and takes 2.0% more search decisions per fight (25.1 vs 24.6), so at equal
simulations it costs 1.079x per fight against 1.070x for greedy10700. Descriptive, not pre-registered:
`roottable10000 − greedy10000` +1.77 [−0.24, +3.87]; `roottable10700 − greedy10700` +2.11 [−0.05, +4.35];
`greedy10700 − greedy10000` −0.02 [−1.69, +1.73]. Win rates 92.6 / 93.1 / 92.6 / 93.2% (greedy10000 / roottable10000
/ greedy10700 / roottable10700). Bosses (262) primary +5.9 [−2.9, +14.5]; Act 4 (25) −2.7 [−38.4, +24.8].
**Interpretation:** the root table's point estimate is about the same at 10k as at 2.5k (§519: +2.69 at equal
simulations), but at 10k it is not significant at equal simulations either. Unlike §519, 7% more simulations buy
nothing at 10k (−0.02), so the CPU-match rule penalises a cost that extra simulations would not measurably have used.
**Inference:** at the production budget, a cheaper root table (or the same one at no simulation cost) could be a
small free gain; across §519 and §521 the equal-simulation contrast is positive in all four budget pairs, but each CI
touches zero except §519's 2,500 pair. Pre-registered decision: stop; the option stays research-only and off (superseded: ADR-0046).
[result.json](evidence/silver_rollout_root_table_10k_20261017/result.json). Raw:

`0e6c3ce7…`, `91834bb7…`, `4ad02fcd…`, `470b53da…`, `8be914d1…`). Seeds 111190500–111190627 used; reviewer smokes

## §525 — Blended Silver leaf (one rollout mixed with a learned value) on the §397 corpus, offline: FAIL (2026-10-17)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-17, thread "StS AI community scan", V1):** "okay versuche mal v1 zu machen". §397 Gate A
tested a learned leaf V replacing one SimpleAgent rollout (R1); AlphaGo-style mixing `B = (1−α)·R1 + α·V` on the
same probe child was never tested in native Silver. Outside evidence: evangambit/sts2 `rl/FINDINGS.md` (StS2) found a
value head ties a rollout only from ~60 simulations and never beats it.
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/silver_blend_leaf_20261017/PREREG.md), written before any blend score. Frozen §397
corpus, features re-extracted with `silversynthfeatures` on main `623a8b60`, `vcont-natpert` (primary) and
`vroll-natpert` retrained with the unchanged §397 recipe, α from {0.1..0.9} on natural validation fold 3, §397 groups,
regret and concordance on natural test fold 4. No gameplay seeds.
**Result: FAIL.** α = 0.8 (vcont) and 0.7 (vroll). On 2,006 natural test groups (43 seeds): R1 regret 3.989,
primary blend 3.972, −0.017 [−0.436, +0.377] vs R1 (concordance 0.6887 vs 0.6730); vroll blend −0.037
[−0.397, +0.327]. Both blends' point estimates sit at a second rollout (B − R2 +0.038 and +0.019), but "at least as good as R2" is
not shown (upper bounds +0.483 and +0.374 above the pre-registered +0.1; `blendAtLeastR2` false). Deviation from
§397: the re-extraction gives R1 3.989 (§397 4.017), R4 − R1 −0.352 [−0.735, +0.040] (§397 −0.47 [−0.78, −0.14])
and 145,000 vcont rows (§397 146,984); **Inference:** probe rollouts redrawn on current main and 1–7 roots per
unit dropped on `rootEdgeMismatch`. The leaf-variance headroom here is ~0.35–0.5 regret. Retrained V alone matches
§397 within 0.3 (vcont − R1 +0.19). V1 closed; no native implementation.
[Result](evidence/silver_blend_leaf_20261017/RESULT.md), [blend_gate.json](evidence/silver_blend_leaf_20261017/blend_gate.json).
Models: `/mnt/project-files/silver-blend-leaf/models/`.
**Knowledge impact:** negative result added to `research/combat-search/leaf-evaluation.md` (rejected approaches).

## §528 — Shield and Spear: rollout block check with worst-case facing, and tree reuse off: both NOT_SHOWN (2026-10-17)

**Question:** Our A20 Act-4 runs lose more HP on Shield and Spear than heart1's engine does on the same entry states
(paired −6.8 HP [−11.2, −2.5] in the A20 loss audit, `/mnt/project-files/audit-2026-10-17/a20-loss-analysis.md`
F1). Does either of two search mechanics account for it?
1. Under Surrounded, damage is ×1.5 from the monster the player does not face, but the Silver rollout's block check
   (`SilverRolloutAgent::getIncomingDamage`) uses the current facing only. heart1's `SimpleAgent` has the same blind
   spot. Philipp asked to fix it anyway (2026-10-17 23:21Z: "sollten wir das nicht trotzdem fixen?").
2. Our tree reuse between decisions (heart1 reuses only exact matches).

**Setup.** `one_combat act4replay` on the 32 recorded Shield-and-Spear entry states, 3 copies, 10k exact sims, two
paired seed blocks (111130200–295 and 111130904–999), 192 fights per arm. Local switches only, nothing committed:
- Facing: `STS_SILVER_ROLLOUT_SURROUNDED_FACING=1` (patch in evidence) makes the block check use the worst facing over
  alive monsters while Surrounded. Switch off reproduces the default 96/96.
- Reuse off: a local hack that disables tree reuse.

**Result** (HP lost incl. full HP on death, paired per state, bootstrap 95% CI; positive = worse):

| arm vs default | seeds 111130904+ | seeds 111130200+ | pooled, 192 fights | wins | CPU |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| worst-case facing | +2.3 [−0.7, +5.5] | +1.7 [−1.4, +4.7] | **+2.0 [−0.2, +4.3]** (35.4 vs 33.3) | 181 vs 179 | 1.12x |
| tree reuse off | −5.7 [−9.5, −2.1] | +0.5 [−3.2, +4.2] | **−2.6 [−5.4, −0.1]** (30.7 vs 33.3) | 184 vs 179 | 0.86x |

The 111130904+ block ran first; the 111130200+ block is the replication. Tree reuse off on the 64 Heart states
(3 copies, 10k and 30k, seeds 111130000–191): 90 vs 89 and 96 vs 96 wins of 192, +0.5 pp and 0.0 pp.

**Interpretation:** worst-case facing does not help and costs 12% CPU. **Inference:** it makes rollouts over-block
(not measured). Tree reuse off did not replicate on the second seed block: pooled −2.6 HP lost [−5.4, −0.1] on
Shield and Spear, 0 pp on the Heart. Exact-match-only reuse was flat (−0.3 [−0.9, +0.2], audit report F1).
Neither closes the −6.8 HP engine gap. **Open question:** the remaining candidates are the fair-view root and
knowledge tracking, and other rollout-agent differences.

**Decision:** no switch, no default change, no PR for the patch.

Evidence: [`evidence/a20_ss_rollout_facing_20261017/`](evidence/a20_ss_rollout_facing_20261017/README.md) (per-fight
CSVs, `facing_switch.patch`, SHA256SUMS). The `act4replay` mode used here is part of this PR.

Seeds used: 111130200–295 and 111130000–191 (reused for pairing), 111130904–999.

**Knowledge impact:** both added to rejected approaches in `research/combat-search/leaf-evaluation.md`.

## §526 — Per-fight and per-root Silver search parameters at A20: no per-fight or per-root preference shown (2026-10-17)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-17 21:57Z):** "investigate a learned model for parameters per fight / per root. i know
that early combats and late combats behave very differently, so we should maybe adapt to that." He then picked the
root-level pilot (decision card, 22:03Z). Exploratory, not pre-registered; smoke seeds only, no default change.
**Part 1, per fight (offline, §518 data):** 3,043 paired A20 fights, 4 widening arms at 2,500 simulations, R = 2.
The arm − base score difference does not repeat across the two redraws of a fight (corr −0.06 / −0.01 / +0.11;
replicate score SD about 48 against mean effects below 1). Picking the best arm per fight on one redraw and scoring
on the other: −0.20 [−1.32, +0.86] vs base. LightGBM on fight features (act, floor, room, encounter, HP, potions,
CTM forecast, control-replay stats), 5 folds grouped by seed: +0.48 [−0.59, +1.63]; act × room table −0.02
[−1.20, +1.20]. No act CI excludes 0. Fight outcomes at R = 2 cannot carry a per-fight parameter model.
Scripts and output: [part1](evidence/silver_root_regret_pilot_20261017/part1/).
**Part 2, per root (design):** research-only armset `rootregret` of `ctmsilvergen` (environment as §518: A20,
sources by plain exact-10k Silver with student C `eff2f74f…`, keys off, `STS_SILVER_LEARNED_STOP=0`, hallway every
3rd). One `base2500` replay per fight with the gen-6 prior (g6_E `ca9bd7f2…`, weight 400, K = 8). Every second
multi-action root of that replay (hash) is searched again from fresh trees: twice at 20k with the default constants
(reference), 4 times each at 2,500 for base, end-turn C doubled (`endwide`), other chance nodes C 2 / alpha 0.5
(`othernarrow`), exploration 12.5 (`c12`) and 50 (`c50`), and twice at 10k with the base constants. Planner seeds
are shared per replicate across arms. Regret of a pick = Q(best) − Q(pick) under the visit-weighted Q of both
references, best = most reference visits (Silver evaluation units; median Q range over a root's edges 11.4).
Probes leave the replay bit-identical (seed 111193552 with and without probes: same arm rows).
Code `80530a06` (main `ff0143e8` + the armset), binary `2bd4b325…`.
**Run:** seeds 111193550–111193553 (smoke, every 6th root) and 111193554–111193601 (every 2nd root), 4 shards
each, all rc = 0. 5,954 probed of 12,652 observed multi-action roots, 52 sources; 5 fights had escape control
mismatches (their roots are kept). Probe CPU 3.0 h; shard wall times sum to about 4.8 h on one 4-CPU container.
**Result (bootstrap over source seeds; corrected by the post-merge review, see below):**
- The metric resolves search quality: base10000 − base2500 regret −0.124 [−0.174, −0.069] (average of the two
  single-reference regrets; pooled reference −0.118 [−0.163, −0.076]). The two reference searches agree on their top
  action at only 75.6% of roots, so reference noise is large.
- Arm − base2500 regret, all roots, average of the single-reference regrets: c12 +0.027 [−0.022, +0.075], c50 −0.020
  [−0.080, +0.050], endwide −0.027 [−0.058, +0.003], othernarrow +0.040 [−0.004, +0.086]; no arm differs from base.
  (Against the pooled reference c12 is +0.079 [+0.028, +0.130]: the c12 sign depends on the reference definition.)
- **Per-root heterogeneity is not shown.** Scoring replicates {0,1} against one reference and {2,3} against the other
  (and swapped), the covariance of arm − base across halves is c50 0.63 [−0.99, 2.58], othernarrow 0.18
  [−0.39, 0.86], c12 0.28 [−0.82, 1.37], endwide 0.14 [−0.24, 0.56]. Picking per root on one half and scoring on the
  other with the other reference cuts regret by 0.032 [−0.014, +0.079] vs base. With both halves scored against the
  same reference these were c50 1.81 [0.29, 3.80], othernarrow 1.20 [0.18, 2.39] and an oracle 0.066 [0.022, 0.114]
  (0.061 [0.027, 0.098] with one single reference): reference noise shared by both halves inflates them, so they are
  upper bounds only. Splitting the references costs power per half, so this is "not shown", not "absent".
- LightGBM on decision-time root features (act, floor, room, turn, HP fraction, actions, energy, hand size, monsters
  alive, inherited visits), 5 folds grouped by seed: −0.006 [−0.065, +0.056]; adding the base search's visit share of
  its pick: −0.003 [−0.055, +0.051]; prediction-target correlations within ±0.03.
- Descriptive, act × room means against the pooled reference: c50 lower at act-1 and act-2 bosses (−0.42, −0.40) and
  act-3 elites (−0.28), higher at act-1 normals and elites; not corrected for multiplicity.
**Interpretation:** neither fight outcomes nor root-level regret show that early and late fights, or individual
roots, want different constants. With independent references even the instance-level oracle gain is
indistinguishable from 0, and a selector on cheap features captures nothing. **Inference:** a controller would need
features from a first search (Q gaps, chance-node statistics) and would have to beat spending that budget on more
simulations; nothing here suggests it would. Both references use the base constants, which may favor base-like picks
(**Unverified** size). Regret is not fight score (silverbot reported that parameters tuned on saved states did not
hold in whole runs). No default change; the armset stays research-only.
**Post-merge review (#648, FAIL fixed in a follow-up PR):** the first version of this entry scored both halves against
one shared reference and reported "roots differ" (c50, othernarrow) and a 0.066 oracle gain; the reviewer showed that
this shared reference noise between selection and scoring, and that splitting the references removes it
(`split_ref.py`). The first selector also had one reference-derived feature (the 20k top-two visit margin), now dropped.
Evidence: [scripts and output](evidence/silver_root_regret_pilot_20261017/). Raw:
`/mnt/project-files/learned-search-params/rr-root-regret.tar` (sha256 `45aecaac…`). Seeds used: 111193550–111193601;
111193602–111193649 of this thread's block unused.
**Knowledge impact:** one paragraph in `evaluation/current-research.md` (Silver root allocation section) and the
`STS_CTMSILVER_ARMSET=rootregret` row in `operations/environment-variables.md`.

## §523 — Several uniform random playouts per Silver leaf vs greedy at A20: random playouts lose at every k (2026-10-18)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-17 22:10Z/22:11Z, thread "Distilled Silver playout picker"):** "multiple random
rollouts, did we ever try that?" then "can you try it on a small pilot with increasing random playouts per leaf?".
§479 had tested one uniform playout per leaf (−22.80 fight score) and 2 or 4 greedy playouts, not several random ones.
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/silver_uniform_playouts_pilot_20261017/PREREG.md), descriptive pilot, no labels, no
decision rule. `ctmsilvergen` armset `uniformpl` (code e762e846, run as 6e4998e2 before the main merge; binary
`8aecc181…`) with the §519/§521 harness (student C source runs, gen-6 E root prior, keys flag off, hallway every 3rd,
R = 2, `STS_SILVER_ROLLOUT_ROOT_TABLE=0` so greedy uses the ADR-0040 table). Arms at 2,500 simulations:
`greedy2500` and `uniform<k>x2500`, k = 1, 2, 4, 8 random playouts averaged per leaf. 16 sources
(111193700–111193715) in-thread on 4 cores, all shards rc = 0; 176 valid paired fights (1 excluded, escape).
**Result (paired, 95% seed bootstrap):**

| arm | fight score | win | HP lost | CPU/fight vs greedy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| greedy2500 | 286.2 | 95.2% | 11.4 | 1 |
| uniform1x2500 | −34.6 [−45.9, −22.8] | −9.1 pp | +7.9 | 0.85x |
| uniform2x2500 | −33.6 [−41.6, −23.7] | −9.1 pp | +7.3 | 1.47x |
| uniform4x2500 | −33.1 [−43.8, −22.4] | −9.7 pp | +6.1 | 2.54x |
| uniform8x2500 | −31.0 [−39.6, −21.2] | −8.5 pp | +6.3 | 4.70x |

`uniform8 − uniform1`: +3.6 [−1.6, +8.2] score, −1.6 [−2.8, −0.3] HP lost. Bosses (33): every k loses 63–79 score and
21–26 pp win rate. CPU per simulation grows almost linearly with k (1.03x, 1.80x, 3.16x, 5.82x); random playouts are
shorter than greedy ones (13.1–13.7 vs 16.9 actions). Smoke (111193790–111193793, 63 fights, same binary): about −58
at every k.
**Interpretation:** averaging random playouts reduces leaf noise only slightly (HP lost improves by about 1.6 from
1 to 8), while the bias of a random playout is unchanged, so the gap to greedy stays near 31–35 at up to 4.7x CPU per
fight. **Inference:** the greedy playout's value comes from its play policy, not from lower variance; more playouts of
a weak policy are no substitute. No follow-up proposed.
[result.json](evidence/silver_uniform_playouts_pilot_20261017/result.json) (sha256 `6d0cff67…`). Raw:
`/mnt/project-files/silver-uniform-playouts-pilot/upl-run.tar.gz` (run and smoke, sha256 `16b187ef…`). Seeds used:
111193700–111193715, 111193790–111193793 and 111193716 (post-merge build smoke of the armset on main at 300
simulations, rc = 0); the rest of 111193700–111193799 unused.
**Knowledge impact:** one sentence added to the rollout paragraph in `architecture/combat-search.md` and the
`STS_CTMSILVER_ARMSET=uniformpl` row in `operations/environment-variables.md`.

## §529 — Opening hand and first-Silver-search screens for the CTM: hand NOT_SHOWN, Silver endpoints biased (2026-10-18)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-18 01:24Z/01:31Z, thread "CTM opening hand", issue #460):** would an opening-hand-aware
CTM widen the OOC tree, and does the hand help? Also: can the endpoint distribution of a 10k Silver search at the
start of a fight replace the CTM's HP distribution? **Width:** no; a combat chance node holds `ceil(K·N^α)`
particles (`OocMctsPlanner.cpp:160`) whatever the CTM's outcome space, and the hand is not in the post-combat state.
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/ctm_opening_hand_20261018/PREREG.md), written before results; code 3c73f1a4, binary
`6eae03c1…` (`ctmopeninghands`, `STS_CTM_ROW_OPENING_HAND`, `STS_CTM_ROW_FIRST_SEARCH`; both fields default off, a
smoke seed gave byte-identical rows with them off and on minus the new fields).
*Screen A (offline, no seeds):* the §443 Stage-4 A20 corpus (80 `main-*` units, 75,871 victory/death rows,
3,995 seeds); opening hands rebuilt from run seed, floor and pre state, plus 16 fair resampled hands. The rebuild
matched the hand recorded with the field on all 1,061 rows (smoke + screen B); both are `BattleContext::init` on the
pre state, so this checks the row round trip, while the live combat draws through the same `init`
(`NativeSilverBackend.cpp:447`, code reading). 4,115 of 76,316 Stage-4 hands (5.4%) are empty: a pending Toolbox
choice before the draw. XGBoost, 5-fold CV
grouped by seed, A = pre-combat features, B = A + hand card counts.
*Screen B:* `combattransitiongen` A20 on 111195113–111195160 (48 seeds, 1,052 fights, 4 cores, ~0.5–0.8 h wall per
12-seed unit); Silver flat exact 10k, g6_E root prior w400 + tree prior K=8, root table on; out of combat the
deployed step with `STS_OOC_HEART1=student_sel` (cf6bf7fb…), keys off. CTM = calibrated `pathb-a20` stack via
`ctmscorerows`. Pre-registered: Silver scored on battle-end HP (before heals), CTM on RAW post HP (after heals).
Added in review: Silver endpoints mapped through the engine's heal rule (Meat on the Bone, Burning/Black Blood,
capped; reproduces the realized post HP on 1,010/1,010 wins) and scored on the CTM's scale
([rescore_matched_scale.py](evidence/ctm_opening_hand_20261018/rescore_matched_scale.py)).
**Result A (B − A, 95% seed bootstrap):**

| target | A | conditional (realized hand) | marginal (16 sampled hands) |
|---|---|---|---|
| death log loss | 0.09269 | +0.00015 [−0.00025, +0.00057] | +0.00016 [−0.00022, +0.00054] |
| HP-lost MSE on wins (var 278) | 128.9 | −0.25 [−0.62, +0.15] | +0.39 [+0.04, +0.76] |

**Result B (1,048 states, 37 deaths):**

| forecaster | death Brier | win HP-lost bias | win HP-lost RMSE | win HP log score (own scale) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CTM | 0.026 | +2.3 | 12.2 | −3.08 |
| Silver root (all 10k sims) | 0.063 | +12.2 | 17.7 | −3.51 |
| Silver best edge | 0.061 | +11.9 | 17.4 | −3.47 |

Pre-registered deltas, Silver root − CTM: Brier +0.036 [+0.022, +0.050]; own-scale HP log score −0.43
[−0.59, −0.26], which is mostly a scale artifact: the heal cap folds 18% of wins into one point mass at max HP that
the CTM predicts as one bin. Matched scale (1,010 wins): win HP bias −2.3 (CTM) vs −11.7 (Silver root), RMSE 12.2
vs 16.8, RMSE after removing the mean bias 11.97 vs 12.07, log score −3.082 vs −3.212, delta −0.13 [−0.25, −0.01].
**Interpretation:** A is `NOT_SHOWN` by the pre-registered rule: even the realized hand adds no measurable signal to
death or HP lost, and the sampled-hand mixture is slightly worse, so an opening-hand latent is not worth a CTM schema
change for OOC use. B: the first search's endpoints carry about as much information about win HP as the CTM (same
spread once the bias is removed), but they are about 12 HP too pessimistic (greedy playouts and exploration) and
overstate death (Brier 0.063 vs 0.026), although Silver sees the hand. **Inference:** a bias-corrected Silver
soft label is not ruled out by this screen, but it costs ~400x the CTM's CPU (§408) and needs its own bias and death
calibration. No follow-up proposed. Raw: `/mnt/project-files/ctm-opening-hand/run-3c73f1a4.tar.gz` (sha256 `2228160b…`),
`stage4-hands16.jsonl.gz` (`51cec25d…`); [screen A](evidence/ctm_opening_hand_20261018/screenA-opening-hand.json)
(`ef06180d…`), [screen B](evidence/ctm_opening_hand_20261018/screenB-first-search.json) (`65af25f3…`). Seeds used:
111195112 (smoke, run twice for the off/on check), 111195113–111195160; 111195161–111195171 unused.
**Knowledge impact:** the two `STS_CTM_ROW_*` rows in `operations/environment-variables.md` and one paragraph in
`evaluation/current-research.md` (§408 CTM vs Silver section).

## §531 — First exact combat parity canary against the real game: 26/34 steps match, one engine difference (2026-10-18)

**Question:** does the native engine produce the game's next combat state for the same state, action and RNG?
**Setup:** one A20 run on Philipp's PC with the live mod built with `STS_DIFFERENTIAL_DEBUG_RNG=1` (draw order
plus 12 RNG streams), driver `--parity-trace` at #651 head `6babedd6`, seed 111194450. The driver stopped at step 69
(floor 5, see below). `tools/combat_parity.py run` with `combat_parity_probe` from the same commit.
**Result:** 34 combat steps compared: 26 MATCH, 8 MISMATCH. Skipped: 2 `HELD_SELECTION_CARDS`, 1 `TRACE_ENDED`.
Coverage: 3 encounters (Two Louse, Small Slimes, Cultist), 1 relic (Burning Blood). The three combat ends match in
outcome; game − native end HP = 6, Burning Blood's post-combat heal. Seven mismatches were native export
leftovers, not behavior:
- No Draw is stored as 1 natively and −1 in Java (2 steps).
- The engine clears removed powers by their flag only, so the `statusMap` amount stays (2 steps).
- Curl Up leaves `uniquePower0` behind (2 steps).
- `cardSelect` is exported outside `CARD_SELECT` (1 step).

One was an engine difference: when Uppercut kills its target, the game puts no Weak or Vulnerable on the dead
monster and the engine did.
**Interpretation:** #656 makes the probe drop inactive payloads on both sides, and adds `STS_DEAD_TARGET_DEBUFF_FIX`
(default on). **Inference:** the debuff fix changes play only where a dead monster's powers carry over. The canary
also surfaced two driver issues, fixed in #656: Explosive Potion is listed once per monster by MCP, which stopped
the run, and the Silver search tree made rows ~85 MB. Coverage is far too small for any claim about overall parity.
Raw traces (4.8 GB) stay on the PC under `~/Documents/sts/artifacts/parity-canary-20261018/`. Seeds used: 111194450
(canary), 111194451–111194452 (fixed unit-test seeds, no gameplay).
**Knowledge impact:** `evaluation/differential-correctness.md` (canary paragraph).
## §530 — Shield and Spear search gap vs heart1's engine: rollout targeting NOT_SHOWN, information worth ~3 HP, line closed (2026-10-18)

**Question:** Where do the extra HP our A20 search loses on Shield and Spear, compared with heart1's engine on the
same 32 entry states, come from (−6.8 HP in the A20 loss audit; §528 ruled out the facing block check and tree
reuse)? Asked by Philipp 2026-10-17 23:57Z ("so we could have a smarter rollout maybe? ... maybe we are not allowed to
turn around anymore?") and 2026-10-18 00:20Z / 00:57Z ("yes compare heart1 and our sample of draw pile").

**Setup.** As in §528: `one_combat act4replay`, 32 states × 3 copies, 10k exact sims, paired seed blocks 111130904–999
(first) and 111130200–295 (replication), 192 fights per arm; local switches only, nothing committed.
- Rollout targeting under Surrounded (attacks normally go to the lowest-HP monster): mode 1 keeps attacking the
  faced monster; mode 2 attacks the monster with the larger frontal intent.
- Full-information root: the search root is the live state (true draw order and rolled intents) instead of the fair
  public view. An upper bound for anything a fair search can gain from information.
- Root-view audit: counted the root draw-pile observation on 1,000 decisions (32 fights, seeds 111130200–231).

**Result** (HP lost incl. full HP on death, paired per state, bootstrap 95% CI; positive = worse):

| arm vs default (31.6 HP lost) | seeds 111130904+ | seeds 111130200+ | pooled, 192 fights | wins | CPU |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| targeting 1, keep facing | +3.6 [−0.1, +7.5] | +2.0 [−2.1, +6.2] | **+2.8 [+0.3, +5.6]** | 178 vs 182 | 0.99x |
| targeting 2, face bigger intent | +1.0 [−3.4, +4.9] | +0.4 [−4.3, +5.4] | **+0.7 [−2.5, +3.8]** | 181 vs 182 | 1.04x |
| full-information root | −1.8 [−5.9, +2.8] | −4.0 [−8.4, +0.5] | **−2.9 [−5.6, +0.0]** | 186 vs 182 | 0.99x* |

- \*The full-information arm ran on a later binary (40d71721); its CPU ratio is against a default rerun on that
  binary, which reproduced the default outcomes on all 192 fights (0.96x against the `t0` CPU times).
- Default at this code loses 31.6 HP vs 33.3 at the §528 commit (same seeds). **Inference:** the rollout root table
  (ADR-0046) and action cap merged in between explain the difference; not separately tested.
- heart1's engine (9 copies per state, §528 audit runs) minus ours, per state: now −3.5 [−8.0, +0.8]; minus our
  full-information root −0.6 [−5.1, +3.7].
- Code comparison: our search `CardPile` information-set mode is a port of heart1's (sorted unknown region, uniform
  sampling at draw time, tracked known top and bottom). Chance outcomes are reseeded as `Random(base + N)` in both,
  and the widening and exploration constants heart1's `SearchAgent` sets equal ours (C 3.70, α 0.52, exploration 25).
- Root-view audit: 0 of 1,000 observations invalid; 16 had a known top card; the rest of the pile was unknown, as in
  heart1's pile.

**Interpretation:** neither targeting rule helps; keep-facing is worse. No difference in draw-pile handling was
found, and our fair root is built correctly. On current main the gap to heart1 is no longer shown. **Inference:** the
remainder is mostly noise plus the value of hidden information, which no fair search can recover.

**Decision:** Philipp closed the Shield-and-Spear search line (2026-10-18 09:44Z: "Okay close the search line"). No
switch or default change. What remains is the entry state (deck, lower max HP) from OOC play, which accounts
for about half of the Shield and Spear excess and the max-HP deficit (A20 loss audit F1).

Evidence: [`evidence/a20_ss_search_gap_close_20261018/`](evidence/a20_ss_search_gap_close_20261018/README.md)
(per-fight CSVs, the three local patches, SHA256SUMS).

Seeds used: 111130904–999 and 111130200–295 (reused for pairing with §528).

**Knowledge impact:** closed line added to `evaluation/current-research.md`; targeting rule added to rejected
approaches in `research/combat-search/leaf-evaluation.md`.

## §533 — Exact speedup of the native student forward: 2.0x per call, OOC MCTS CPU 1.67–1.77x, play identical (2026-10-18)

**Question:** Philipp (2026-10-18 11:52Z) asked to make the student forward faster after an A20 profile of the
winrate-check stack (4 seeds, 111195252–255, gdb stack samples plus `STS_OOC_CPU_PROFILE`/`STS_RUN_PROFILE`): OOC
MCTS was 97–98% of CPU, real Silver combat 2–3%; student_sel forwards inside rollout3 leaves (about 11 per leaf at
0.95 ms) were 66–83% of CPU, imagined Act-4 Silver fights 43% of Act-3 CPU, CTM sampling 3–5%.
**Change:** bit-identical fast paths in `heart1_policy.cpp`: AVX attention with `dot()`'s reduction order, four-output
reductions in the projection kernel, a per-thread FixedVec projection memo keyed by weights and input bits,
key/value-only observation rows in the last logits-only block, reused buffers, and a four-lane copy of glibc's
`__expf_fma` fast path for softmax and SiLU, enabled only when a start-up self-test matches `std::exp` bit for bit.
`STS_OOC_HEART1_SCALAR=1` keeps every reference loop.
**Result:** student_sel logits-only pass 887–933 → 450 µs per call on 4,383 captured A20 rollout records (full pass
1.8x); `heart1score` byte-identical to main on 6,778 student_sel records, 300 heart1 and 300 student C records, and
in scalar mode. Paired A20 `bestbench` units with the winrate-check env (main `658d43ee` vs the candidate), seed
111195257 full run and 111195258–260 Act 1: 4/4 byte-identical play; OOC MCTS CPU 1,350 → 763, 373 → 211,
343 → 205, 488 → 285 s (1.67–1.77x).
**Decision:** adopt (exact, no behavior change). **Inference:** Act 3 gains less, since imagined Act-4 Silver fights
do not use the student. Acts 3–4 records were not in the parity set.

Evidence: [`evidence/heart1_forward_speedup_20261018/`](evidence/heart1_forward_speedup_20261018/README.md); raw
`/mnt/project-files/heart1-forward-speedup/raw.tar.gz`; profile `/mnt/project-files/a20-profile/REPORT.md`.

Seeds used: 111195252–111195260 (profile 252–255, capture 256, gate 257–260).

## §532 — OOC MCTS prior guidance: search follows the prior; max-Q root pick WORSE, prior temperature 3 screen-pass (2026-10-18)

**Question (Philipp, 11:46Z):** does the student_sel prior over-guide A20 OOC MCTS so that search only explores the
top pick, and would a looser prior or picking the root move by mean Q instead of visits play better? Cheapest test:
Act 1 only.

**Diagnostic** (no new runs; decision logs of 224 A20 winrate-check seeds, 12,802 non-trivial roots): median top
prior 0.9925 (above 0.99 in 52% of roots); the top child gets a median 97.8% of visits; the early-stop visit lock ends
100% of searches (~2,050 of 4,096 sims); executed move = prior argmax 90.5%; non-selected children get a median 2
visits (exactly 1 visit: 46% in Act 1, 44% across all acts). So yes: search spends almost everything on the
prior's pick.

**Design** ([PREREG](evidence/ooc_prior_guidance_20261018/PREREG.md), frozen before variant data; Philipp 12:01Z
"do 16 workers"): A20 winrate-check stack at code 658d43ee, Act 1 only (`STS_STOP_AFTER_ACT=1`), 64 paired seeds,
4 arms: C (default), T3 (`STS_OOC_MCTS_TEMPERATURE=3`), Q (`ROOT_SELECTION=q`, 2,048 sims, lock off), T3Q (both).
C averaged 2,327 sims per Act-1 decision, so Q ran ~12% fewer sims and ~21% less OOC CPU than C. Primary:
post-Act-1-boss HP, death = 0, paired vs C, seed bootstrap 95% CI. Rule: WORSE if CI upper < 0; SCREEN_PASS if
mean ≥ +3 HP and deaths ≤ C; else NOT_SHOWN.

**Validity:** `verify_campaign.py` OK for all 16 workers (256 units, run 3d0d5120, binary 3315a7c1…).

**Result:**

| arm | Act-1 clears | score | Δ vs C [95% CI] | verdict | pick = prior argmax | sims/root | OOC CPU/run |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C | 57/64 | 34.1 | — | — | 92.1% | 2,327 | 508 s |
| T3 | 60/64 | 37.2 | +3.1 [−2.1, +8.3] | SCREEN_PASS | 86.5% | 2,618 | 576 s |
| Q | 32/64 | 13.8 | −20.3 [−25.7, −14.7] | WORSE | 40.1% | 2,048 | 401 s |
| T3Q | 45/64 | 25.1 | −9.0 [−14.9, −3.0] | WORSE | 46.2% | 2,048 | 419 s |

- T3 vs C clears: 4 seeds only T3 cleared, 1 only C; on the 56 seeds both cleared T3 has +2.2 HP.
- Q's off-prior picks (843) had a median 11 visits (39% ≤ 5). T3Q's (779) had a median 195 visits and still lost.

**Interpretation:** picking by mean Q is clearly harmful, and not only because of low-visit noise: with T3Q the
off-prior picks were well sampled and still lost 9 HP and 12 more Act-1 runs. **Inference:** the rollout3 + X2-B
leaf ranks OOC options worse than the student_sel prior, so letting Q override the prior hurts; the prior's
dominance is mostly protecting the search from its leaf (consistent with §441, §392). A softer prior with visit
selection (T3) passes the screen rule at the margin, with a CI that includes 0 and ~13% more OOC CPU. Act-1 HP
ignores deck quality, and with `STOP_AFTER_ACT=1` the search values the Act-1 boss clear as a win.

**Decision:** no default change. `ROOT_SELECTION=q` is rejected for this stack. T3 earns a confirmation that
reaches later acts, on Philipp's word.

Evidence: [`evidence/ooc_prior_guidance_20261018/`](evidence/ooc_prior_guidance_20261018/README.md) (PREREG,
campaign files, analyzer, diagnostic script, result, tar hashes; raw tars on the project share).

Seeds used: 111195272 (smoke), 111195280–111195343.

**Knowledge impact:** result line added to `evaluation/current-research.md`.

argmax over card plays and END_TURN, no potions; card selects stay greedy) and `ctmsilvergen` armset `priorpl`

R = 2) with the ADR-0046 root table on. Arms at 2,500 simulations, both with root prior and tree prior K = 8:
`greedy2500` (production playouts) and `priorpl2500`. 16 sources (111197692–111197707) in-thread on 4 cores, all
shards rc = 0; 162 valid paired fights (3 excluded, escapes). Smoke 111197780–111197783 (32 fights, rc = 0).

| subset | fights | Δ score | Δ win | Δ HP lost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| all | 162 | +3.81 [−2.43, +10.29] | +0.9 pp [−1.3, +3.2] | −1.45 [−2.51, −0.31] |
| elite | 67 | +12.09 [+0.16, +25.81] | +4.5 pp [0, +8.2] | −2.90 [−5.17, −0.73] |
| boss | 27 | +0.89 [−1.84, +3.03] | 0 | −2.52 [−4.80, −0.10] |
| normal and other | 68 | −3.19 [−11.23, +0.64] | −1.5 pp | +0.40 [−0.11, +0.90] |

**Label (pre-registered): `INCONCLUSIVE`** (mean +3.81 below the +5 bar, CI includes 0 and +5).
**Interpretation:** a better-playing playout lowers HP lost by about 1.5 per fight, concentrated in elites and bosses,
where it is significant on HP. **Inference:** that is more than the about 0.7 a 4x larger greedy budget gave in §479
(different harness), so leaf quality has some headroom, but at this resolution it is modest and the score gain is not
shown. The prior forward costs 7.6x per simulation, so any use needs a distilled fast version. No default change;
The prior-playout mode stays research-only, reachable only via `STS_CTMSILVER_ARMSET=priorpl`.
[result.json](evidence/silver_prior_playout_pilot_20261018/result.json) (sha256 `b6e1e649…`). Raw:
`/mnt/project-files/silver-prior-playout-pilot/ppl-run.tar.gz` (run and smoke, sha256 `a748c6bc…`). Seeds used:
111197692–111197707, 111197780–111197783; the rest of 111197692–111197791 unused.
**Knowledge impact:** rejected/open line in `research/combat-search/leaf-evaluation.md`; env-var rows for
