- **Inference:** the lean favours the value head, within a test that resolves about ±4 pp. No act-1 penalty, unlike
  §522. The compressed value scale makes the prior weigh more at the same cpuct (fewer overrides).
- **Knowledge impact:** `evaluation/current-research.md`.


## §619 — Gumbel sequential halving at OOC full-budget roots: offline target quality (116 A20 roots): SH beats PUCT against a uniform reference, play A/B pending (2026-10-21)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-21 15:04Z):** full-budget OOC roots are ~59% of run CPU. Does a Gumbel AlphaZero root
with sequential halving (SH) give better root choices and targets than PUCT at matched or lower budget?
**Design:** new opt-in `STS_OOC_MCTS_GUMBEL_ROOT=M[:SCALE]` (full-budget roots only, default off, byte-identical) and
research `STS_OOC_MCTS_ROOT_COMPARE`. At each full root it runs a uniform 8192-sim reference (even split over all
root actions, own seed) and SH with M = 4/16 at 512/1024/2048. PUCT@k is the main 4096 search's checkpoint.
Combined-stack A20 config, seeds 111145010–017 (014–017 cut short by a container restart), 116 full roots.
**Result:** paired regret in reference Q (×1e-3, SH − PUCT, matched sims): M16@2048 −6.91 [−10.33, −3.83],
M16@1024 −4.92 [−8.37, −1.75], M16@512 −4.40 [−7.43, −1.50]. Every SH cell is below 0, and M16@2048 also beats
PUCT@4096 (−6.30) at half the root CPU. Agreement with the reference's best action: M16@2048 0.69, PUCT@4096 0.44,
prior argmax 0.41. Target KL(π'_ref‖π'): M16@2048 0.030 vs PUCT@2048 0.091 (paired −0.062 [−0.112, −0.021]) and
PUCT@4096 0.060. At 512/1024 KL shows no difference. Flag-off identity run and compare-mode non-intrusion are
byte-identical on seed 111145010.
**Interpretation:** PUCT at 4096 barely leaves student_sel's ~0.99 prior. SH explores the sampled candidates and plays
by Q.
**Inference:** offline only. The reference shares the leaf evaluator (rollout3 + X2-B), and Q-based root selection lost
twice in play (§414, §560). So this does not show more Heart kills; a paired A20 play A/B (GUMBEL_ROOT=16, full roots
2048, vs current) must decide. The flag stays default off.
[Result](evidence/gumbel_root_sh_20261021/RESULT.md). Raw: `/mnt/project-files/az-speed-profile/gumbel-compare/`.
Seeds 111145010–017 used (010 reused from the speed profile).

## §635 — Gumbel sequential-halving root at OOC full-budget roots, paired A20 A/B (511 seeds): WORSE, Heart kills 9.4% vs 20.7% (2026-10-22)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-21 21:07Z "Jo mach den gepaarten a/b mit 32 wirken nach gen2"):** does the offline
win of §619 carry over to play? Gumbel SH with M = 16 at 2048 simulations had beaten PUCT@4096 against a uniform
leaf-Q reference.
**Design:** [PREREG](evidence/az_gumbel_root_ab_20261021/PREREG.md), pre-launch review PASS (C). A is the gen-2 A/B
arm A config (student_sel, PUCT, full roots 4096). B adds `STS_OOC_MCTS_GUMBEL_ROOT=16` and
`STS_OOC_MCTS_FULL_ROOT_SIMS=2048` (#791) on full-budget roots only. Seeds 111153152–663, RUN_COMMIT `3baca749`
(code main `b0a8f596`, v3 binary `be70a1c1…`), 32 workers on the queue schedule.
**Result: WORSE.** 511 valid pairs; unit 111153366 used up its queue attempts and is reported missing.

| | A (PUCT 4096) | B (Gumbel SH 2048) | B − A |
|---|---|---|---|
| Heart kills | 106 (20.7%) | 48 (9.4%) | −11.4 pp [−14.8, −7.9], McNemar p = 2.6e-10 |
| Reached Act 4 | 39.3% | 26.8% | −12.5 pp [−17.2, −7.9] |
| Wall | | | 0.60× |
| Played action ≠ prior argmax | 6.5% of searched roots | 17.3% of searched roots | |

**Interpretation:** B overrides student_sel's prior much more often, and the overrides lose: deaths move from Act 4
into Acts 2–3. Root selection that follows leaf Q (rollout3 + X2-B) is worse than the prior. This is the third loss
for Q-based root selection, after §414 and §560.
**Inference:** offline agreement with a leaf-Q reference (§619) is not a valid gate for root-selection changes. The
flag stays default off. A Gumbel-style root needs a value signal that beats the prior, or must keep the prior
dominant, and either needs a play A/B.
[Result](evidence/az_gumbel_root_ab_20261021/RESULT.md), [result.json](evidence/az_gumbel_root_ab_20261021/result.json).
Raw: `/mnt/project-files/az-gumbel-root-ab/units/`. Seeds 111153152–663 and smokes 111145018–019 used.
## §631 — Live advisor: Headbutt killing Awakened One's first form was refused (2026-10-22)

**Question:** why did overnight live seed 111200541 seg 1 stop with `silver_selection_pending_actions` after Headbutt+
killed Awakened One's first form (`actions=[UseCardAction,ShoutAction,SetMoveAction]`, no refusal tag; problem 90 in
`engine-parity/overnight-20261019/ISSUES.md` on the share)?
**Setup:** the canary's observation (`issue90/p90-observation.json` on the share) and `AwakenedOne` javap
(`issue91/javap.md`); `live_silver_importer_test` (Ironclad seed 111200071, AWAKENED_ONE; no gameplay runs).
**Result:** `AwakenedOne.damage` at the first-form death sets Rebirth (3), `addToTop(ClearCardQueueAction)`, then
`addToBottom(ShoutAction)` and `addToBottom(SetMoveAction(this, 3, UNKNOWN))`. The producer's `ShoutAction` branch only
knew the Gremlin Leader's escape run and returned without a refusal tag. Native `Monster::die` sets Rebirth, clears the
card queue and queues `SetMonsterMove(Rebirth)` alike, but the wire conversion only accepted the Darkling's Regrow.
The fight had Runic Dome, and the tracker reported the AwakenedOne row as `roll_unsettled` while the duplicate setter was
queued.
**Interpretation:** the producer emits `MONSTER_SET_MOVE {move:3, slot}` for the pair. Under
`STS_SILVER_AWAKENED_REBIRTH_QUEUE` (default on, `=0` restores the refusal) the importer imports it as native
`SetMonsterMove(Rebirth)`. The tracker reports the window as complete with one known transition; the importer accepts
that row only with the queued item. The importer test gains the Headbutt kill with native parity before and after the
pick, and the Runic Dome form, with fail-closed cases. Play-changing only where the advisor used to refuse.
Seeds: none new (live seed 111200541 as reported; unit test seed 111200071 from this thread's block).
**Knowledge impact:** `operations/environment-variables.md`, `operations/live-model-inspector.md`.
## §630 — Live advisor: Headbutt killing a Bronze Orb holding Stasis, and a half-dead Darkling's Regrow, were refused (2026-10-22)

**Question:** why did overnight live seed 111200539 stop at Headbutt's grid with `silver_selection_pending_actions`
after Headbutt+ killed the Bronze Orb holding Dark Embrace (problem 88: `refusal=1:unknown_action`), and after
Headbutt took a Darkling to half-dead (problem 89, seg 2: `refusal=1:half_dead_set_move`), in
`engine-parity/overnight-20261019/ISSUES.md` on the share?
**Setup:** the canary's observation, field dump and javap (`issue88-89/` on the share; the p88 observation kept as
`tests/fixtures/live_automaton_stasis_headbutt_return.json`); `live_silver_importer_test` (Ironclad seed 111200071,
AUTOMATON; no gameplay runs).
**Result:** problem 88: `StasisPower.onDeath` queues `MakeTempCardInHandAction(card, false, true)` (hand under 10;
otherwise `MakeTempCardInDiscardAction`) behind the grid, which the producer did not know. Native `returnStasisCard`
moves the card at the death. Under Corruption, native zeroed only `costForTurn`, while Java's add-to-hand runs the
`onCardDrawOrDiscard` pass (`STS_CORRUPTION_HAND_COST_FIX`, problem 83). Problem 89: the producer's check used
`isDeadOrEscaped()`, which is true for every half-dead monster (`AbstractCreature` checks `halfDead`; javap), so the
existing `MONSTER_SET_MOVE` fold was never reached.
**Interpretation:** the producer now emits `STASIS_RETURN {slot}` only for the dead orb whose Stasis card has that uuid,
and checks `isDying`/`isEscaping`/`escaped` for the Darkling. Under `STS_SILVER_STASIS_RETURN_QUEUE` (default on, `=0`
restores the `silver_unmapped_stasis` refusal) the importer moves the card to hand as native does; a full hand stays
refused. Native's Stasis return under Corruption now runs the hand cost pass (under `STS_CORRUPTION_HAND_COST_FIX`).
The importer test gains a Headbutt-kills-orb case with and without Corruption, with native parity before and after the
pick, and the captured observation imports and searches. Play-changing only where the advisor used to refuse, plus
generated-skill costs after a Stasis return under Corruption.
Seeds: none new (live seed 111200539 as reported; unit test seed 111200071 from this thread's block).
**Knowledge impact:** `operations/environment-variables.md`, `operations/live-model-inspector.md`.
## §624 — Silver attack-over-block bias vs exact solves: max backup + block-first playout halve first-fight regret; fight-level A20 A/B pre-registered (2026-10-22)

**Question (Philipp, 2026-10-21 19:12Z):** why does Silver play Strike over Defend on Jaw Worm turn 2 (seed
111147001, regret 2.29 points), and is it a systematic leaf or rollout bias he also sees in live play?
**Design:** exact expectimax from the exact-combat tools (#794 and the research branch's abstract solvers) scores
every root Silver searches. New opt-in flags, default off and bit-identical when off:
`STS_SILVER_MAX_BACKUP=m` (a decision node's selection value is its best child with at least m simulations, a
chance node's the visit-weighted mean of its outcomes) and `STS_SILVER_ROLLOUT_BLOCK_FIRST=<margin>` (+ `_BLOCK_OFFSET`,
`_BLOCK_LETHAL=0`; one_combat's ADR-0022 env allowlist refuses all four, so they act only through the
`maxbackup` armset or in `exact_combat_solver`): the playout plays its best defensive card first while incoming damage exceeds block by more than
the margin and its affordable attacks cannot kill a lone monster. The margin was fit by exact policy evaluation on
111149120–143; m on Jaw Worm 111149150–249.
**Result:** paired regret per fight (Silver points, ±1 SE), both flags (m = 4, margin 3) vs today:
Jaw Worm fresh 111149250–349 prod 1.57 → 0.74 (−0.83 ± 0.15), live 1.54 → 0.67 (−0.86 ± 0.14); Two Louse
111149600–699 prod 0.35 → 0.12, live 0.44 → 0.12; Cultist 111149350–369 6 → 0 wrong decisions. Each flag alone
helps less; higher exploration c is worse. CPU about +20% per simulation (A20 smoke 1.20x).
**Interpretation:** two causes. The greedy playout never blocks because it is hit, and mean backups undervalue the
less-visited, longer line (Defend's mean 5–10 points below exact). More simulations do not fix it.
**Inference:** only starter-deck first fights are measured. Whole-run fight score is untested, and the learned stop
was trained on mean-backup trees. The pre-registered A20 A/B
([PREREG](evidence/silver_maxbackup_ab_20261022/PREREG.md), arms base10000 / base12000 / fix10000, sources
111149400–463) needs Philipp's go. Flags stay default off.
Report: `/mnt/project-files/silver-rollout-bias/REPORT.md`. Seeds used 111149100–147, 111149150–389, replays of
111147001 and 111149600–699.
## §636 — OOC value head: the §622 hinge holds over three seeds, and a 15 % logit blend with X2-B ranks leaf siblings better than X2-B alone (offline, exploratory) (2026-10-22)

**Question:** (1) is §622's hinge result (M0.3: best selection BCE, monotone prices) more than one seed? (2) the head
alone ranks rollout siblings worse than X2-B (0.55 vs 0.633, §577 and §622); does a mix of the two rank them better?
Authorization for the GPU runs: Philipp 2026-10-22 06:48Z ("Merge 799 and go for gpu").
**Setup:** M0.3 (`--mono-weight 0.3`) seeds 1 and 2 and a control seed 1 on the §622 recipe, GPU on Philipp's PC;
`prices.py` (2,916 round-2 REWARDS states) and the §577 sibling/outcome tool. Blend v = sigmoid((1 − w) logit(X2-B) +
w logit(head)) on the §577 data with the tool's aggregation (w = 0 reproduces X2-B), w picked on round-2 TRAIN per head,
reported on round-2 VALIDATION and §494 with a 2,000-sample source bootstrap.
**Result:** M0.3 vs control (seed means): sel BCE 0.539 vs 0.542, val BCE 0.510 vs 0.513; HP monotone 89 % on every
seed vs 52-55 %, max HP +5 priced > 0 51-67 % vs 18-19 %, −3 HP sign right 89-90 % vs 81-82 %; round-2 sibling
concordance 0.551-0.554 vs 0.549, outcome AUC 0.758-0.764 vs 0.758-0.761. Blend, w 0.15 picked for all three heads:
round-2 VALIDATION concordance − X2-B +0.011 [+0.001, +0.021] (M0.3 s0), +0.012 [+0.002, +0.021] (s1), +0.010
[−0.000, +0.020] (control); §494 +0.011 to +0.015, regret −0.0005 to −0.0006 (CIs include 0); Heart-kill AUC on
VALIDATION 0.698-0.699 vs 0.683, on all round-2 sources 0.715-0.716 vs 0.694 (CIs exclude 0); mean leaf 0.73 vs 0.79.
Act-1 sibling concordance 0.669 vs X2-B 0.663 (head alone 0.537).
**Interpretation:** the hinge's monotonicity gain holds on 3 / 3 seeds; its BCE gain is small. Inference: the head adds
run-level information X2-B lacks, a small weight keeps X2-B's act-1 ranking, and the head's training barely matters
for the blend (control ≈ M0.3). Exploratory: w was not pre-registered, the sibling target ends in X2-B, the online leaf
is a rollout3 end state that these data do not score, and the learned OOC stop was trained on X2-B's scale.
`STS_OOC_MCTS_LEAF_HEART1_VALUE_WEIGHT` (default off; [smoke](evidence/value_leaf_blend_20261022/SMOKE.md): unset
reproduces main's decisions exactly) makes the blend testable in an A20 A/B, which needs a pre-registration and
Philipp's go. [Offline report](evidence/value_leaf_blend_20261022/OFFLINE.md); weights on data
branch `claude/az-gen2-data` `c3bd827a`, `gen2/value-cf/`.
Seeds: none (offline scoring of stored states and training on stored rows).
**Knowledge impact:** none yet (default-off option; no play change).

## §622 — OOC value head: counterfactual raw-heart1 delta distillation fixes the slopes but fails the BCE gate; the hinge on the T1 recipe is the best head so far (2026-10-22)

**Question:** can the value head learn raw heart1's clean HP / max HP / gold slopes (handoff from the gen-2 thread:
distilling heart1's absolute values did not transfer them, §609's hinge flattened the head) without losing the
T1-teacher accuracy (VDF_T1 v0.5, sel BCE 0.542)?
**Setup:** [PLAN](evidence/value_cf_distill_20261022/PLAN.md) (gate pre-registered). New loss on value-logit
*differences*: per batch one rule (hp, mhp, gold, round robin) with random deltas on 64 rows, target = 1.3587 × raw
heart1's delta, loss Σ(Δs − Δt)² / ΣΔt², fp32 without TF32. Weights 0.3 / 1 / 3, a control, and the #777 hinge at 0.3
on the same recipe; seed 0; GPU on Philipp's PC; `prices.py` and the §577 sibling tool in the cloud.
**Result:** sel BCE control / 0.3 / 1 / 3 / hinge 0.542 / 0.571 / 0.596 / 0.618 / 0.5365 (AUC 0.766 / 0.730 / 0.709 /
0.682 / 0.770). CF sign agreement with heart1 rises from 67 / 30 / 72 % (hp / mhp / gold) to 85-91 %; max-HP price
> 0 from 19 % to 92-96 %; −3 HP sign right 81 → 89-90 % (REWARDS states). Round-2 sibling
concordance 0.549 → 0.548-0.558 (X2-B 0.633). The hinge: max-HP price > 0 67 %, HP monotone 89 % vs 52 %, sibling
0.553, outcome AUC 0.764.
**Interpretation:** FAIL (BCE ≤ 0.545 and KL ≤ 0.0600 missed by every CF weight; −3 HP ≥ 95 % likely out of
reach with heart1 as the teacher, which is wrong-signed in 19 % of selection-fold states). Inference: correct end-state slopes are not why the head ranks siblings poorly (+0.009 at best). Unlike
§609 on z targets, the hinge on T1 targets costs no BCE (one seed). Options stay off.
[Result](evidence/value_cf_distill_20261022/RESULT.md). Runs and weights: data branch `claude/az-gen2-data`
`02f2c60d`, `gen2/value-cf/`.
Seeds: none (offline training).
**Knowledge impact:** none (default-off training options; no play change).

## §639 — Sibling capture with common random numbers: the variance of sibling differences drops to 0.36 pooled (one A20 seed) (2026-10-22)

**Question:** the §577 sibling labels are noisy. In round 2 the median best-minus-second gap is 0.016, and the
64-repeat target of one public state scatters by about 0.025. Does seeding repeat r of every leaf of a root
identically (common random numbers) make sibling differences cleaner?
**Design:** new opt-in `STS_OOC_SIBLING_COMMON_SEEDS=1` (default off). It replaces the leaf ordinal in the repeats'
`seed_seq`, and rows then carry `"commonSeeds": true`. [Smoke](evidence/ooc_sibling_common_seeds_20261022/SMOKE.md):
seed 111144997 with the #806 quick-smoke setup and sibling capture every 4th root (32 repeats, root children). Three
runs: main, branch with the flag off, branch with it on.
**Result:**
- Flag off: rows and play match main, CPU-time fields aside.
- Flag on: play is unchanged and the per-leaf means are not shifted (+0.0033, SE 0.0037 with roots as clusters).
- Variance of the paired difference over var(v_i) + var(v_j), across 3,287 sibling pairs on 18 roots:
  - per-leaf seeds: 1.006;
  - common seeds: 0.363 pooled (0.436 without the 165 pairs whose repeat vectors are identical), median pair 0.869.
- The noisy half of the pairs carries the gain (pooled 0.25–0.40). Low-variance pairs gain 3–11 %.
**Interpretation:** for sibling differences, pooled over pairs, common seeds are worth about 2.8× the repeats. One
seed, 256 simulations.
**Decision:** the option stays default off. Proposed use is a new sibling capture for value-head ranking labels
(needs seeds, workers and Philipp's go). Seed used: 111144997.

## §641 — OOC value head: a sibling-ranking loss makes the head rank leaf siblings at X2-B's level (0.644 vs 0.633) and its X2-B blend better (+0.032 to +0.040 over three seeds); auxiliary heads do not help (offline, exploratory) (2026-10-22)

**Question:** every value head so far ranks round-2 VALIDATION siblings at about 0.55, against X2-B's 0.633 (§577,
§622, §636). Can a training loss on sibling order fix that? Philipp chose more offline research before any play test
(2026-10-22 09:51Z) and asked about auxiliary targets.
**Design:** plan written before any run ([PLAN.md](evidence/value_sibling_rank_20261022/PLAN.md)). All arms use the
M0.3 recipe (§622) with one change, on Philipp's GPU:
- SR_w0.1, SR_w0.3, SR_w1: a RankNet loss with weight w over round-2 TRAIN sibling groups (8,458 groups from
  1,088 sources; targets are 64-rollout3 means). The pairs are weighted by the target gap. Holdout sources
  (seed % 8 == 6) are never trained on.
- AUX0.3: training-only heads for the next boss, Act 4 and final floor.
- The gate is the head alone on round-2 VALIDATION (320 sources): PASS ≥ 0.633, PARTIAL ≥ 0.585. It also needs the
  bars selection BCE ≤ 0.552 and "−3 HP sign" ≥ 85 %.
- A PASS arm gets seeds 1–2.
- The blend sigmoid((1 − w)·logit X2-B + w·logit head) is secondary, with w chosen on the TRAIN holdout.
**Result** ([README](evidence/value_sibling_rank_20261022/README.md)):

| arm | VALIDATION | − X2-B | − M0.3 | blend − X2-B | sel BCE | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M0.3 (control) | 0.555 | −0.078 | – | +0.011 [+0.001, +0.021] | 0.5365 | – |
| AUX0.3 | 0.557 | −0.076 | +0.002 [−0.003, +0.006] | +0.014 | 0.5398 | FAIL |
| SR_w0.1 | 0.586 | −0.048 | +0.030 [+0.019, +0.041] | +0.024 [+0.016, +0.032] | 0.5362 | PARTIAL (by 0.0006) |
| SR_w0.3 | 0.613 | −0.020 [−0.036, −0.002] | +0.058 | +0.033 [+0.023, +0.044] | 0.5363 | PARTIAL |
| SR_w1 | 0.644 | +0.011 [−0.004, +0.026] | +0.088 [+0.075, +0.102] | +0.040 [+0.030, +0.049] | 0.5466 | PASS |

- SR_w1 seeds 1 and 2 score 0.645 and 0.618 (mean 0.636), with blends of +0.032 and +0.032. Seed 2 was stopped at
  epoch 4 by the value-only selection while its holdout ranking was still rising.
- The SR weight costs monotonicity (gold+50 > 0: 94 % for M0.3 vs 65–84 % for SR_w1; maxHP+5 > 0: 67 % vs 42–54 %)
  and outcome calibration (SR_w1's leaf BCE against the run's Heart kill is 0.47–0.50 vs M0.3's 0.43; a constant
  scores 0.475). The bars hold.
- Exploratory:
  - The SR_w1 blend gains on every screen except the boss relic, most in Act 1 (+0.055).
  - The head alone beats X2-B on rewards and shops but loses on events and boss relics.
  - Noise-corrected concordance keeps the order.
**Interpretation:** a ranking loss transfers to sources it never saw, and the auxiliary heads do not help. The targets
end in X2-B, which favours it, so matching X2-B is a real gain. The PASS is a point estimate: the CI against X2-B
includes 0 and seed 2 alone would be PARTIAL, so the head ranks at X2-B's level, not above it. The online meaning is
open: §615's head ranked siblings at only 0.547 offline and still leaned +3.1 pp as the rollout3 end value.
**Decision:** no default change. SR_w1 (seed 0, `146a4512…` on `claude/az-gen2-data`) is the leaf candidate. Next is
an online test (blend and head alone vs X2-B), or a new capture with common seeds (§639) for cleaner labels; Philipp
decides. A later recipe should select epochs on a combined value and ranking objective. No game seeds were used.

## §642 — Shield and Spear: prior playouts in the elite room do not cut HP lost (−0.3 HP [−3.3, +2.8]) at 6.4x CPU (NOT_SHOWN, 2026-10-22)

**Question:** since ADR-0056 (#775) elite rooms use greedy root-table playouts and only the Heart keeps prior
playouts. Shield and Spear is the biggest HP sink before the Heart (about 32 HP per fight, §530). Would prior playouts
there (`STS_SILVER_PRIOR_PLAYOUT_ELITE=1`, ADR-0050's rooms) save HP? Started in the exact-combat research thread after
Philipp's 14:53Z question (prior rollouts everywhere vs leaf research); analysed in its own thread.
**Setup** ([evidence](evidence/shield_spear_prior_playouts_20261022/README.md)): `one_combat act4replay` on the 32
recorded A20 Shield and Spear entry states of the loss audit F1, 4 copies each, seeds 111149768–111149895 (both arms on
the same battle and planner seeds, paired per state and copy). Flat 10k exact sims with the §528 env (learned stop
off), g7f_E root prior weight 400, tree prior K = 8, g7f_E rollout root table. Binary from `f8831b48`
(claude/project-thread-kgjoid, main `165b5060` merged in). Research run, no prereg; nothing changes play.
**Result** (128 paired fights per arm, HP lost incl. full HP on death, per-state bootstrap 95% CI):

| arm | HP lost | wins | turns | CPU/fight |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| greedy playouts (default) | 32.77 | 117 | 4.27 | 8.0 s |
| prior playouts | 32.46 | 119 | 4.43 | 51.5 s |

- Prior − greedy: **−0.30 HP [−3.28, +2.77]**, fight SE 1.76; CPU 6.41x.
- In the 113 fights both arms win, HP lost is 26.73 vs 26.72. Wins differ in 10 pairs (greedy only 4, prior only 6).
- Potions used are equal (0.73 vs 0.74). The fight noise is large: the SD over the 4 copies of one state is 18.7 HP.
**Interpretation:** at this sample the effect is at most about 3 HP per fight either way, and the point estimate is
zero, so the playout policy is not what makes Shield and Spear expensive. This fits §541 (prior playouts saved only
about 0.4 HP in hallway fights) and §530 (the entry
state, not search, explains about half the excess). At 6.4x CPU per fight even the upper end of the CI would be hard
to pay for.
**Decision:** no change; elite rooms keep greedy playouts (ADR-0056). Seeds 111149768–111149895 used.

## §644 — Common-seed sibling recapture (320 A20 sources): cleaner sibling labels; the SR_w1 blend still beats X2-B (+0.018 to +0.026) but the head alone ranks below it (−0.019 to −0.035) (offline, 2026-10-22)

**Question:** round-2 sibling labels (§503; 64 independent rollout3 repeats per child) are noisy (§641). Does a
recapture with common seeds (§639) give cleaner labels, and how do the existing heads rank the new siblings? Philipp
chose the recapture (2026-10-22 14:51Z) and authorized it with 32 workers (15:34Z).
**Design:** pre-registered ([PREREG.md](evidence/ooc_sibling_crn_capture_20261022/PREREG.md), RUN_COMMIT `9fad3f60`,
pre-launch review PASS).
- Play is gen-2 A/B arm A (§621). The sibling capture adds every searched root at depth 1, with at most 64 leaves and
  32 common-seed repeats. Code `90eb9f07`.
- Seeds 111144512–111144831 (320 sources). VALIDATION is seed % 4 == 3 (80 sources); TRAIN is the other 240.
- 32 cloud workers, 120 core-h.
**Result** ([README](evidence/ooc_sibling_crn_capture_20261022/README.md)):
- **Integrity:** 320/320 units verified, and every source returned rc 0. 578,987 rows, with no bad rows. VALIDATION
  has 5,587 groups.
- **Label noise (VALIDATION):**
  - Split-half agreement at 16 vs 16 repeats is 0.718, against round 2's 0.653 (0.682 at 32 vs 32).
  - The stream variance of a sibling difference is 0.36 of independent streams, so 32 common-seed repeats are worth
    about 89 independent ones.
- **Hidden state is small, but not zero:**
  - Rows of one root with the same action and the same public record share their streams, and 69 % of these sets roll
    out identically.
  - Counting each set once, the hidden-state variance is 0.00005 per row (TRAIN 0.00009; round 2 0.00022 [0.00007,
    0.00042]), 2–4 % of a row's stream variance. Counting each row pair once, it is about 0.
  - With independent hidden states it would add 6–12 % to the stream variance of a sibling difference.
- **Ceiling:** 0.873 with stream noise only (round 2: 0.849). A hidden term on every row lowers it to 0.80–0.83. That
  term overstates the noise of deterministic siblings, so the truth lies in between. All ceilings lean optimistic.
- **Correction to §641:**
  - §641's noise model (`sr_noise.py`) treated rows with the same action and X2-B value as one public state. Only 9 %
    of those sets (round 2: 19 %) hold one public record.
  - The rest differ in gold, HP, the boss or the cards offered. That is not label noise for the concordance, since the
    head and the label average over the same children.
  - With identical records, round 2's inflation is 1.12, not 1.40, and #812's ceiling is 0.84, not about 0.81.
- **Heads (VALIDATION; no head was trained on these seeds):**

| evaluator | VALIDATION | − X2-B [95 % CI] | round 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| X2-B | 0.664 | – | 0.633 |
| M0.3 | 0.585 | −0.079 [−0.093, −0.065] | 0.555 |
| SR_w0.3 | 0.628 | −0.036 [−0.048, −0.026] | 0.613 |
| SR_w1 seed 0 | 0.645 | −0.019 [−0.031, −0.008] | 0.644 |
| SR_w1 seeds 1, 2 | 0.644, 0.629 | −0.020, −0.035 | 0.645, 0.618 |
| SR_w1 seed 0 blend, w 0.05 | 0.690 | +0.026 [+0.020, +0.032] | 0.673 |
| SR_w1 seeds 1, 2 blends, w 0.25, 0.10 | 0.683, 0.682 | +0.019, +0.018 | 0.665, 0.665 |

- **TRAIN (240 sources, also unseen):** SR_w1 seed 0 is at −0.007 [−0.014, +0.002], and the blends at +0.020 to
  +0.027.
- **By screen:** the blend gains on rewards, rest sites and shops. It is level on map choices, where X2-B is weakest
  (0.602).
**Interpretation:**
- Common seeds do what §639 promised. Most of the remaining label noise is stream noise, not hidden state.
- The blend's gain over X2-B replicates on new sources with cleaner labels, though it is smaller than on round 2.
- The head alone does not keep up. X2-B gains 0.031 on the new data and SR_w1 gains nothing, so §641's "at X2-B's
  level" was the optimistic end.
- X2-B (0.664) and the best blend (0.690) are well below the ceiling (0.80–0.87), so there is room left.
**Decision:** no default change. The blend stays the online candidate; the head alone is not a leaf replacement.
- Philipp chose to retrain the ranking loss on the new TRAIN labels ("go gpu", 17:50Z). The plan is
  `gen2/value-sr-crn/PLAN.md` on `claude/az-gen2-data`.
- Lessons for future label captures are in the README: common seeds on, duplicates by the full public record,
  adaptive repeats, a noise model (with its weighting) tested before the run, some labels that do not end in X2-B,
  and coverage of map choices.
- Seeds 111144512–111144831 used (smoke: 111144900).
## §643 — AZ gen-3 prior: trained on all 5,760 AZ runs it beats both gen-2 nets offline (selection KL 0.0506 vs 0.0525 / 0.0547), but it changes only ~3% of top choices, mostly the ones gen 2 already changed; no A/B candidate (offline, NEGATIVE, 2026-10-22)

Authorization: Philipp 2026-10-22 14:16Z ("merge 811 and then go"); flip check after his 17:27Z question (which offline
values matter for online play). Plan and outputs: `docs/experiments/evidence/az_gen3_train_20261022/` (`PLAN.md`,
`RESULT.md`, `flip/`, `tools/`); rows, runs, weights and parity on the data branch `claude/az-gen2-data` `9866689b`
(`gen3/`).

- **Question:** does fine-tuning the OOC prior on the whole AZ window (gen 0, gen-1b A/B, gen-2 A/B, gen-3 exploration
  §640) give a candidate worth a paired A20 A/B against student_sel?
- **Setup:** student_sel fine-tuned with the gen-2 pick recipe (d64/L2, lr 1e-4, anchor 0.3, value weight 0.3,
  `--value-k 32`) in three arms: value target z; calibrated n-step search value (slope 0.58 on non-exploration training
  folds); n-step with the exploration runs' value rows removed. Folds by run seed (selection % 8 == 6, validation
  % 8 == 7); gen-2 pick, gen-2 n-step net and student_sel scored on the same folds. Philipp's GPU, 14:33–17:21Z.
- **Result (offline):** pick (plan rule) = n-step without exploration values: selection KL 0.0506 (seeds 1, 2: 0.0506,
  0.0509) vs gen-2 n-step 0.0525, gen-2 pick 0.0547, student_sel 0.1052; z arm 0.0521, n-step arm 0.0512. Validation
  top-1 vs π′ flat at 0.933–0.935 for every net. Export `d5780dee…`, native parity 0 argmax mismatches on 400 records.
- **Decision-flip check** (validation-fold roots searched with student_sel, matched to the raw captures):
  - How often the top choice changes: gen 3's top choice differs from student_sel's at 3.24% of 8,424 full-budget
    roots and 3.48% of 25,150 fast roots. Gen 2 differs at 3.55% / 3.61%; gen 3 and gen 2 differ at 2.1%.
  - Overlap with gen 2: gen 2 picks the same move at 72% of gen 3's departures (fast roots 70%).
  - How close the departures are: both moves are well searched (median visits ~1,700 each at full budget, ~510 at fast
    roots). Root q separates them by a median of 0.015 (fast roots 0.020), against 0.011 between the two best moves
    at all roots, so they are not near-ties.
  - What the search already does: it plays gen 3's move at 120 of the 273 full-budget departures, where its q prefers
    that move. It keeps student_sel's move at 126, where its q prefers student_sel's (calibrated −1.1 pp; fast roots
    −0.6 pp).
  - π′ is biased toward the prior that guided its search (it carries that prior's log-ratio), so π′ agreement cannot
    referee: student_sel 132 vs gen 3 120 on student_sel-searched roots, but gen 3 40 vs student_sel 16 on
    gen-2-searched roots.
- **Inference:**
  - The KL gain is mostly confidence in moves student_sel already picks.
  - A trained prior changes ~3% of top choices, and the search already plays about half of them. The rest are where
    the search's own q prefers student_sel's move, so any gain there depends on the evaluation being wrong, not on the
    prior.
  - Gen 3 repeats most of gen 2's departures, and gen 2 was NOT_SHOWN (§621), so a gen-3 A/B would most likely be
    NOT_SHOWN again at about ±2.7 pp.
- **Recommendation (Philipp decides):** no gen-3 A/B; student_sel stays the prior; prior-only AZ generations wait until
  the evaluation (leaf values) changes. Future prior candidates report their departures from the current prior, the
  overlap with earlier candidates, and the search's verdict at those roots, not KL alone. No game seeds were used.
- **Knowledge impact:** `evaluation/current-research.md`.

## §645 — Sibling-ranking loss on the common-seed labels: both arms FAIL (head alone 0.640 and 0.649, SR_w1 0.645, X2-B 0.664); the ranking-selected epoch of SR_crn_r2 reaches X2-B's level (0.660) and its blend beats SR_w1's by +0.014 (offline, exploratory, 2026-10-22)

**Question:** SR_w1 (§641) ranks the common-seed VALIDATION siblings below X2-B (0.645 vs 0.664, §644). Does the same
recipe do better when it learns from the recapture's cleaner labels? Philipp typed "go gpu" (2026-10-22 17:50Z).
**Design:** pre-registered ([PLAN.md](evidence/value_sr_crn_20261022/PLAN.md), data branch `a8ab7da`).
- Arms on SR_w1's recipe (seed 0). Only the ranking data change:
  - SR_crn: the recapture's TRAIN groups (15,129);
  - SR_crn_r2: those plus round-2 TRAIN (23,587).
- Groups with source seed % 8 == 6 are held out. Selection is unchanged (fold objective, patience 3). The epoch with
  the best holdout ranking is exported too, as exploratory.
- Gate: the head alone on the common-seed VALIDATION, with the bars met (selection-fold BCE ≤ 0.552, −3 HP sign
  ≥ 85 %). PASS at ≥ X2-B; IMPROVED above SR_w1 with the paired CI above 0; FAIL otherwise.
- Trained on Philipp's GPU (18:03–19:31Z), evaluated in the cloud.
**Result** ([README](evidence/value_sr_crn_20261022/README.md)):

| head | selection-fold BCE | VALIDATION | − SR_w1 [95 % CI] | blend | blend − SR_w1's blend | round 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SR_w1 (control) | 0.547 | 0.645 | – | 0.689 | – | 0.644 |
| SR_crn | 0.556 (bar missed) | 0.640 | −0.005 [−0.012, +0.002] | 0.688 | −0.001 | 0.610 |
| SR_crn_r2 | 0.543 | 0.649 | +0.004 [−0.002, +0.010] | 0.690 | +0.001 | 0.639 |
| SR_crn epoch 8 (exploratory) | 0.587 | 0.650 | +0.005 [−0.001, +0.013] | 0.692 | +0.003 | 0.624 |
| SR_crn_r2 epoch 11 (exploratory) | 0.557 | 0.660 | +0.015 [+0.009, +0.022] | 0.703 | +0.014 [+0.009, +0.019] | 0.648 |

- X2-B scores 0.664 on the common-seed VALIDATION and 0.633 on round 2. Blend weights were chosen on the TRAIN holdout.
- Gate: SR_crn FAIL (level with SR_w1; BCE bar missed). SR_crn_r2 FAIL (the CI includes 0).
- The value objective stopped both runs while the holdout ranking still rose. It was 0.644 at SR_crn's selected
  epoch 5 and 0.657 at epoch 8; 0.646 at SR_crn_r2's selected epoch 8 and 0.656 at epoch 11.
- Monotonicity is better than SR_w1's (gold +50 valued higher in 83–87 % of cases, against 65 %). −3 HP sign is
  86–90 %. Outcome AUC on round 2 is 0.671–0.675 for every head.
**Interpretation:**
- Cleaner and more labels did not lift the selected heads. They are level with SR_w1, so label noise was not what
  held the head back.
- Selection on value stops training while ranking still improves. The ranking-selected epochs gain +0.010 and +0.011
  on VALIDATION, which no choice read. This sharpens §641's lesson (select on value and ranking).
- SR_crn_r2's epoch 11 is the best evaluator so far: alone at X2-B's level, and its blend is 0.703 (+0.039 over X2-B).
  It is one seed, its epoch was chosen after the run, and its BCE is just over the bar.
- Training only on common-seed labels loses on round 2 (0.610). Mixing in round 2's labels removes that loss.
**Decision:** no default change. The leaf stays X2-B, and SR_w1's blend stays the online candidate.
- Next, if Philipp agrees: confirm the ranking-selected recipe with seeds 1–2 under a new plan (about 2 h GPU). If it
  replicates, epoch 11's blend replaces SR_w1's as the online candidate.
- No game seeds were used.
- **Knowledge impact:** `evaluation/current-research.md`.
